entries.name: Zero Resource Speech Benchmark 2021
entries.full_title: The Zero Resource Speech Benchmark 2021: Metrics and baselines for unsupervised spoken language modeling
entries.summary: Defines the unsupervised task of spoken language modelling (learning linguistic representations from raw audio without labels) and provides a suite of four black-box, zero-shot metrics that probe a model at the phonetic, lexical, syntactic and semantic levels. A composite baseline of self-supervised contrastive representations, k-means clustering and a language model over the resulting pseudo-text scores above chance on all four metrics but below text-based toplines trained on the same data.
metrics: four zero-shot black-box metrics (phonetics, lexicon, syntax, semantics)
entries.note: Gap between raw-speech models and same-data text toplines delineates the space for end-to-end spoken LMs.

entries.name: ZeroSpeech 2021 (Zero Resource Speech Challenge 2021)
entries.full_title: The Zero Resource Speech Challenge 2021: Spoken language modelling
entries.summary: A challenge asking participants to learn a language model directly from audio, with no text and no labels, built on the Libri-light dataset (up to 60k hours of English audiobook audio). It supplies a baseline pipeline (contrastive predictive coding encoder + k-means quantizer + standard BERT/LSTM language model) and a metric suite evaluating the learned representations at the acoustic (ABX discrimination), lexical (spot-the-word), syntactic (acceptability judgment) and semantic (similarity judgment) levels, and reports an overview of the eight submitted systems from four groups.
entries.io: raw audio in (no text or labels), model scores/likelihoods over spoken minimal pairs out
entries.size: based on Libri-light: up to 60k hours of English audiobook audio
entries.note: Establishes the likelihood-based minimal-pair evaluation protocol (sWUGGY/sBLIMP) that later spoken language model benchmarks reuse.

entries.name: SD-QA
entries.full_title: SD-QA: Spoken Dialectal Question Answering for the Real World
entries.summary: A spoken question-answering benchmark built by augmenting an existing QA dataset with recorded spoken queries across five languages and many dialects, so that QA systems are measured under real speech input rather than clean text. Baselines quantify how language variety and speaker attributes affect downstream QA performance, and the paper analyses ASR and QA fairness with respect to the underlying speaker populations.
entries.io: spoken question in, text answer out
entries.size: more than 68k audio prompts in 24 dialects from 255 speakers
entries.note: Shows QA performance varies with dialect and speaker attributes, making it the standard dialect axis in later speech-LLM evaluations.

entries.name: dGSLM turn-taking statistics
entries.full_title: Generative Spoken Dialogue Language Modeling
entries.summary: Introduces dGSLM, described as the first textless model able to generate audio samples of naturalistic spoken dialogues, combining unsupervised spoken unit discovery with a dual-tower transformer with cross-attention trained on 2000 hours of two-channel raw conversational audio (Fisher) without any text or labels. The model generates speech, laughter and other paralinguistic signals in the two channels simultaneously, and is shown to reproduce more naturalistic and fluid turn-taking than a text-based cascaded model.
tasks: turn-taking behaviour evaluation (naturalness/fluidity of turn-taking vs a cascaded text-based model)
entries.io: two-channel raw conversational audio in, two-channel generated dialogue audio out
entries.size: trained on 2000 hours of two-channel conversational audio (Fisher)
entries.note: Source of the turn-taking/overlap statistics protocol widely reused for full-duplex spoken dialogue evaluation.

entries.name: ProsAudit
entries.full_title: ProsAudit, a prosodic benchmark for self-supervised speech models
entries.summary: An English benchmark assessing structural prosodic knowledge in self-supervised speech models, consisting of two subtasks with corresponding metrics and an evaluation dataset: a protosyntax task (identifying strong versus weak prosodic boundaries) and a lexical task (distinguishing pauses inserted between words from pauses inserted within words). Human evaluation scores are also provided. All evaluated SSL models scored above chance on both subtasks, even in an unseen language, but non-native models were significantly worse on the lexical task and larger-data models performed better on both subtasks.
metrics: above-chance discrimination accuracy on the two subtasks
entries.io: paired speech stimuli in -> model score used to pick the natural member of the pair
entries.size: two subtasks (protosyntax, lexical) with an evaluation dataset; counts not given in abstract
entries.note: Cross-lingual transfer probe: models perform above chance even on an unseen language, but lexical-task performance depends on native lexical knowledge; clear effect of training-data size.

entries.name: Spoken QA test set released with Spectron (synthesized spoken WebQuestions)
entries.full_title: Spoken Question Answering and Speech Continuation Using Spectrogram-Powered LLM
entries.summary: Spectron adapts pretrained LLMs to spoken question answering and speech continuation by adding a pretrained speech encoder and operating end-to-end on spectrograms, jointly supervising speech recognition, text continuation and speech synthesis so a cross-modal chain-of-thought happens in a single decoding pass. The method surpasses existing spoken language models in speaker preservation and semantic coherence and better retains the original LLM's knowledge, as shown on spoken QA datasets; the authors release audio samples and their spoken QA dataset.
entries.note: Publicly released spoken QA dataset (LLAMA1-Test-Set) and audio samples.

entries.name: SpokenWOZ
entries.full_title: SpokenWOZ: A Large-Scale Speech-Text Benchmark for Spoken Task-Oriented Dialogue Agents
entries.summary: A large-scale speech-text benchmark for spoken task-oriented dialogue built from human-to-human spoken conversations across eight domains, intended to close the gap between annotator-written TOD datasets and real spoken interaction. It introduces cross-turn slot and reasoning slot detection as new challenges and evaluates text-modal models, dual-modal models and LLMs such as ChatGPT.
entries.size: 5.7k dialogues, 203k turns, 249 hours of audio, 8 domains
entries.note: Best dialogue state tracker reaches only 25.65% joint goal accuracy and the best end-to-end model completes the user request in 52.1% of dialogues.

entries.name: tStoryCloze / sStoryCloze (spoken StoryCloze, from the TWIST paper)
entries.full_title: Textually Pretrained Speech Language Models
entries.summary: The TWIST paper trains speech language models (which process and generate acoustic data only, without textual supervision) by warm-starting from pretrained text LLMs, and additionally introduces two spoken versions of the textual StoryCloze benchmark to improve evaluation of speech language models. It also analyses the effect of speech tokenizer, pretrained text model and dataset size, and presents the largest SpeechLM at the time in parameters and training data.
tasks: spoken story continuation / commonsense continuation selection
entries.io: speech in -> speech out (no textual supervision); story-continuation pairs scored by the model
entries.size: two spoken StoryCloze variants; counts not given in abstract
entries.note: Speech samples, code and models released publicly.

entries.name: BabySLM
entries.full_title: BabySLM: language-acquisition-friendly benchmark of self-supervised spoken language models
entries.summary: A language-acquisition-friendly benchmark that probes spoken language models at the lexical and syntactic levels using vocabulary and constructions typical of children's language experience, so that self-supervised speech models can be evaluated after training on developmentally plausible corpora. The paper reports experiments demonstrating the benchmark's usefulness and highlights the text-speech and clean-speech vs in-the-wild gaps as open challenges.
entries.note: Frames spoken-LM evaluation around infant language acquisition rather than adult corpora.

entries.name: LibriSQA
entries.full_title: LibriSQA: A Novel Dataset and Framework for Spoken Question Answering with Large Language Models
entries.summary: A free-form and open-ended spoken question answering dataset curated from LibriSpeech, with Part I in natural conversational format and Part II containing multiple-choice questions followed by answers and analytical segments, totalling 107k SQA pairs across various topics; the paper also proposes a lightweight end-to-end framework for running SQA on LibriSQA with speech-text LLMs and shows the same framework handles ASR by reformulating it into the SQA format.
tasks: spoken multiple-choice question answering with analysis
entries.io: speech + question -> free-form text answer or multiple-choice selection
entries.size: 107k SQA pairs (Part I conversational, Part II multiple-choice with answer plus analysis)
entries.note: Motivated by the deficit of speech-text LLMs in aligning speech and text features; dataset and demo released.

entries.name: Dynamic-SUPERB
entries.full_title: Dynamic-SUPERB: Towards A Dynamic, Collaborative, and Comprehensive Instruction-Tuning Benchmark for Speech
entries.summary: A collaborative, community-extensible instruction-tuning benchmark for universal speech models, testing zero-shot generalisation to unseen tasks given natural-language instructions. The initial release combines many tasks and datasets into evaluation instances spanning content, speaker, semantic, degradation, paralinguistic and non-speech audio dimensions, with baselines built from speech models, text LMs and a multimodal encoder.
entries.io: speech in (with text instruction), text out
entries.size: 55 evaluation instances combining 33 tasks and 22 datasets
entries.note: Baselines do reasonably on seen tasks but struggle on unseen ones, exposing weak instruction generalisation.

entries.name: CompA
entries.full_title: CompA: Addressing the Gap in Compositional Reasoning in Audio-Language Models
entries.summary: Two expert-annotated benchmarks probing compositional reasoning in audio-language models: CompA-order tests whether a model understands the order of occurrence of acoustic events, and CompA-attribute tests attribute binding of events to sources. Each instance pairs two audio-caption pairs whose audios contain the same events in different compositions, and the model must match each audio to the correct caption; the paper also fine-tunes CLAP with composition-aware hard negatives to build CompA-CLAP.
entries.io: audio + text in, matching score out
entries.note: Existing audio-language models perform only marginally above chance on compositional reasoning.

entries.name: Zero Resource Code-switched Speech Benchmark
entries.full_title: Zero Resource Code-switched Speech Benchmark Using Speech Utterance Pairs For Multiple Spoken Languages
entries.summary: A zero-resource benchmark that assesses the code-switching ability of self-supervised speech encoders using speech utterance pairs, scored by language modelling over discrete units without any labelled data. Experiments cover several well-known speech encoders and examine the effect of pre-training languages and model size.
languages: multilingual (code-switched; specific languages not stated in the abstract)
entries.note: Multilingually pre-trained encoders beat monolingual ones on code-switching, but all leave substantial headroom.

entries.name: E-chat200
entries.full_title: E-chat: Emotion-sensitive Spoken Dialogue System with Large Language Models
entries.summary: Introduced together with E-chat, a spoken dialogue system that combines an emotion embedding from a speech encoder with an LLM so it can comprehend and respond to emotions conveyed in speech, E-chat200 is a dataset designed explicitly for emotion-sensitive spoken dialogue; across various evaluation metrics E-chat consistently outperforms the baseline model.
entries.io: emotional speech in -> emotion-appropriate dialogue response
entries.note: Targets the gap where audio-event-aware LLMs still cannot generate responses appropriate to the emotion in the speech.

entries.name: EmphAssess
entries.full_title: EmphAssess : a Prosodic Benchmark on Assessing Emphasis Transfer in Speech-to-Speech Models
entries.summary: A prosodic benchmark that evaluates whether speech-to-speech models encode prosodic emphasis in their input and reproduce it in their output, applied to speech resynthesis and speech-to-speech translation, including across changes of speaker and language. The evaluation pipeline includes EmphaClass, a new classifier that detects emphasis at the frame or word level.
entries.note: One of the few benchmarks scoring prosody in generated speech rather than only in the input.

entries.name: AIR-Bench
entries.full_title: AIR-Bench: Benchmarking Large Audio-Language Models via Generative Comprehension
entries.summary: A two-track benchmark for large audio-language models covering human speech, natural sounds and music: a foundation track of single-choice questions probing basic single-task ability, and a chat track of open-ended question-answer instances probing comprehension of complex audio plus instruction following. Both require free generation, and a unified framework uses a strong LLM (GPT-4) with audio meta-information to score the hypotheses.
entries.size: 19 foundation tasks with ~19k single-choice questions; 2k open-ended chat instances
entries.note: Reports high agreement between the GPT-4-based scoring and human evaluation.

entries.name: StyleTalk
entries.full_title: Advancing Large Language Models to Capture Varied Speaking Styles and Respond Properly in Spoken Conversations
entries.summary: A speech-to-speech dataset built so that when two current-turn utterances have identical content but are spoken in different styles their appropriate responses differ, created to teach and test whether LLMs can listen to speaking style (paralinguistic and prosodic information) and respond accordingly. The paper also proposes the Spoken-LLM framework modelling both linguistic content and speaking style, trained on StyleTalk with a two-stage pipeline, and shows it outperforms text-only baselines and prior speech LLM methods.
entries.note: Explicitly isolates the paralinguistic gap between text and speech modalities: identical sentences in different styles must yield different responses.

entries.name: AudioBench
entries.full_title: AudioBench: A Universal Benchmark for Audio Large Language Models
entries.summary: A universal benchmark for audio large language models spanning eight tasks and 26 datasets, seven of which are newly proposed, organised around speech understanding, audio scene understanding and voice (paralinguistic) understanding. It targets instruction-following conditioned on audio signals and ships an open-source evaluation toolkit, data and leaderboard.
entries.note: Across five popular models, no single model is consistently best on all tasks.

entries.name: CompA-R / CompA-R-test (from the GAMA paper)
entries.full_title: GAMA: A Large Audio-Language Model with Advanced Audio Understanding and Complex Reasoning Abilities
entries.summary: Alongside GAMA, a general-purpose large audio-language model, the paper proposes CompA-R, a synthetically generated instruction-tuning dataset whose instructions require complex reasoning over the input audio, and CompA-R-test, a human-labeled evaluation dataset for assessing LALMs on open-ended audio question answering that requires complex reasoning. Through automated and expert human evaluation, GAMA outperforms other LALMs on diverse audio understanding tasks by margins of 1%-84%, and GAMA instruction-tuned on CompA-R is superior in complex reasoning and instruction following.
tasks: open-ended audio question answering requiring complex reasoning
audio understanding (non-speech sounds and non-verbal speech)
entries.io: audio + open-ended instruction/question -> free-form text answer
entries.note: CompA-R-test is human-labeled and targets open-ended reasoning rather than closed-set classification; GAMA adds a soft prompt carrying event-tag semantic evidence.

entries.name: LALM object hallucination probe (Kuan et al.)
entries.full_title: Understanding Sounds, Missing the Questions: The Challenge of Object Hallucination in Large Audio-Language Models
entries.summary: Introduces methods for measuring object hallucination in publicly available large audio-language models by contrasting free-form audio captioning with discriminative questions about whether a particular object sound is present in a clip. The study finds that LALMs match specialised captioning models on audio understanding yet fail on the discriminative presence questions, and explores prompt engineering as a mitigation.
entries.note: Seminal demonstration that LALMs describe audio well but hallucinate when asked whether a specific sound is present.
aka: Object hallucination in LALMs (Kuan et al.)

entries.name: SD-Eval
entries.full_title: SD-Eval: A Benchmark Dataset for Spoken Dialogue Understanding Beyond Words
entries.summary: A benchmark for spoken dialogue understanding and generation that goes beyond the words, testing whether a model's response is appropriate given paralinguistic and environmental information. The data is aggregated from eight public datasets along four perspectives (emotion, accent, age and background sound), and responses are scored with objective metrics, subjective judgement and LLM-based metrics; a matched training set is also released.
entries.size: 7,303 utterances / 8.76 hours of speech (evaluation set); 724.4k utterances / 1,052.72 hours (training set)
entries.note: Models conditioned on paralinguistic and environmental information beat their counterparts, and LLM-based metrics correlate better with human judgement than BLEU/ROUGE.

entries.name: Speech-Specific Risk Benchmark
entries.full_title: Towards Probing Speech-Specific Risks in Large Multimodal Models: A Taxonomy, Benchmark, and Insights
entries.summary: Proposes a speech-specific risk taxonomy of eight categories spanning hostility (malicious sarcasm, threats), malicious imitation (age, gender, ethnicity) and stereotypical bias (age, gender, ethnicity), motivated by the fact that paralinguistic cues can change the intended meaning of an utterance beyond its transcript. A small-scale dataset built on the taxonomy evaluates whether large multimodal models can detect these risks.
entries.size: small-scale evaluation dataset (exact size not stated)
entries.note: Even recent models are near chance, e.g. Gemini 1.5 Pro performs only slightly above a random baseline.

entries.name: Audio Entailment
entries.full_title: Audio Entailment: Assessing Deductive Reasoning for Audio Understanding
entries.summary: Defines the Audio Entailment task to measure deductive reasoning in audio-language models: given an audio recording as premise and a textual hypothesis, decide whether the hypothesis is entailed, neutral or contradicted. Two datasets are built from audio in AudioCaps and Clotho with LLM-generated hypotheses, and state-of-the-art ALMs are benchmarked zero-shot and with linear probes.
entries.io: audio + text hypothesis in, three-way label out
entries.size: two datasets sourced from AudioCaps and Clotho (sizes not stated)
entries.note: ALMs show clear deficiencies in logical reasoning; a 'caption-before-reason' intermediate step adds 6% (zero-shot) and 3% (linear probe) absolute.

entries.name: Listen and Speak Fairly
entries.full_title: Listen and Speak Fairly: A Study on Semantic Gender Bias in Speech Integrated Large Language Models
entries.summary: A curated spoken bias evaluation toolkit and dataset for measuring semantic gender bias in speech-integrated LLMs. Bias is probed across four semantic tasks — speech-to-text translation, spoken coreference resolution, spoken sentence continuation and spoken question answering — using several complementary bias measurement methods.
entries.venue: 2024 IEEE Spoken Language Technology Workshop (SLT), Macao, 2024, pp. 439-446
entries.note: Bias levels are language-dependent and differ depending on the evaluation method used, so a single bias metric is not sufficient.

entries.name: MuChoMusic
entries.full_title: MuChoMusic: Evaluating Music Understanding in Multimodal Audio-Language Models
entries.summary: A human-validated multiple-choice benchmark for music understanding in audio-focused multimodal language models. Questions cover fundamental musical concepts plus their cultural and functional context, testing both knowledge and reasoning about a given music track.
entries.note: Evaluation of five open-source models exposes an over-reliance on the language modality rather than genuine multimodal integration.

entries.name: SLU-GLUE
entries.full_title: WHISMA: A Speech-LLM to Perform Zero-shot Spoken Language Understanding
entries.summary: The paper introduces WHISMA, a speech-LLM combining the Whisper encoder with Llama-3, fine-tuned parameter-efficiently on a collection of SLU datasets. To evaluate generalisation to unseen domains it develops SLU-GLUE, a new task-agnostic spoken-language-understanding benchmark; WHISMA gains 26.6% relative on zero-shot slot filling over prior SOTA on SLURP and outperforms the speech-LLM Qwen-Audio by 33.0% relative on SLU-GLUE.
metrics: zero-shot slot-filling performance (relative gain over baselines)
entries.io: speech input plus text task prompt -> text SLU output
entries.note: Task-agnostic benchmark used to compare speech-LLMs (WHISMA vs Qwen-Audio) on unseen domains; introduced inside a model paper rather than as a standalone benchmark release.

entries.name: Spoken StereoSet
entries.full_title: Spoken Stereoset: On Evaluating Social Bias Toward Speaker in Speech Large Language Models
entries.summary: A dataset for evaluating social bias toward the speaker in speech large language models. Models hear speech from diverse demographic groups and their responses are compared to reveal stereotypical versus anti-stereotypical tendencies triggered by speaker characteristics rather than content.
entries.venue: 2024 IEEE Spoken Language Technology Workshop (SLT), Macao, 2024, pp. 871-878
entries.note: Most evaluated models show minimal bias, but some display slight stereotypical or anti-stereotypical tendencies toward speaker demographics.

entries.name: "What Do You Like?" (identity-critical spoken QA diagnostic)
entries.full_title: Just ASR + LLM? A Study on Speech Large Language Models' Ability to Identify and Understand Speaker in Spoken Dialogue
entries.summary: A diagnostic evaluation of whether speech LLMs actually identify and reason about speakers in spoken dialogue, or merely answer from the transcript. The authors show many Gaokao listening-test questions are answerable from the conversation transcript alone, and propose the "What Do You Like?" dataset contrasting context-based questions with identity-critical questions that require correct speaker identification.
entries.note: Evaluated models score far higher on context-based than identity-critical questions, behaving like a text LLM reading the transcript.

entries.name: JASCO (Joint Audio-Speech Co-Reasoning)
entries.full_title: What Are They Doing? Joint Audio-Speech Co-Reasoning
entries.summary: A benchmark and task formulation for auditory LLMs that must reason jointly over non-speech sound and human speech present in the same clip, rather than treating either modality alone. Released with a scene-reasoning dataset called "What Are They Doing", plus an analysis of how much each model depends on each modality.
entries.note: Introduces an explicit modality-dependence analysis to reveal whether models lean on speech content or ambient sound.

entries.name: MAE (Multi-Audio Evaluation)
entries.full_title: Beyond Single-Audio: Advancing Multi-Audio Processing in Audio Large Language Models
entries.summary: A multi-audio evaluation benchmark for audio LLMs, assembling 20 datasets across 11 tasks that require processing several audio streams at once, in both speech and general sound scenarios. The same paper also proposes MALLM, a model trained with discriminative learning on synthetic multi-audio data.
entries.io: multiple audio clips in, text out
entries.note: Existing audio LLMs handle single-audio inputs well but degrade sharply once several audio streams must be compared.

entries.name: OmniBench
entries.full_title: OmniBench: Towards The Future of Universal Omni-Language Models
entries.summary: A human-annotated benchmark for omni-language models that must recognise, interpret and reason over visual, acoustic and textual inputs simultaneously; correct answers require integrating all three modalities. The paper also releases OmniInstruct, a tri-modal instruction-tuning set of 84.5K training samples (training data, not benchmark items).
entries.venue: The Thirty-Ninth Annual Conference on Neural Information Processing Sy
entries.io: image + audio + text in, text out
entries.note: Most baselines score below 50% accuracy even when given textual substitutes for the image and/or audio, indicating weak tri-modal context construction.

entries.name: SALMon
entries.full_title: Salmon: A Suite for Acoustic Language Model Evaluation
entries.summary: A likelihood-based evaluation suite testing whether speech language models are aware of acoustic aspects beyond spoken content: background noise, emotion, speaker identity and room impulse response. Each element is probed both for consistency within a sample and for whether it matches the spoken text, by checking that the model scores correct samples higher than incorrect ones.
entries.note: The likelihood-scoring design makes the benchmark cheap to compute even for large models.

entries.name: Audio Hallucination Benchmark (object existence / temporal order / attribute)
entries.full_title: Can Large Audio-Language Models Truly Hear? Tackling Hallucinations with Multi-Task Assessment and Stepwise Audio Reasoning
entries.summary: A three-task diagnostic suite for hallucination in large audio-language models: object existence (hallucinating non-existent sound events), temporal order of events, and object attribute (sound source attribution). The paper also proposes a multi-turn chain-of-thought prompting approach that improves scores on these tasks.
entries.note: Models fail on these fundamental checks, hallucinating absent events and mis-ordering or mis-attributing sounds.

entries.name: Audio Is the Achilles' Heel (audio LMM red teaming)
entries.full_title: Audio Is the Achilles' Heel: Red Teaming Audio Large Multimodal Models
entries.summary: A red-teaming evaluation of audio large multimodal models under three settings: harmful questions delivered in audio and in text, harmful text questions accompanied by distracting non-speech audio, and speech-specific jailbreaks. It tests whether text-side safety alignment carries over to the audio channel.
entries.note: Open-source audio LMMs average a 69.14% attack success rate on harmful audio questions, and speech jailbreaks reach 70.67% on Gemini-1.5-Pro.

entries.name: AVHBench
entries.full_title: AVHBench: A Cross-Modal Hallucination Benchmark for Audio-Visual Large Language Models
entries.summary: A cross-modal hallucination benchmark for audio-visual LLMs, testing perception and comprehension where audio and visual signals interact. It includes hallucination tests alongside cross-modal matching and reasoning tasks.
entries.note: Most existing audio-visual LLMs hallucinate under cross-modal interaction; simple training on the benchmark improves robustness.

entries.name: CMM (Curse of Multi-Modalities)
entries.full_title: The Curse of Multi-Modalities: Evaluating Hallucinations of Large Multimodal Models across Language, Visual, and Audio
entries.summary: A benchmark for systematically evaluating hallucination in large multimodal models across language, visual and audio inputs — the discrepancy between factual multimodal input and generated text. Its analysis isolates two causes: overreliance on unimodal priors and spurious inter-modality correlations.
entries.io: audio + visual + text in, text out
entries.note: Attributes hallucination to unimodal priors and spurious inter-modality correlations, pointing to imbalanced modality integration.

entries.name: MMAU
entries.full_title: MMAU: A Massive Multi-Task Audio Understanding and Reasoning Benchmark
entries.summary: A large multi-task benchmark of human-annotated question-answer pairs over speech, environmental sound and music, targeting expert-level knowledge and complex reasoning. It mixes information-extraction questions with reasoning questions spanning 27 distinct skills.
entries.note: Best systems reported reach only about 53% accuracy (Gemini Pro v1.5 52.97%, Qwen2-Audio 52.50%) across 18 evaluated models.

entries.name: OpenMU-Bench
entries.full_title: OpenMU: Your Swiss Army Knife for Music Understanding
entries.summary: A large-scale music-understanding benchmark suite assembled from existing datasets plus bootstrapped annotations, broadening music understanding to include lyrics understanding and music tool usage. It is used both to train and to evaluate the accompanying OpenMU model.
entries.note: Explicitly built to address data scarcity, so it doubles as training data as well as evaluation.

entries.name: SAGI Benchmark
entries.full_title: Roadmap towards Superhuman Speech Understanding using Large Language Models
entries.summary: A benchmark organised around a proposed five-level roadmap for speech understanding, running from basic ASR up to superhuman models that combine non-semantic information with abstract acoustic knowledge. It standardises evaluation across the tasks at each level to expose where capability is missing.
entries.note: Reveals gaps in handling paralinguistic cues and abstract acoustic knowledge, plus incompleteness of capability coverage.
aka: SAGI benchmark / Roadmap to Superhuman Speech Understanding

entries.name: VoiceBench
entries.full_title: VoiceBench: Benchmarking LLM-Based Voice Assistants
entries.summary: A multi-faceted benchmark for LLM-based voice assistants that goes beyond ASR accuracy and clean-speech knowledge testing. It combines real and synthetic spoken instructions carrying three kinds of real-world variation — speaker characteristics, environmental conditions and content factors.
entries.note: Exposes that current voice assistants degrade under realistic speaker and acoustic variation that clean-speech evaluations hide.

entries.name: CAA (Chat-Audio Attacks)
entries.full_title: Who Can Withstand Chat-Audio Attacks? An Evaluation Benchmark for Large Audio-Language Models
entries.summary: An evaluation benchmark probing how large audio-language models withstand four distinct types of audio attack in conversational settings, aiming for model-agnostic rather than model-specific adversarial audio. It is scored three ways: standard automatic metrics, a GPT-4o-based evaluation simulating conversational complexity, and human evaluation.
entries.note: Across six voice-capable LALMs evaluated, GPT-4o shows the highest resilience to the four attack types.

entries.name: Dynamic-SUPERB Phase-2
entries.full_title: Dynamic-SUPERB Phase-2: A Collaboratively Expanding Benchmark for Measuring the Capabilities of Spoken Language Models with 180 Tasks
entries.summary: An open, community-expanded benchmark for instruction-based universal speech models, growing the first generation to 180 tasks with 125 new community contributions. Unlike Phase-1's classification-only scope, it adds regression and sequence-generation tasks across speech, music and environmental audio.
entries.io: speech/audio + text instruction in, text out
entries.note: No model performs well universally — SALMONN-13B leads on English ASR while Qwen2-Audio-7B-Instruct leads on emotion recognition.

entries.name: LongVALE
entries.full_title: LongVALE: Vision-Audio-Language-Event Benchmark Towards Time-Aware Omni-Modal Perception of Long Videos
entries.summary: The first Vision-Audio-Language Event understanding benchmark, comprising 105K omni-modal events with precise temporal boundaries and detailed relation-aware captions within 8.4K high-quality long videos, produced by an automatic pipeline for multi-modal filtering, omni-modal event boundary detection, and cross-modal correlation-aware captioning. A baseline is built to enable video LLMs to perform omni-modality fine-grained temporal video understanding.

entries.name: ADU-Bench
entries.full_title: Benchmarking Open-ended Audio Dialogue Understanding for Large Audio-Language Models
entries.summary: A four-dataset benchmark for open-ended audio dialogue understanding in large audio-language models, spanning 3 general scenarios, 12 skills, 9 languages and 4 categories of ambiguity handling. The ambiguity portion is novel: identical literal sentences carrying different intentions through intonation, pause position or homophones.
entries.note: Across 16 LALMs, models struggle with mathematical symbols and formulas, roleplay, multiple languages, and ambiguity from intonation, pauses and homophones.

entries.name: Audiopedia
entries.full_title: Audiopedia: Audio QA with Knowledge
entries.summary: A knowledge-intensive audio question answering benchmark requiring both audio comprehension and external knowledge reasoning, unlike audio-only AQA sets. It defines three sub-tasks: single-audio QA, multi-audio QA requiring reasoning over several clips, and retrieval-augmented QA where relevant audio must first be retrieved.
entries.note: Benchmarked LALMs perform suboptimally, motivating an audio entity linking plus knowledge-augmented framework.

entries.name: AV-Odyssey Bench
entries.full_title: AV-Odyssey Bench: Can Your Multimodal LLMs Really Understand Audio-Visual Information?
entries.summary: A multiple-choice audio-visual benchmark in which every problem couples text, image/video and audio so that answers require using clues from both the visual and audio channels. It is motivated by DeafTest, a probe showing that multimodal LLMs fail trivial tasks such as judging which of two sounds is louder or higher in pitch.
entries.io: audio + visual + text in, text out
entries.note: The DeafTest probe shows MLLMs fail at basic loudness and pitch comparisons that humans find trivial.

entries.name: SPIRAL
entries.full_title: SpeechPrune: Context-aware Token Pruning for Speech Information Retrieval
entries.summary: Introduces Speech Information Retrieval as a new long-context task for Speech LLMs and presents SPIRAL, a 1,012-sample benchmark testing models' ability to extract critical details from approximately 90-second spoken inputs. The paper also proposes SpeechPrune, a training-free token pruning strategy evaluated on SPIRAL.

entries.name: AVTrustBench
entries.full_title: AVTrustBench: Assessing and Enhancing Reliability and Robustness in Audio-Visual LLMs
entries.summary: A trustworthiness assessment benchmark of 600K samples spanning nine crafted tasks that evaluates audio-visual LLMs along three dimensions: adversarial attack, compositional reasoning, and modality-specific dependency, including whether models calibrate their responses under perturbed inputs. Thirteen state-of-the-art AVLLMs are evaluated and fall well short of human-like comprehension; the paper additionally proposes a model-agnostic calibrated preference optimization method.

entries.name: Fleurs-SLU
entries.full_title: Fleurs-SLU: A Massively Multilingual Benchmark for Spoken Language Understanding
entries.summary: Fleurs-SLU is a massively multilingual spoken language understanding benchmark with two parts: topical utterance classification and multiple-choice question answering via listening comprehension. It is used to compare end-to-end speech classification models, ASR-plus-LLM cascades and multimodal speech-LLMs, with a focus on languages that lack reliable ASR or a writing system.
languages: multilingual (102 languages for classification, 92 for QA)
entries.size: 692 hours of speech across 102 languages (topical classification) and 944 hours across 92 languages (listening-comprehension MCQ)
entries.note: cascaded systems are more robust for multilingual SLU, while closed-source speech-LLMs match or surpass them; robust multilingual ASR, S2T translation and SLU are strongly correlated

entries.name: Jailbreak-AudioBench
entries.full_title: Jailbreak-AudioBench: In-Depth Evaluation and Analysis of Jailbreak Threats for Large Audio Language Models
entries.summary: Jailbreak-AudioBench packages a toolbox, a curated dataset and a benchmark for audio-modality jailbreaks against large audio-language models. The toolbox does text-to-audio conversion plus editing techniques that inject hidden semantics, and the dataset supplies explicit and implicit jailbreak audio in both original and edited forms for evaluating multiple state-of-the-art LALMs.
entries.note: presented as the most comprehensive audio-modality jailbreak benchmark to date, exposing threats such as query-based audio editing
aka: Xiao et al. (2025) audio modality-specific edit jailbreak evaluation

entries.name: MNSC (Multitask National Speech Corpus, Singlish)
entries.full_title: Advancing Singlish Understanding: Bridging the Gap with Datasets and Multimodal Models
entries.summary: The paper standardizes and annotates a large spoken Singlish corpus as the Multitask National Speech Corpus (MNSC), with standardized splits and a human-verified test set supporting ASR, spoken question answering, spoken dialogue summarization and paralinguistic question answering. It is used to evaluate audio LLMs and cascaded systems on an under-served English variety, alongside a proposed multitask model, SingAudioLLM.
entries.note: SingAudioLLM outperforms other AudioLLMs and cascaded solutions by 10-30% on these Singlish tasks

entries.name: VoxEval
entries.full_title: VoxEval: Benchmarking the Knowledge Understanding Capabilities of End-to-End Spoken Language Models
entries.summary: VoxEval is a SpeechQA benchmark that tests end-to-end spoken language models' knowledge understanding entirely in the speech modality, keeping both input and output as speech. It additionally varies input audio conditions to probe robustness and includes complex tasks such as mathematical reasoning posed in spoken form.
entries.note: current SLMs are sensitive to varying audio conditions and show weak spoken-format reasoning

entries.name: ADIFF
entries.full_title: ADIFF: Explaining audio difference using natural language
entries.summary: ADIFF introduces the task of explaining differences between two audio recordings in natural language, with two datasets derived from AudioCaps and Clotho and three tiers of explanation: concise event/object descriptions, brief sentences about events, scenes and signal properties, and comprehensive explanations covering semantics and listener emotion. The paper provides baselines and a prefix-tuning-based model, evaluated with objective metrics and human evaluation against an audio-language model baseline.
entries.io: two audio clips in, text out
entries.note: naive baselines fail to distinguish perceptually similar sounds and cannot produce the most detailed tier-3 explanations

entries.name: ContextDialog
entries.full_title: Does Your Voice Assistant Remember? Analyzing Conversational Context Recall and Utilization in Voice Interaction Models
entries.summary: ContextDialog is a benchmark for measuring how well multi-turn voice interaction models recall and use information from earlier utterances in a conversation. It systematically compares open-source speech-based interaction models against text-based ones, including a retrieval-augmented setting.
entries.note: speech-based models struggle more than text-based ones, especially recalling information conveyed in speech, and RAG does not close the gap

entries.name: TalkArena
entries.full_title: Mind the Gap! Static and Interactive Evaluations of Large Audio Models
entries.summary: This work introduces an interactive, arena-style evaluation approach for large audio models in which real participants converse with the models and give preference rankings and qualitative feedback. Topic modeling of the collected queries identifies primary voice-interface use cases, and the resulting interactive rankings are compared against twenty existing static benchmarks.
entries.note: no individual static benchmark correlates strongly with interactive user preference (Kendall tau <= 0.33); only spoken QA and age prediction show significantly positive correlations

entries.name: URO-Bench
entries.full_title: URO-Bench: Towards Comprehensive Evaluation for End-to-End Spoken Dialogue Models
entries.summary: URO-Bench is a speech-to-speech benchmark for end-to-end spoken dialogue models covering Understanding, Reasoning and Oral conversation, split into a basic and a pro track of 20 test sets each. It is described as the first S2S benchmark to cover multilingualism, multi-round dialogue and paralinguistics alongside cognitive dimensions such as logic and knowledge.
entries.size: two difficulty tracks (basic and pro), 20 test sets each
entries.note: open-source SDMs do well on daily QA but lag their backbone LLMs on instruction following, show catastrophic forgetting, and remain weak on paralinguistic and audio understanding

entries.name: WorldSense
entries.full_title: WorldSense: Evaluating Real-world Omnimodal Understanding for Multimodal LLMs
entries.summary: WorldSense is a benchmark for omni-modal (visual, audio and text) video understanding in multimodal LLMs, designed so that questions require the coupled use of audio and video rather than either alone. Videos span 8 primary domains and 67 fine-grained subcategories, and all QA pairs were manually labeled by 80 expert annotators with multiple correction rounds.
entries.size: 1,662 audio-visual synchronised videos and 3,172 multiple-choice QA pairs across 26 tasks
entries.note: best evaluated model reaches only 65.1% accuracy, showing current models struggle with real-world omni-modal scenarios

entries.name: AVUT (Audio-centric Video Understanding benchmark without Text shortcut)
entries.full_title: Audio-centric Video Understanding Benchmark without Text Shortcut
entries.summary: AVUT is an audio-centric video understanding benchmark that evaluates the video comprehension of multimodal LLMs with a particular focus on auditory information, with tasks probing both audio content and audio-visual interactions. It also addresses the text shortcut problem — where the correct answer is inferable from the question text alone — via an answer-permutation-based filtering mechanism, and evaluates a range of open-source and proprietary multimodal LLMs.

entries.name: DAVE (Diagnostic Audio Visual Evaluation)
entries.full_title: DAVE: Diagnostic benchmark for Audio Visual Evaluation
entries.summary: DAVE is a diagnostic benchmark dataset for systematically evaluating audio-visual models under controlled settings. It counters the visual bias of existing benchmarks by ensuring both modalities are necessary to answer correctly and by decoupling evaluation into atomic subcategories, so that failures in visual understanding, audio interpretation, and audio-visual alignment can be told apart in state-of-the-art models.
tasks: atomic diagnostic subtasks isolating audio, visual, and alignment errors

entries.name: FinAudio
entries.full_title: FinAudio: A Benchmark for Audio Large Language Models in Financial Applications
entries.summary: FinAudio is a benchmark for audio LLMs in the financial domain, built around three tasks: ASR on short financial audio, ASR on long financial audio, and summarization of long financial audio such as earnings calls and CEO speeches. It curates two short and two long audio datasets and adds a new financial audio summarization dataset, evaluating seven audio LLMs.
entries.size: two short-audio and two long-audio datasets plus a new financial audio summarization dataset
entries.note: exposes limitations of existing AudioLLMs on financial-domain audio

entries.name: Full-Duplex-Bench
entries.full_title: Full-Duplex-Bench: A Benchmark to Evaluate Full-duplex Spoken Dialogue Models on Turn-taking Capabilities
entries.summary: Full-Duplex-Bench evaluates full-duplex spoken dialogue models on the interactive behaviours that turn-based metrics miss: pause handling, backchanneling, turn-taking and interruption management. It uses automatic metrics for reproducible, fast assessment and releases benchmark and code.

entries.name: MAVERIX
entries.full_title: MAVERIX: Multimodal Audio-Visual Evaluation and Recognition IndeX
entries.summary: A unified audiovisual benchmark of 2,556 multiple-choice and open-ended questions over 700 videos, with human performance baselines, explicitly designed so that questions require tight integration of video and audio. It targets cross-modality comprehension in multimodal LLMs across a range of agentic scenarios.

entries.name: OmniMMI
entries.full_title: OmniMMI: A Comprehensive Multi-modal Interaction Benchmark in Streaming Video Contexts
entries.summary: A comprehensive multi-modal interaction benchmark tailored for OmniLLMs in streaming video contexts, with over 1,121 videos and 2,290 questions across six subtasks addressing streaming video understanding and proactive reasoning. The paper also proposes M4, a multi-modal multiplexing modeling framework for inference-efficient streaming models that can see and listen while generating.

entries.name: QualiSpeech
entries.full_title: QualiSpeech: A Speech Quality Assessment Dataset with Natural Language Reasoning and Descriptions
entries.summary: QualiSpeech is a low-level speech quality assessment dataset covering 11 key aspects, annotated with natural-language comments that include reasoning and contextual insight rather than only numeric scores. The accompanying QualiSpeech Benchmark evaluates whether auditory LLMs can describe speech quality in natural language.
entries.size: 11 low-level quality aspects with natural-language comments
entries.note: fine-tuned auditory LLMs can reliably describe noise and distortion types and their temporal characteristics, and reasoning appears to improve assessment reliability

entries.name: S2S-Arena
entries.full_title: S2S-Arena: Evaluating Paralinguistic Instruction Following in Speech-to-Speech Models
entries.summary: S2S-Arena is a speech-native benchmark for instruction-following speech-to-speech models that assesses both semantic understanding and paralinguistic expression (prosody, emotion, speaker traits). It uses a four-level interaction protocol of increasing paralinguistic complexity, a two-stage data construction pipeline, and reference-free pairwise arena comparison directly in the speech modality, benchmarking 10 S2S systems over 1,000+ comparisons.
entries.note: substantial gaps between academic and industrial S2S systems, most pronounced under complex paralinguistic demands

entries.name: Talking Turns
entries.full_title: Talking Turns: Benchmarking Audio Foundation Models on Turn-Taking Dynamics
entries.summary: Talking Turns proposes an evaluation protocol that scores spoken dialogue systems on turn-taking using a supervised model trained to predict turn-taking events in human-human conversations as the judge. It combines a user study of deployed spoken dialogue systems with API-based evaluation of open-source and proprietary audio foundation models on curated Switchboard test sets measuring understanding and prediction of turn-taking events.
entries.note: systems often misjudge when to speak, interrupt too aggressively, and rarely backchannel

entries.name: TaskAnything / JudgeAnything
entries.full_title: Judge Anything: MLLM as a Judge Across Any Modality
entries.summary: This paper introduces two benchmarks for any-to-any modality evaluation: TaskAnything, which assesses multimodal understanding and generation across 15 any-to-any modality categories (images, audio, video) using 1,500 curated queries, and JudgeAnything, which evaluates the judging capability of five advanced MLLMs under Pair Comparison and Score Evaluation with human judgments and detailed rubrics. Experiments show MLLM judges are promising but limited on cross-modal evaluation.

entries.name: EvalSIFT
entries.full_title: SIFT-50M: A Large-Scale Multilingual Dataset for Speech Instruction Fine-Tuning
entries.summary: EvalSIFT is a benchmark dataset released alongside the SIFT-50M speech instruction fine-tuning corpus, built to evaluate the instruction-following capabilities of speech-text LLMs. SIFT-50M spans five languages and covers both speech understanding and controllable speech generation instructions; EvalSIFT is its dedicated evaluation counterpart.
entries.note: introduced together with SIFT-LLM, which is reported to outperform existing speech-text LLMs on instruction-following benchmarks

entries.name: Multi-AudioJail
entries.full_title: Multilingual and Multi-Accent Jailbreaking of Audio LLMs
entries.summary: Multi-AudioJail is a framework for evaluating safety alignment of large audio-language models under multilingual and multi-accent spoken jailbreaks. It contributes a dataset of adversarially perturbed multilingual/multi-accent jailbreak prompts and a hierarchical evaluation pipeline that measures how acoustic perturbations such as reverberation, echo and whisper effects interact with cross-lingual phonetics.
languages: multilingual and multi-accent (specific languages not listed in abstract)
entries.note: jailbreak success rates rise by up to 57.25 percentage points under accent plus reverberation, and multilingual audio-only attacks succeed 3.1x more often than text-only ones
aka: Multilingual and Multi-Accent Jailbreaking of Audio LLMs

entries.name: RUListening
entries.full_title: Are you really listening? Boosting Perceptual Awareness in Music-QA Benchmarks
entries.summary: A framework for hardening music question-answering benchmarks so that answering requires actually listening. It introduces the Perceptual Index (PI), which measures how much a question depends on audio perception by analysing log-probability distributions from text-only language models, and uses it to synthesise harder distractors. Applied to MuchoMusic, the filtered set drives text-only LLMs to chance level and degrades LALMs when audio is replaced by noise.
entries.note: On MuchoMusic, text-only LLMs without audio reached up to 56.4% accuracy and LALMs stayed above chance on Gaussian noise, indicating existing music-QA benchmarks largely measure reasoning rather than perception.

entries.name: AJailBench
entries.full_title: Audio Jailbreak: An Open Comprehensive Benchmark for Jailbreaking Large Audio-Language Models
entries.summary: A benchmark for jailbreak vulnerabilities in large audio-language models. AJailBench-Base contains adversarial audio prompts across 10 policy-violating categories converted from textual jailbreak attacks via TTS; an Audio Perturbation Toolkit then applies time, frequency and amplitude distortions under a semantic-consistency constraint with Bayesian optimisation to produce the extended AJailBench-APT set.
entries.size: 1,495 adversarial audio prompts (Base) plus optimised APT variants
entries.note: No evaluated LAM is consistently robust, and small semantically preserved perturbations markedly reduce safety performance.

entries.name: ALAS (Automatic Latent Alignment Score)
entries.full_title: ALAS: An Automatic Latent Alignment Score for Audio Language Models
entries.summary: A model- and task-agnostic evaluation metric that probes a Speech-LLM's per-layer hidden states, scoring cross-modal cosine similarity between audio and text representations against a Whisper-derived reference, requiring only a frozen forward pass and an off-the-shelf ASR reference and calibrated to an interpretable uniform baseline. Applied to four open-source Speech-LLMs (AF3, Qwen2-Audio, Qwen-Omni, SALMONN) across emotion recognition (IEMOCAP), open-ended SQA (LibriSQA) and multi-choice audio understanding (MMAU-speech), it shows alignment depth reflects encoder design and tracks but does not duplicate task accuracy.

entries.name: Audio Injection Robustness Benchmark
entries.full_title: Evaluating Robustness of Large Audio Language Models to Audio Injection: An Empirical Study
entries.summary: A benchmark framework and empirical study evaluating how well large audio-language models resist malicious audio injection, covering four attack scenarios: Audio Interference Attack, Instruction Following Attack, Context Injection Attack and Judgment Hijacking Attack. Five leading LALMs are scored with Defense Success Rate, Context Robustness Score and Judgment Robustness Index, and the study varies the position of injected content and the system prompt.
entries.note: No single model is best across attack types; injected content is most effective at the start of a sequence, and stronger instruction-following correlates negatively with robustness.

entries.name: AudioTrust
entries.full_title: AudioTrust: Benchmarking the Multifaceted Trustworthiness of Audio Large Language Models
entries.summary: A large-scale framework for evaluating the trustworthiness of audio large language models under audio-specific risks arising from non-semantic acoustic cues such as timbre, accent and background noise. It spans six dimensions - fairness, hallucination, safety, privacy, robustness and authentication - over 26 sub-tasks, using real-world audio from daily conversations, emergency calls and voice-assistant interactions with human-validated automated scoring pipelines.
entries.size: more than 4,420 audio samples across 26 sub-tasks
entries.note: Evaluation of 14 open- and closed-source ALLMs across 18 experimental settings reveals failure boundaries in high-risk audio scenarios.

entries.name: BLAB
entries.full_title: BLAB: Brutally Long Audio Bench
entries.summary: Brutally Long Audio Bench evaluates audio LMs on localization, duration estimation, emotion and counting over full-length recordings averaging about 51 minutes. Audio comes from permissively licensed sources filtered with human assistance, and each clip is paired with human-annotated natural-language questions and answers.
entries.size: 833+ hours of audio, clips averaging 51 minutes
entries.note: All six open and proprietary audio LMs tested, including Gemini 2.0 Pro and GPT-4o, degrade as duration grows and lean more on the prompt than on the audio content.

entries.name: Daily-Omni
entries.full_title: Daily-Omni: Towards Audio-Visual Reasoning with Temporal Alignment across Modalities
entries.summary: A multiple-choice audio-visual QA benchmark of real-world videos whose questions, spanning 6 task families, explicitly require cross-modal temporal reasoning. It was built with a semi-automatic pipeline covering annotation, cross-modal consistency refinement, temporal alignment elicitation and text-only leakage filtering, followed by human verification, and ships a diagnostic suite evaluating models under Audio+Video, Audio-only, Video-only and Text-only settings.
entries.note: Across 24 foundation models in 37 model-modality settings, many end-to-end MLLMs still fail on alignment-critical questions.

entries.name: DCASE 2025 Task 5 Audio QA
entries.full_title: Multi-Domain Audio Question Answering Benchmark Toward Acoustic Content Reasoning
entries.summary: The DCASE 2025 Challenge Task 5 benchmark for audio question answering over diverse acoustic scenes, split into three QA subsets: Bioacoustics, Temporal Soundscapes and Complex QA. The paper describes dataset composition (from marine mammal calls to soundscapes and complex real-world clips), the evaluation protocol, and baseline systems Qwen2-Audio-7B, AudioFlamingo 2 and Gemini-2-Flash.
entries.note: Preliminary development-set results vary strongly across models and subsets.

entries.name: IFEval-Audio
entries.full_title: IFEval-Audio: Benchmarking Instruction-Following Capability in Audio-based Large Language Models
entries.summary: An evaluation dataset for instruction-following in audio LLMs. Each example pairs an audio input with a text instruction whose output must satisfy a specified structural constraint, spanning six dimensions: Content, Capitalization, Symbol, List Structure, Length and Format.
entries.io: audio in with text instruction, text out
entries.note: Targets the observation that instruction-following degrades after alignment with non-text modalities, an area unexplored for audio LLMs.

entries.name: JALMBench
entries.full_title: JALMBench: Benchmarking Jailbreak Vulnerabilities in Audio Language Models
entries.summary: A unified benchmark and framework for comparing jailbreak attacks against large audio-language models, pairing a large adversarial audio dataset with support for 12 LALMs, 8 attack methods (4 text-transferred and 4 audio-originated) and 5 defenses. It analyses attack efficiency, topic sensitivity, voice diversity and model architecture, plus prompt- and response-level mitigations.
entries.size: 11,316 text samples and 245,355 audio samples (>1,000 hours)
entries.note: Text-based safety alignment partially transfers to audio input and interleaved audio-text strategies generalise better, while general-purpose moderation barely helps.

entries.name: MMAR
entries.full_title: MMAR: A Challenging Benchmark for Deep Reasoning in Speech, Audio, Music, and Their Mix
entries.summary: A benchmark of curated audio-question-answer triplets drawn from real-world internet videos, spanning sound, music, speech and mixed-modality audio. Questions are organised into four hierarchical reasoning layers - Signal, Perception, Semantic and Cultural - with sub-categories, and each item is annotated with a chain-of-thought rationale; some questions require graduate-level perceptual or domain knowledge.
entries.note: Evaluated across LALMs, audio reasoning models, omni models and text LLMs given captions, exposing broad limitations in audio understanding and reasoning.

entries.name: S2SBench
entries.full_title: S2SBench: A Benchmark for Quantifying Intelligence Degradation in Speech-to-Speech Large Language Models
entries.summary: A benchmark quantifying "intelligence degradation" in end-to-end speech-to-speech LLMs, i.e. the drop in reasoning and generation quality when input is audio rather than text. It provides diagnostic datasets for sentence continuation and commonsense reasoning under audio input and a pairwise protocol based on perplexity differences between plausible and implausible samples.
entries.note: Applied to trace the training process of Baichuan-Audio.

entries.name: SAKURA
entries.full_title: SAKURA: On the Multi-hop Reasoning of Large Audio-Language Models Based on Speech and Audio Information
entries.summary: A benchmark assessing multi-hop reasoning in large audio-language models, i.e. the ability to recall and integrate multiple facts grounded in speech and audio information. It targets a gap left by existing suites that focus on general speech/audio processing, conversational ability and fairness.
entries.note: LALMs fail to integrate speech/audio representations for multi-hop reasoning even when they extract the relevant information correctly.

entries.name: Speech-IFEval
entries.full_title: Speech-IFEval: Evaluating Instruction-Following and Quantifying Catastrophic Forgetting in Speech-Aware Language Models
entries.summary: An evaluation framework for the instruction-following ability of speech-aware language models that also quantifies catastrophic forgetting relative to the underlying text LLM. It is designed to disentangle instruction following from speech perception, which existing benchmarks conflate.
entries.note: Most SLMs struggle with even basic instructions, performing far worse than text-based LLMs and proving highly sensitive to prompt variation.

entries.name: Spoken-MQA
entries.full_title: Towards Spoken Mathematical Reasoning: Benchmarking Speech-based Models over Multi-faceted Math Problems
entries.summary: A benchmark for mathematical reasoning from spoken input, covering pure arithmetic, single-step and multi-step contextual reasoning, and knowledge-oriented math problems presented in unambiguous natural spoken language. It evaluates both cascaded ASR+LLM pipelines and end-to-end speech LLMs.
entries.note: Speech LLMs handle contextual reasoning with basic arithmetic yet fail on direct arithmetic, are biased toward LaTeX-style symbolic expressions over verbalized ones, and lose much math knowledge reasoning.

entries.name: StressTest
entries.full_title: StressTest: Can YOUR Speech LM Handle the Stress?
entries.summary: A benchmark testing whether speech-aware language models can distinguish between meanings of an utterance based on its sentence-stress pattern, covering stress reasoning and stress detection. The paper additionally releases a synthetic training set (Stress-17k) and a finetuned model, StresSLM.
entries.note: Leading SLMs perform poorly on stress-based meaning disambiguation despite strong general capabilities.

entries.name: TREA
entries.full_title: Benchmarking and Confidence Evaluation of LALMs For Temporal Reasoning
entries.summary: TREA (temporal reasoning evaluation of audio) is a dataset for benchmarking temporal reasoning in large audio-language models, accompanied by an uncertainty metric that measures a model's invariance to semantically identical perturbations of the input.
entries.note: Open-source LALMs stay consistently below human performance, and accuracy and uncertainty are not necessarily correlated, arguing for evaluation beyond accuracy in high-stakes use.

entries.name: VocalBench
entries.full_title: VocalBench: Benchmarking the Vocal Conversational Abilities for Speech Interaction Models
entries.summary: A benchmark for the vocal conversational abilities of speech interaction models, built from curated instances designed to mimic real interaction scenarios. It scores models along four dimensions - semantic quality, acoustic performance, conversational abilities and robustness - across 14 user-oriented characters.
entries.note: Evaluation of 27 mainstream models exposes challenges common to current speech-interaction designs.

entries.name: Vox-Profile
entries.full_title: Vox-Profile: A Speech Foundation Model Benchmark for Characterizing Diverse Speaker and Speech Traits
entries.summary: A benchmark for characterizing rich speaker and speech traits with speech foundation models, producing multi-dimensional profiles of static traits (age, sex, accent) and dynamic speech properties (emotion, speech flow). It is grounded in speech science and linguistics with domain-expert input, and its automated profiles are validated against human evaluation. Downstream uses include augmenting ASR datasets to analyse performance variability and evaluating speech generation systems.
entries.size: experiments over 15+ publicly available speech datasets
entries.note: Automated profiles show convergent validity with human evaluation.

entries.name: CMI-Bench
entries.full_title: CMI-Bench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Evaluating Music Instruction Following
entries.summary: Reinterprets a broad range of traditional music information retrieval annotations as instruction-following tasks so that audio-text LLMs can be evaluated on them directly. Tasks include genre classification, emotion regression and tagging, instrument classification, pitch estimation, key detection, lyrics transcription, melody extraction, vocal and instrument performance technique recognition, music tagging, music captioning and (down)beat tracking, scored with the standard MIR metrics used by supervised systems so results are directly comparable. An evaluation toolkit supports open-source audio-text LLMs such as LTU, Qwen-Audio, SALMONN and MusiLingo.
metrics: standard supervised MIR metrics per task
entries.note: finds large gaps between audio-text LLMs and supervised MIR models, plus culture, chronological and gender bias

entries.name: DEBATE
entries.full_title: DEBATE: A Dataset for Disentangling Textual Ambiguity in Mandarin Through Speech
entries.summary: A public Chinese speech-text dataset for studying disambiguation through speech: how pronunciation, pause, stress and intonation resolve textual ambiguity and reveal a speaker's intended meaning. It pairs 1,001 carefully selected ambiguous utterances with recordings by 10 native speakers each, and is used to benchmark three state-of-the-art large speech and audio-language models against human listeners.
entries.size: 1,001 ambiguous utterances, each recorded by 10 native speakers
entries.note: reports large gaps between machine and human understanding of spoken intent

entries.name: MMSU
entries.full_title: MMSU: A Massive Multi-task Spoken Language Understanding and Reasoning Benchmark
entries.summary: A massive multi-task benchmark for spoken language understanding and reasoning, built from curated audio-question-answer triplets across 47 tasks. It is grounded in linguistic theory, systematically covering phonetics, prosody, rhetoric, syntactics, semantics and paralinguistics, and probes both fine-grained perception and complex reasoning in natural speech.
entries.note: Rigorous evaluation of 14 advanced SpeechLLMs shows substantial room for improvement across the perception and reasoning levels.

entries.name: mSTEB
entries.full_title: mSTEB: Massively Multilingual Evaluation of LLMs on Speech and Text Tasks
entries.summary: A massively multilingual benchmark evaluating LLMs on speech and text modalities across language identification, text classification, question answering and translation, aimed at the lack of standardized evaluation for low-resource languages. It reports results for Gemini 2.0 Flash, GPT-4o (Audio), Qwen2-Audio and Gemma 3 27B.
entries.io: speech and text in, text out
entries.note: A wide high- versus low-resource performance gap, most severe for languages spoken in Africa and the Americas/Oceania.

entries.name: OmniEval
entries.full_title: OmniEval: A Benchmark for Evaluating Omni-modal Models with Visual, Auditory, and Textual Inputs
entries.summary: A benchmark for omni-modal models that take visual, auditory and textual input, designed so that tasks require joint audio-video perception rather than a single modality. It contains 810 audio-visual synchronised videos (285 Chinese, 525 English) and 2,617 question-answer pairs (1,412 open-ended, 1,205 multiple-choice) spanning 3 major and 12 sub-task types, including a fine-grained video localisation task called Grounding.
entries.io: video, audio and text in, text out

entries.name: SOVA-Bench
entries.full_title: SOVA-Bench: Benchmarking the Speech Conversation Ability for LLM-based Voice Assistant
entries.summary: The Speech cOnversational Voice Assistant Benchmark compares LLM-based voice assistants on general knowledge, speech recognition and understanding, and both semantic and acoustic generative ability. It is motivated by the fact that prior evaluations focused on speech understanding and did not quantify the acoustic quality of the generated response.
entries.note: Presented as one of the more systematic end-to-end evaluation frameworks for speech LLMs, adding acoustic-quality measurement to understanding-focused evaluation.

entries.name: WildSpeech-Bench
entries.full_title: WildSpeech-Bench: Benchmarking End-to-End SpeechLLMs in the Wild
entries.summary: A benchmark for end-to-end speech LLMs built from curated real-world chat data rendered into spoken queries, with deliberate variation in speaker attributes and acoustic conditions and injected speech-specific phenomena such as prosody, homophones and stuttering. Responses are scored by a query-aware automatic evaluation method that generates a customised checklist and prompt per query, enabling fine-grained analysis across speech scenarios.
entries.note: reports significant performance differences across speech scenarios among mainstream speech models

entries.name: AP²
entries.full_title: The Man Behind the Sound: Demystifying Audio Private Attribute Profiling via Multimodal Large Language Model Agents
entries.summary: An audio benchmark dataset, built from two real-world subsets annotated with sensitive personal-attribute labels, for studying whether multimodal LLMs can infer private attributes from covertly captured audio (termed audio private attribute profiling). The paper also proposes Gifts, a hybrid multi-agent framework in which an LLM guides an audio-language model and then forensically consolidates its inferences, and investigates model-level and data-level defences.
entries.size: two real-world subsets with sensitive-attribute annotations
entries.note: validates that audio-based privacy attacks with MLLMs are feasible; existing ALMs hallucinate badly on long-context responses

entries.name: C3
entries.full_title: C3: A Bilingual Benchmark for Spoken Dialogue Models Exploring Challenges in Complex Conversations
entries.summary: A bilingual English/Chinese benchmark of 1,079 instances targeting the challenges that make voice interaction harder than text for spoken dialogue models: semantic ambiguity from polysemy, phonological ambiguity from heterographs, heteronyms and stress patterns, and context-dependency from omission, coreference and multi-turn interaction. It ships with an LLM-based evaluation method reported to align closely with human judgment.
metrics: LLM-based evaluation aligned with human judgment

entries.name: FD-Bench
entries.full_title: FD-Bench: A Full-Duplex Benchmarking Pipeline Designed for Full Duplex Spoken Dialogue Systems
entries.summary: A benchmarking pipeline that combines LLMs, TTS and ASR to stress-test full-duplex spoken dialogue systems on behaviours that turn-taking benchmarks do not cover: handling user interruptions, managing delays and staying robust under frequent disruption and noise. It was applied to three open-source full-duplex systems (Moshi, Freeze-Omni, VITA-1.5) using over 40 hours of generated speech across 293 simulated conversations and 1,200 interruptions.
entries.size: 293 simulated conversations, 1,200 interruptions, 40+ hours of generated speech
entries.note: all three tested systems frequently fail to respond to user interruptions under frequent disruption and noise

entries.name: Full-Duplex-Bench v1.5
entries.full_title: Full-Duplex-Bench v1.5: Evaluating Overlap Handling for Full-Duplex Speech Models
entries.summary: A fully automated benchmark that probes how full-duplex speech models behave during overlapping speech, simulating four scenarios: user interruption, user backchannel, the user talking to someone else, and background speech. It works with both open-source and commercial API models and reports categorical dialogue behaviours, stop and response latency, and prosodic adaptation.
entries.note: separates two divergent strategies among current agents: responsive (fast reaction to any input) versus floor-holding (filtering overlapping events)

entries.name: MCIF
entries.full_title: MCIF: Multimodal Crosslingual Instruction-Following Benchmark from Scientific Talks
entries.summary: A human-annotated crosslingual, multimodal instruction-following benchmark derived from scientific talks, covering speech, vision and text in English, German, Italian and Chinese with all dimensions fully aligned in parallel. It spans four macro-tasks — recognition, translation, question answering and summarisation — over both short- and long-form inputs, so instruction following can be assessed jointly across languages, modalities and input length.
entries.io: speech, vision and text in, text out
entries.note: benchmarking 23 models shows universal challenges across modalities and tasks; released CC-BY 4.0

entries.name: MECAT
entries.full_title: MECAT: A Multi-Experts Constructed Benchmark for Fine-Grained Audio Understanding Tasks
entries.summary: A Multi-Expert Constructed Benchmark for fine-grained audio understanding, generated via a pipeline combining specialized expert-model analysis with chain-of-thought LLM reasoning to produce multi-perspective fine-grained captions and open-set question-answering pairs. It introduces the DATE metric, which penalizes generic terms and rewards detailed descriptions by combining semantic similarity with cross-sample discriminability, and presents a comprehensive evaluation of state-of-the-art audio models.

entries.name: MultiVox
entries.full_title: MultiVox: A Benchmark for Evaluating Voice Assistants for Multimodal Interactions
entries.summary: The first omni voice assistant benchmark designed to evaluate whether voice assistants integrate spoken and visual cues, including implicit paralinguistic speech features such as pitch, emotion, timbre and volume and environmental acoustic context. It includes 1000 human-annotated and recorded speech dialogues covering diverse paralinguistic features together with images and videos as visual cues.
tasks: paralinguistic cue integration with visual signals

entries.name: SpeechIQ
entries.full_title: SpeechIQ: Speech-Agentic Intelligence Quotient Across Cognitive Levels in Voice Understanding by Large Language Models
entries.summary: An evaluation pipeline that scores voice-understanding LLMs on three cognitive levels adapted from Bloom's taxonomy: Remembering (WER for verbatim accuracy), Understanding (similarity of the model's interpretation) and Application (QA accuracy standing in for downstream tasks). It gives a unified comparison between cascaded ASR-plus-LLM pipelines and end-to-end models.
entries.note: also surfaces annotation errors in existing benchmarks and detects hallucinations in voice LLMs

entries.name: TELEVAL
entries.full_title: TELEVAL: A Dynamic Benchmark Designed for Spoken Language Models in Chinese Interactive Scenarios
entries.summary: A dynamic, user-centred benchmark for spoken language models in realistic Chinese spoken interaction, organised around two aspects: Reliable Content Fulfillment (understanding spoken input and producing semantically correct responses) and Interactional Appropriateness (human-like, colloquial replies that implicitly account for paralinguistic cues). It is positioned against benchmarks that emphasise task completion and capability scaling rather than how users actually talk to such systems.
entries.note: models strong on semantic and knowledge tasks still fail to produce interactionally appropriate responses

entries.name: UGC-VideoCap
entries.full_title: UGC-VideoCaptioner: An Omni UGC Video Detail Caption Model and New Benchmarks
entries.summary: A benchmark and model framework for detailed omnimodal captioning of short-form user-generated videos, built on 1000 TikTok videos annotated through a three-stage human-in-the-loop pipeline covering audio-only, visual-only, and joint audio-visual semantics. It also includes 4000 QA pairs probing both unimodal and cross-modal understanding, emphasizing balanced integration of audio and visual modalities.

entries.name: AHELM
entries.full_title: AHELM: A Holistic Evaluation of Audio-Language Models
entries.summary: A HELM-style holistic benchmark for audio-language models that aggregates many datasets — including two new synthetic audio-text sets, PARADE for stereotype avoidance and CoRe-Bench for inferential multi-turn reasoning over conversational audio — to measure 10 aspects: audio perception, knowledge, reasoning, emotion detection, bias, fairness, multilinguality, robustness, toxicity and safety. Prompts, inference parameters and metrics are standardised so 14 open-weight and closed-API models plus three ASR-plus-LLM baseline systems can be compared equitably, and all raw prompts and generations are published.
entries.io: interleaved audio and text in, text out
entries.note: Gemini 2.5 Pro leads 5 of 10 aspects but shows group unfairness on ASR tasks (p=0.01), and a speech-to-text-only baseline still ranks 6th overall

entries.name: AudioSafe
entries.full_title: Hidden in the Noise: Unveiling Backdoors in Audio LLMs Alignment through Latent Acoustic Pattern Triggers
entries.summary: A benchmark spanning nine distinct risk types, developed to test how robust audio LLMs are to backdoor triggers hidden in acoustic features rather than in content. It accompanies HIN (Hidden in the Noise), an attack framework that modifies raw waveforms via temporal-dynamics changes and spectrally tailored noise so the acoustic encoder picks up a consistent trigger pattern.
entries.note: environment noise and speech-rate triggers exceed 90% average attack success rate, while volume is a near-useless trigger and poisoning barely perturbs the loss curve

entries.name: AURA
entries.full_title: AURA: A Fine-Grained Benchmark and Decomposed Metric for Audio-Visual Reasoning
entries.summary: A benchmark for evaluating cross-modal reasoning of Audio-Visual LLMs and Omni-modal Language Models, with questions across six cognitive domains including causality, timbre and pitch, tempo and audio-visual synchronization, unanswerability, implicit distractions, and skill profiling, explicitly designed to be unanswerable from a single modality. It introduces AuraScore, a decomposed metric separating factual consistency (grounding in perceptual evidence) from core inference to assess reasoning fidelity rather than final-answer accuracy.

entries.name: CCFQA
entries.full_title: CCFQA: A Benchmark for Cross-Lingual and Cross-Modal Speech and Text Factuality Evaluation
entries.summary: A cross-lingual and cross-modal factuality benchmark containing parallel speech-text factual questions across 8 languages, designed to systematically evaluate multimodal LLMs' cross-lingual and cross-modal factuality. Experiments show current MLLMs still face substantial challenges, and the authors propose a few-shot transfer strategy that reaches competitive performance with GPT-4o-mini-Audio using 5-shot training.
entries.size: parallel speech-text factual QA across 8 languages

entries.name: EMO-Reasoning
entries.full_title: EMO-Reasoning: Benchmarking Emotional Reasoning Capabilities in Spoken Dialogue Systems
entries.summary: A benchmark for emotional coherence in spoken dialogue systems, using a curated TTS-generated dataset to simulate diverse emotional states and so work around the scarcity of emotional speech data. It introduces a Cross-turn Emotion Reasoning Score for emotion transitions across multi-turn dialogue and evaluates seven dialogue systems with continuous, categorical and perceptual metrics.
entries.venue: (ASRU 2025) 2025 IEEE Automatic Speech Recognition and Understanding W
metrics: continuous, categorical and perceptual emotion metrics
entries.note: the framework detects emotional inconsistencies in current dialogue systems

entries.name: MCR-Bench
entries.full_title: When Audio and Text Disagree: Revealing Text Bias in Large Audio-Language Models
entries.summary: A benchmark that presents large audio-language models with deliberately inconsistent audio-text pairs across diverse audio understanding tasks to measure which modality they prioritise. It shows a pronounced bias toward the textual input, with models frequently disregarding audio evidence, and additionally analyses contributing factors, supervised-finetuning mitigation, and confidence patterns.
entries.io: audio and text in, text out
entries.note: models stay overconfident even when the text contradicts the audio, degrading audio-centric task performance

entries.name: MMAU-Pro
