entries.full_title: MMAU-Pro: A Challenging and Comprehensive Benchmark for Holistic Evaluation of Audio General Intelligence
entries.summary: A comprehensive benchmark for holistic audio intelligence with 5,305 instances, each pairing one or more in-the-wild audio clips with expert-written question-answer pairs spanning speech, sound, music and their combinations. It covers 49 distinct skills and dimensions including long-form audio comprehension, spatial audio reasoning and multi-audio understanding, with questions deliberately designed to require multi-hop reasoning in both multiple-choice and open-ended formats.
entries.note: Gemini 2.5 Flash reaches only 59.2% and Audio Flamingo 3 only 51.7%, near chance in several categories

entries.name: MSU-Bench
entries.full_title: MSU-Bench: Towards Understanding the Conversational Multi-talker Scenarios
entries.summary: A speaker-centric benchmark for multi-speaker conversational understanding in large audio-language models, organised into four progressive tiers: single-speaker static attribute understanding, single-speaker dynamic attribute understanding, multi-speaker background understanding and multi-speaker interaction understanding. Every task is grounded in speaker context, moving from basic perception to reasoning across several speakers.
entries.io: multi-speaker conversational audio in, text out
entries.note: all models degrade sharply as tier complexity rises, and open-source models lag commercial ones most on multi-speaker interaction reasoning

entries.name: MTalk-Bench
entries.full_title: MTalk-Bench: Evaluating Speech-to-Speech Models in Multi-Turn Dialogues via Arena-style and Rubrics Protocols
entries.summary: A multi-turn speech-to-speech benchmark covering three dimensions — semantic information, paralinguistic information and ambient sound — each with nine realistic scenarios plus targeted tasks for capabilities such as reasoning. Evaluation uses a dual protocol combining arena-style pairwise comparison for relative ranking and rubric-based absolute scoring, with both model and human outputs judged by human evaluators and by LLMs.
entries.note: S2S models handle semantics well but underperform on paralinguistics and ambient sound, and regain coherence by padding response length; LLM judges show position and length bias

entries.name: OMHBench
entries.full_title: OMHBench: Benchmarking Balanced and Grounded Omni-Modal Multi-Hop Reasoning
entries.summary: A benchmark of 6,144 questions with balanced reasoning paths jointly grounded across text, vision, and speech, designed to rigorously evaluate omni-modal multi-hop reasoning while avoiding modality shortcuts and biased reasoning paths. Evaluation of 13 state-of-the-art models shows high sensitivity to reasoning-path variation and particular difficulty with the speech modality.

entries.name: Omni-SafetyBench
entries.full_title: Omni-SafetyBench: A Benchmark for Safety Evaluation of Audio-Visual Large Language Models
entries.summary: A parallel safety benchmark for omni-modal LLMs consisting of 24 modality variations with 972 samples each, including audio-visual harm cases, so that safety under joint audio-visual input and consistency across modalities can both be measured. It proposes a Safety-score built from Conditional Attack Success Rate and Conditional Refusal Rate (to discount comprehension failures) plus a Cross-Modal Safety Consistency score, and is used to assess existing safety alignment algorithms.
entries.io: audio, visual and text in, text out
entries.note: only 3 of 10 evaluated models exceed 0.6 on both scores, and defences weaken most under joint audio-visual input

entries.name: OmniPlay
entries.full_title: OmniPlay: Benchmarking Omni-Modal Models on Omni-Modal Game Playing
entries.summary: A diagnostic benchmark of five game environments that probes fusion and reasoning across the full sensory spectrum, deliberately creating scenarios of modality synergy and conflict so agents must perform genuine cross-modal reasoning rather than ignoring auditory and temporal cues. Evaluation of six leading omni-modal models finds superhuman high-fidelity memory but systemic failures in reasoning and strategic planning, with catastrophic degradation under modality conflict.

entries.name: RealTalk-CN
entries.full_title: RealTalk-CN: A Realistic Chinese Speech-Text Dialogue Benchmark With Cross-Modal Interaction Analysis
entries.summary: A Chinese multi-turn, multi-domain speech-text dual-modal task-oriented dialogue benchmark of 5.4k dialogues (60K utterances, 150 hours) with paired speech-text annotations and annotated spontaneous speech disfluencies. It adds a cross-modal chat task in which the user dynamically switches between speech and text, and evaluates robustness to disfluencies, sensitivity to speaker characteristics and cross-domain performance of speech-based LLMs.
entries.io: speech or text in, text out
entries.note: first Chinese speech-text dual-modal TOD resource with annotated spontaneous disfluencies

entries.name: SageLM
entries.full_title: SageLM: A Multi-aspect and Explainable Large Language Model for Speech Judgement
entries.summary: An end-to-end, multi-aspect and explainable speech LLM built to judge speech-to-speech models, assessing semantic and acoustic dimensions jointly rather than discarding acoustics as cascaded evaluators do. It uses rationale-based supervision for explainability and is trained in two stages on SpeechFeedback, a synthetic speech preference dataset introduced to offset the scarcity of real speech preference data.
entries.note: reaches 82.79% agreement with human evaluators, beating cascaded baselines by at least 7.42% and SLM-based judges by 26.20%

entries.name: SpeechR
entries.full_title: SpeechR: A Benchmark for Speech Reasoning in Large Audio-Language Models
entries.summary: A benchmark for reasoning over speech in large audio-language models along three dimensions — factual retrieval, procedural inference and normative judgment — in contrast to evaluations that stop at surface-level perception. It has three formats: a multiple-choice version measuring answer selection accuracy, a generative version assessing coherence and logical consistency of reasoning chains, and an acoustic-feature version testing whether variation in stress and emotion changes reasoning performance.
entries.note: across eleven LALMs, high transcription accuracy does not translate into strong reasoning ability

entries.name: SpeechRole
entries.full_title: SpeechRole: A Large-Scale Dataset and Benchmark for Evaluating Speech Role-Playing Agents
entries.summary: A unified framework for building and assessing speech role-playing agents. SpeechRole-Data provides 98 roles and 111k speech-to-speech conversations with rich timbre and prosodic variation, while SpeechRole-Eval is a multidimensional benchmark that scores the generated speech directly — preserving paralinguistic cues — along interaction ability, speech expressiveness and role-playing fidelity.
entries.note: GPT-4o Audio is fluent and natural but weak on prosody consistency and emotion appropriateness; cascaded and end-to-end systems tie on interaction and role fidelity, suggesting the text LLM dominates those

entries.name: WoW-Bench
entries.full_title: WoW-Bench: Evaluating Fine-Grained Acoustic Perception in Audio-Language Models via Marine Mammal Vocalizations
entries.summary: WoW-Bench (World-of-Whale) evaluates low-level listening in large audio language models using marine mammal vocalizations, where semantic shortcuts are unavailable. It splits into a Perception benchmark for categorizing novel sounds (e.g. pitch and duration cues) and a Cognition benchmark structured on Bloom's taxonomy (remember, understand, apply, analyze), with distractor questions added to check whether models actually listen rather than rely on heuristics.
entries.note: state-of-the-art LALMs score far below human level, indicating weak auditory grounding

entries.name: AU-Harness
entries.full_title: AU-Harness: An Open-Source Toolkit for Holistic Evaluation of Audio LLMs
entries.summary: AU-Harness is an open-source evaluation framework for large audio language models that standardizes prompting protocols and configurations for fair comparison across many audio benchmarks. It adds optimized batch processing and parallel execution for large-scale runs, and explicit multi-turn dialogue support enabling analysis of cross-turn context integration and audio reasoning.
entries.note: reports up to 151% speedup over existing evaluation toolkits and fills a gap in multi-turn dialogue support

entries.name: CMDAR
entries.full_title: CMDAR: A Chinese Multi-scene Dynamic Audio Reasoning Benchmark with Diverse Challenges
entries.summary: A Chinese benchmark for complex, multi-scene, and dynamically evolving audio reasoning, comprising 3,000 curated question-answer pairs linked to diverse audio clips across five categories of complex reasoning and three question types. Twenty-six state-of-the-art audio language models are benchmarked, showing limitations on complex reasoning, multi-audio multiple choice, and open-ended tasks.

entries.name: CP-Bench
entries.full_title: Benchmarking Contextual and Paralinguistic Reasoning in Speech-LLMs: A Case Study with In-the-Wild Data
entries.summary: CP-Bench evaluates speech-LLMs on contextual paralinguistic reasoning: integrating verbal content with non-verbal cues such as emotion and prosody. It consists of two curated question-answering datasets over in-the-wild speech that require both linguistic and empathetic understanding, with analysis across question types and a temperature-tuning study on the two strongest models.
entries.note: exposes a gap left by existing evaluations, which do not test joint verbal plus non-verbal understanding

entries.name: FairDialogue
entries.full_title: Evaluating Bias in Spoken Dialogue LLMs for Real-World Decisions and Recommendations
entries.summary: FairDialogue systematically measures bias in end-to-end spoken dialogue models with audio input and output, examining how paralinguistic attributes (age, gender, accent) affect decision-making and recommendation outputs, and how multi-turn conversations with repeated negative feedback compound those effects. Bias is quantified with a Group Unfairness Score for decisions and a similarity-based normalized statistics rate for recommendations, over open-source and closed-source models.
tasks: multi-turn dialogue with repeated negative feedback
entries.note: closed-source models show lower bias, open-source models are more sensitive to age and gender, recommendation tasks amplify cross-group disparities, and biased decisions can persist across turns

entries.name: Faithfulness benchmark for LALMs (audio and CoT interventions)
entries.full_title: Investigating Faithfulness in Large Audio Language Models
entries.summary: A systematic framework plus benchmark for evaluating chain-of-thought faithfulness in Large Audio Language Models with respect to both the input audio and the final prediction, defining three criteria: hallucination-free, holistic, and attentive listening. It uses audio interventions and CoT interventions, and experiments on Audio Flamingo 3 and Qwen2.5-Omni suggest reasoning often aligns with the final prediction but is not strongly grounded in the audio.

entries.name: FLEXI
entries.full_title: FLEXI: Benchmarking Full-duplex Human-LLM Speech Interaction
entries.summary: FLEXI benchmarks full-duplex speech-to-speech human-LLM interaction, and is framed as the first such benchmark to explicitly include model-initiated interruption in emergency scenarios. It evaluates latency, response quality and conversational effectiveness of real-time dialogue across six human-LLM interaction scenarios.
entries.note: reveals large gaps between open-source and commercial models in emergency awareness, turn terminating and interaction latency

entries.name: Game-Time Benchmark
entries.full_title: Game-Time: Evaluating Temporal Dynamics in Spoken Language Models
entries.summary: Game-Time assesses temporal dynamics in conversational spoken language models: timing, tempo and simultaneous speaking. Inspired by language-learning activities, it pairs basic spoken instruction-following tasks with advanced tasks that add temporal constraints such as tempo adherence and synchronized responses.
entries.note: nearly all models degrade substantially under temporal constraints, and many contemporary systems still fail basic instruction following

entries.name: Gaslighting Attacks Benchmark for Speech LLMs
entries.full_title: Benchmarking Gaslighting Attacks Against Speech Large Language Models
entries.summary: A benchmark of manipulative prompting against speech LLMs using five gaslighting strategies (Anger, Cognitive Disruption, Sarcasm, Implicit, Professional Negation) designed to mislead, override or distort model reasoning. It records both accuracy degradation and behavioural responses such as unsolicited apologies and refusals, and adds acoustic perturbation experiments to probe multimodal robustness.
entries.note: average 24.3% accuracy drop across five gaslighting strategies over 5 speech and multimodal LLMs

entries.name: MusiCRS
entries.full_title: MusiCRS: Benchmarking Audio-Centric Conversational Recommendation
entries.summary: MusiCRS is a benchmark for audio-centric conversational recommendation that links authentic Reddit user conversations to the tracks they discuss, with audio grounding via YouTube links. It supports three input configurations — audio-only, query-only and audio+query — so audio-LLMs, retrieval models and traditional approaches can be compared on whether they actually use the audio.
tasks: audio-only vs query-only vs audio+query ablation
entries.io: audio and text in, text out
entries.note: optimal performance often occurs in single-modality settings, showing current systems fail at cross-modal integration of dialogue semantics with audio

entries.name: RePOPE-Spk
entries.full_title: Evaluating Hallucinations in Audio-Visual Multimodal LLMs with Spoken Queries under Diverse Acoustic Conditions
entries.summary: The paper introduces a systematic pipeline that converts existing multimodal hallucination benchmarks into spoken-query versions while preserving the original tasks and labels, and instantiates it as RePOPE-Spk, where all queries are provided as spoken audio under diverse acoustic conditions. Experiments show hallucination error rates increase by 3-6% with clean speech and up to 30% under environmental noise relative to written queries, with many-shot prompting and chain-of-thought providing only partial mitigation.
tasks: object hallucination probing with spoken queries

entries.name: Speech Continuation Bias Probe
entries.full_title: Speak Your Mind: The Speech Continuation Task as a Probe of Voice-Based Model Bias
entries.summary: This work uses the Speech Continuation task — generating a coherent extension of a spoken prompt while preserving semantic context and speaker identity — as a controlled diagnostic for bias in speech foundation models. It evaluates how speaker gender and phonation type (breathy, creaky, end-creak) affect continuations across speaker similarity, voice-quality preservation and text-based bias metrics, on SpiritLM (base and expressive), VAE-GSLM and SpeechGPT.
entries.note: once coherence is high enough, gender effects appear on agency and sentence polarity, and continuations revert toward modal phonation more strongly for female prompts

entries.name: SpeechLLM Bias Transferability Suite
entries.full_title: Do Bias Benchmarks Generalise? Evidence from Voice-based Evaluation of Gender Bias in SpeechLLMs
entries.summary: A meta-evaluation testing whether multiple-choice gender-bias benchmarks for speech LLMs predict behaviour elsewhere. Three SpeechLLMs are LoRA-fine-tuned to induce stereotypical, anti-stereotypical or neutral MCQA behaviours, then checked for transfer to a second MCQA bias benchmark and to long-form creative generation; the paper also proposes an evaluation suite for measuring behaviour transferability in future models and benchmarks.
entries.note: MCQA bias scores fail to reliably predict bias on other MCQA benchmarks or on long-form generation

entries.name: SSEU-Bench
entries.full_title: Can Large Audio Language Models Understand Audio Well? Speech, Scene and Events Understanding Benchmark for LALMs
entries.summary: SSEU-Bench evaluates whether large audio language models understand audio clips that mix speech and non-speech content, explicitly varying the energy levels of the speech and non-speech components. It provides both independent and joint understanding settings for speech, acoustic scene and audio events, and shows that Chain-of-Thought decomposition improves joint understanding.
entries.note: some LALMs underperform in the joint understanding setting relative to the independent settings

entries.name: TAU (Taiwan Audio Understanding)
entries.full_title: TAU: A Benchmark for Cultural Sound Understanding Beyond Semantics
entries.summary: A benchmark of everyday Taiwanese "soundmarks" built from curated sources, human editing, and LLM-assisted question generation, producing 702 clips and 1,794 multiple-choice items that cannot be solved from transcripts alone. State-of-the-art LALMs including Gemini 2.5 and Qwen2-Audio perform far below local humans, exposing cultural blind spots in non-semantic audio.
entries.venue: ICASSP 2026 - 2026 IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech and Signal Processin

entries.name: VERA (Voice Evaluation of Reasoning Ability)
entries.full_title: Voice Evaluation of Reasoning Ability: Diagnosing the Modality-Induced Performance Gap
entries.summary: VERA comprises 2,931 voice-native episodes derived from established text benchmarks, organized into five tracks (Math, Web, Science, Long-Context, Factual) and adapted for speech interaction under real-time conversational constraints while preserving reasoning difficulty. Evaluating 12 voice systems against text baselines reveals large modality gaps (e.g., 74.8% vs 6.1% on competition math; 54.0% vs 11.3% macro-averaged) and a low-latency plateau where fast voice systems cluster near 10% accuracy.

entries.name: VoiceAssistant-Eval
entries.full_title: VoiceAssistant-Eval: Benchmarking AI Assistants across Listening, Speaking, and Viewing
entries.summary: VoiceAssistant-Eval benchmarks voice-first AI assistants across three axes: listening (natural sounds, music, spoken dialogue), speaking (multi-turn dialogue, role-play imitation, varied scenarios) and viewing (heterogeneous images). It scores response content quality, speech quality and the consistency between them, and was applied to 21 open-source models plus GPT-4o-Audio.
entries.io: speech and image in, speech and text out
entries.note: proprietary models do not universally beat open-source ones; most models speak well but lag in audio understanding, and multimodal plus role-play voice imitation remain hardest

entries.name: VoiceBBQ
entries.full_title: VoiceBBQ: Investigating Effect of Content and Acoustics in Social Bias of Spoken Language Model
entries.summary: VoiceBBQ is a spoken extension of the BBQ bias benchmark that converts every BBQ context into controlled voice conditions, enabling per-axis accuracy, bias, and consistency scores comparable to the original text benchmark. It separates social bias arising from the content aspect versus the acoustic aspect, and is used to evaluate LLaMA-Omni and Qwen2-Audio, revealing architectural contrasts in how they handle acoustic, gender, and accent bias.
tasks: spoken question answering over ambiguous/disambiguated contexts
social bias measurement across content and acoustic axes

entries.name: VoxRole
entries.full_title: VoxRole: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Evaluating Speech-Based Role-Playing Agents
entries.summary: VoxRole is a benchmark for speech-based role-playing conversational agents, targeting long-term persona consistency including paralinguistic aspects (intonation, prosody, rhythm) that text-only role-play benchmarks ignore. It was built with a two-stage automated pipeline that aligns movie audio with scripts and then uses an LLM to construct multi-dimensional character profiles, and is used for a multi-dimensional evaluation of contemporary spoken dialogue models.
entries.size: 13,335 multi-turn dialogues, 65.6 hours of speech, 1,228 characters across 261 movies

entries.name: VStyle
entries.full_title: VStyle: A Benchmark for Voice Style Adaptation with Spoken Instructions
entries.summary: VStyle defines and benchmarks Voice Style Adaptation: whether spoken language models can change their speaking style — timbre, prosody, persona — in response to natural-language spoken commands. The bilingual benchmark covers four categories of speech generation (acoustic attributes, natural language instruction, role play, implicit empathy) and is scored with an LALM-as-a-Judge framework that assesses textual faithfulness, style adherence and naturalness.
metrics: LALM-as-a-Judge: textual faithfulness, style adherence, naturalness
entries.note: both commercial systems and open-source SLMs show clear limits on controllable style adaptation

entries.name: AQEval / AURA Score
entries.full_title: AURA Score: A Metric For Holistic Audio Question Answering Evaluation
entries.summary: AQEval is presented as the first benchmark for systematically comparing Audio Question Answering evaluation metrics, consisting of 10k Audio-Language Model responses annotated by multiple humans for correctness and relevance. Analysis on AQEval shows existing metrics (BLEU, METEOR, BERTScore) correlate weakly with human judgment, especially for longer answers, motivating the proposed AURA score which achieves state-of-the-art correlation with human ratings.

entries.name: AudioMarathon
entries.full_title: AudioMarathon: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Long-Context Audio Understanding and Efficiency in Audio LLMs
entries.summary: AudioMarathon evaluates both understanding and inference efficiency of large audio language models on long-form audio. It is built on three pillars: long-context inputs of 90 to 300 seconds (2,250 to 7,500 audio tokens), full domain coverage across speech, sound and music, and tasks requiring multi-hop inference; it also analyses acceleration techniques such as token pruning and KV cache eviction.
entries.size: audio inputs of 90.0-300.0 seconds (2,250-7,500 audio tokens)
entries.note: clear performance drops as audio length grows, with trade-offs quantified for token pruning and KV cache eviction

entries.name: AV-EMO-Reasoning
entries.full_title: AV-EMO-Reasoning: Benchmarking Emotional Reasoning Capabilities in Omni-modal LLMS with Audio-visual Cues
entries.summary: A benchmark for systematically assessing emotional reasoning in omni-modal LLMs using audio-visual cues, built on a curated corpus of synthetic single-turn and multi-turn dialogues plus a real-world subset. It pairs emotion perception and interaction reasoning metrics to evaluate whether models understand user emotions and produce appropriate responses.
entries.size: synthetic single-turn and multi-turn dialogues plus a real-world subset (count not stated)

entries.name: Core Music Perception evaluation (syncopation / transposition / chord quality)
entries.full_title: Evaluating Multimodal Large Language Models on Core Music Perception Tasks
entries.summary: A diagnostic evaluation of three SOTA multimodal LLMs (Gemini 2.5 Pro, Gemini 2.5 Flash, Qwen2.5-Omni) on three core music skills - syncopation scoring, transposition detection, and chord quality identification - separating perceptual limitations (audio vs MIDI input), few-shot exposure, and reasoning strategy. Models are near ceiling on MIDI but drop notably on audio, showing they reason over symbols but do not yet listen reliably.
entries.venue: the NeurIPS 2025 Workshop on AI for Music (AI4Music), 16 pages, 1 figu
entries.size: three task suites, audio and MIDI conditions (count not stated)

entries.name: CS3-Bench
entries.full_title: CS3-Bench: Evaluating and Enhancing Speech-to-Speech LLMs for Mandarin-English Code-Switching
entries.summary: CS3-Bench (Code-Switching Speech-to-Speech Benchmark) measures how speech-to-speech LLMs handle Mandarin-English code-switching, with a knowledge-intensive question answering set and an open-ended conversation set. The paper additionally proposes data construction and training methods — Chain of Recognition for understanding and Keyword Highlighting for generation — to improve language alignment.
entries.note: 7 mainstream models drop up to 66% relatively on knowledge-intensive QA under code-switching

entries.name: EchoMind
entries.full_title: EchoMind: An Interrelated Multi-level Benchmark for Evaluating Empathetic Speech Language Models
entries.summary: EchoMind is an interrelated multi-level benchmark that walks speech language models through the cognitive stages of empathetic dialogue via sequential, context-linked tasks: spoken-content understanding, vocal-cue perception, integrated reasoning and response generation. All tasks share identical, semantically neutral scripts free of explicit emotional cues, with controlled variation in vocal style so that delivery can be tested independently of the transcript, under an empathy framework of 3 coarse and 12 fine-grained dimensions covering 39 vocal attributes.
entries.size: 3 coarse and 12 fine-grained dimensions covering 39 vocal attributes
entries.note: across 12 advanced SLMs, even the strongest struggle with high-expressive vocal cues, and weaknesses persist in instruction following and resilience to natural speech variability

entries.name: EgoSocial
entries.full_title: EgoSocial: Benchmarking Proactive Intervention Ability of Omnimodal LLMs via Egocentric Social Interaction Perception
entries.summary: EgoSocial is a large-scale egocentric dataset of 13,500 social video-question pairs designed to benchmark when an AI assistant should intervene in social interaction. The paper presents an in-depth analysis of current omnimodal LLMs (OLLMs) on detecting diverse social contextual cues, finding they struggle with intervention timing (14.4% for Gemini 2.5 Pro), and proposes EgoSoD, a method integrating multimodal contextual cues such as audio and visual signals into a social thinking graph.

entries.name: EMIS
entries.full_title: Evaluating Emotion Recognition in Spoken Language Models on Emotionally Incongruent Speech
entries.summary: A diagnostic dataset of emotionally incongruent synthetic speech, where the semantic content of an utterance conveys one emotion while the vocal expressiveness conveys another. Four spoken language models are evaluated on speech emotion recognition under this conflict to test whether they genuinely integrate acoustic and textual representations. Code and the dataset are released.
entries.note: SLMs rely predominantly on textual semantics rather than speech emotion, indicating text representations dominate acoustic ones

entries.name: Full-Duplex-Bench-v2
entries.full_title: Full-Duplex-Bench-v2: A Multi-Turn Evaluation Framework for Duplex Dialogue Systems with an Automated Examiner
entries.summary: FDB-v2 is a streaming evaluation framework for multi-turn full-duplex speech agents in which an automated examiner enforces staged goals under two pacing setups (Fast and Slow). It covers four task families — daily, correction, entity tracking and safety — and reports turn-taking fluency, multi-turn instruction following and task-specific competence, supporting both commercial APIs and open-source models.
entries.size: four task families under two pacing setups
entries.note: full-duplex systems get confused during simultaneous speech, handle corrections poorly, and lose track of referents

entries.name: Hearing the Order
entries.full_title: Hearing the Order: Investigating Position Bias in Large Audio-Language Models
entries.summary: A systematic diagnostic of position bias in large audio-language models: whether predictions depend on the order in which answer choices are presented. Six LALMs are tested on three widely used benchmarks and their spoken counterparts, and permutation-based mitigation strategies are evaluated.
entries.note: Shuffling answer options causes performance swings of up to 24% and can change model rankings, questioning current evaluation practice

entries.name: ISA-Bench
entries.full_title: ISA-Bench: Benchmarking Instruction Sensitivity for Large Audio Language Models
entries.summary: A dynamic benchmark measuring how sensitive large audio language models are to instruction phrasing, along three axes: instruction description, output format, and task composition. Open-source and proprietary LALMs are profiled for both instruction-following compliance and task accuracy under controlled instruction variations, and Qwen2-Audio is fine-tuned on an instruction-variant dataset as a mitigation.
entries.note: Even state-of-the-art LALMs degrade markedly under instruction variation, and fine-tuning for instruction robustness induces nontrivial catastrophic forgetting

entries.name: LALM MCQA robustness assessment
entries.full_title: Robustness assessment of large audio language models in multiple-choice evaluation
entries.summary: A systematic study of the fragility of the multiple-choice QA framework used to evaluate large audio-language models, spanning three benchmarks (MMAU, MMAR, MMSU) and four models (Audio Flamingo 2, Audio Flamingo 3, Qwen2.5-Omni-7B-Instruct, Kimi-Audio-7B-Instruct). It shows sensitivity to both choice ordering and paraphrasing of questions and choices, and proposes a simpler evaluation protocol and metric that account for these variations.
entries.note: Single-number MCQA accuracies hide substantial variability; the paper argues for a more detailed reporting protocol

entries.name: LISTEN
entries.full_title: Do Audio LLMs Really LISTEN, or Just Transcribe? Measuring Lexical vs. Acoustic Emotion Cues Reliance
entries.summary: Lexical vs. Acoustic Speech Test for Emotion in Narratives: a controlled benchmark that disentangles reliance on lexical content from genuine acoustic sensitivity in emotion understanding. Six state-of-the-art LALMs are evaluated under conditions where lexical and acoustic cues are aligned, conflicting, lexically neutral or absent, plus a paralinguistic-only setting.
entries.note: Consistent lexical dominance — models default to "neutral" when text is neutral, fail under cue conflict, and perform near chance in paralinguistic settings

entries.name: LongInsightBench
entries.full_title: LongInsightBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Evaluating Omni-Modal Models on Human-Centric Long-Video Understanding
entries.summary: A benchmark for human-centric long-video understanding that integrates visual, audio, and text modalities, selecting roughly 1,000 information-dense videos (lectures, interviews, vlogs) chosen for the information density of both visual and audio streams. It defines six challenging intra-event and inter-event task scenarios and uses a three-step semi-automated quality-assurance pipeline; omni-modal models still struggle with precise temporal localization.

entries.name: M3-SLU
entries.full_title: M3-SLU: Evaluating Speaker-Attributed Reasoning in Multimodal Large Language Models
entries.summary: A multimodal LLM benchmark for evaluating multi-speaker, multi-turn spoken language understanding and speaker-attributed reasoning - understanding who said what and when. Built from CHiME-6, MELD, MultiDialog and AMI, it comprises over 12,000 validated instances with paired audio, transcripts and metadata across two tasks (speaker-attributed QA and speaker attribution via utterance matching), with baselines for cascaded pipelines and end-to-end MLLMs.

entries.name: MMA-ASIA
entries.full_title: MMA-ASIA: A Multilingual and Multimodal Alignment Framework for Culturally-Grounded Evaluation
entries.summary: A human-curated, multilingual and multimodally aligned multiple-choice benchmark of 27,000 questions covering 8 Asian countries and 10 languages, aligned at the input level across text, image and speech to enable direct tests of cross-modal transfer. Its five-dimensional protocol measures cultural-awareness disparities, cross-lingual consistency, cross-modal consistency, knowledge generalization and grounding validity, with a module detecting shortcut learning.
tasks: culturally grounded multiple-choice QA from speech, text and image inputs

entries.name: MUSE
entries.full_title: The MUSE Benchmark: Probing Music Perception and Auditory Relational Reasoning in Audio LLMS
entries.summary: The Music Understanding and Structural Evaluation benchmark, an open-source resource of 10 tasks probing fundamental music perception and auditory relational reasoning in audio LLMs. Four models (Gemini Pro and Flash, Qwen2.5-Omni, Audio-Flamingo 3) are compared against a large human baseline of 200 participants, with chain-of-thought prompting also tested.
entries.note: Wide variance across models with a persistent gap to human experts; Qwen2.5-Omni and Audio-Flamingo 3 perform at or near chance, and CoT prompting is inconsistent or harmful

entries.name: OASIS
entries.full_title: OASIS: A Multilingual and Multimodal Dataset for Culturally Grounded Spoken Visual QA
entries.summary: A large-scale culturally grounded multimodal QA dataset covering images, text and speech, built with the EverydayMMQA semi-automatic framework plus multi-stage human-in-the-loop validation. It supports four input settings (text-only, speech-only, text+image, speech+image) and targets pragmatic, commonsense and culturally grounded reasoning rather than object recognition. Four closed-source, three open-source and one fine-tuned model are benchmarked.
languages: Arabic (Modern Standard and dialectal varieties, 18 countries)
entries.io: speech and/or image in, text out
entries.size: ~0.92M images, 14.8M QA pairs including 3.7M spoken questions; 383 hours human-recorded speech and 20K hours voice-cloned speech from 42 speakers
entries.note: Targets cultural and everyday knowledge in low-resource and underrepresented language varieties, where large multimodal models are typically weak

entries.name: Omni-Captioner (omni detailed perception benchmark)
entries.full_title: Omni-Captioner: Data Pipeline, Models, and Benchmark for Omni Detailed Perception
entries.summary: This work investigates omni detailed perception through a data pipeline, models, and a benchmark, identifying an inherent co-growth between detail and hallucination in current Omni Language Models. It contributes the Omni-Detective agentic data generation pipeline, an Audio-Captioner and an Omni-Captioner model, and a benchmark for evaluating fine-grained audio and audio-visual detailed description, with cascade-protocol results reported on MMAU and MMAR.

entries.name: OmniVideoBench
entries.full_title: OmniVideoBench: Towards Audio-Visual Understanding Evaluation for Omni MLLMs
entries.summary: A large-scale benchmark for synergistic audio-visual understanding in omni MLLMs, with 1,000 manually verified QA pairs derived from 628 videos ranging from seconds to 30 minutes, each annotated with step-by-step reasoning traces. It spans 13 question types covering temporal reasoning, spatial localization, counting, causal inference and summarization, emphasizing modality complementarity and logical consistency.

entries.name: Speaker-emotion safety evaluation for LALMs
entries.full_title: Investigating Safety Vulnerabilities of Large Audio-Language Models Under Speaker Emotional Variations
entries.summary: A dataset of malicious speech instructions rendered across multiple speaker emotions and intensity levels, used to test whether the safety alignment of large audio-language models holds under paralinguistic variation. Several state-of-the-art LALMs are evaluated.
entries.note: Safety is emotion-dependent and the effect of intensity is non-monotonic, with medium-intensity expressions often eliciting the most unsafe responses

entries.name: STAR-Bench
entries.full_title: STAR-Bench: Probing Deep Spatio-Temporal Reasoning as Audio 4D Intelligence
entries.summary: A benchmark for "audio 4D intelligence" — reasoning over sound dynamics in time and 3D space. It combines a Foundational Acoustic Perception setting (six attributes under absolute and relative regimes, built from procedurally synthesized and physics-simulated audio) with a Holistic Spatio-Temporal Reasoning setting covering segment reordering for continuous and discrete processes, static localization, multi-source relations and dynamic trajectories, curated through a four-stage human-annotation process. Nineteen models are evaluated against humans.
entries.note: Caption-only answering drops accuracy far more than on prior benchmarks (-31.5% temporal, -35.2% spatial), showing the tasks require cues that are hard to describe in language

entries.name: TeleEgo
entries.full_title: TeleEgo: Benchmarking Egocentric AI Assistants in the Wild
entries.summary: A long-duration, streaming, omni-modal benchmark for egocentric AI assistants, with over 14 hours per participant of synchronized egocentric video, audio and text across four life domains on a unified global timeline. It defines 12 diagnostic subtasks across Memory, Understanding and Cross-Memory Reasoning, with 3,291 human-verified QA items in multiple formats evaluated strictly in a streaming setting.

entries.name: UNO-Bench
entries.full_title: UNO-Bench: A Unified Benchmark for Exploring the Compositional Law Between Uni-modal and Omni-modal in Omni Models
entries.summary: A unified benchmark that evaluates both uni-modal and omni-modal capabilities of omni models under one ability taxonomy, spanning 44 task types and 5 modality combinations. It includes 1,250 human-curated omni-modal samples with 98% cross-modality solvability plus 2,480 enhanced uni-modal samples, and adds a multi-step open-ended question format with a general scoring model for automatic evaluation.
entries.size: 1,250 omni-modal samples plus 2,480 uni-modal samples, 44 task types

entries.name: VCB Bench
entries.full_title: VCB Bench: An Evaluation Benchmark for Audio-Grounded Large Language Model Conversational Agents
entries.summary: VCB Bench (Voice Chat Bot Bench) is a Chinese benchmark for audio-grounded conversational LALMs built entirely on real human speech rather than TTS. It evaluates three complementary dimensions: instruction following including speech-level control beyond text commands, knowledge understanding (general knowledge, reasoning, daily dialogue), and robustness under perturbations in content, environment and speaker traits.
entries.note: addresses the English-centric, synthetic-speech bias of existing LALM conversational benchmarks

entries.name: VocalBench-DF
entries.full_title: VocalBench-DF: A Benchmark for Evaluating Speech LLM Robustness to Disfluency
entries.summary: VocalBench-DF systematically evaluates the robustness of speech LLMs to disfluent user speech using a multi-dimensional disfluency taxonomy, including disfluencies associated with conditions such as Parkinson's disease that idealized benchmark inputs omit. It was run over 22 mainstream speech LLMs and analyses which components cause failure.
entries.note: substantial degradation across 22 speech LLMs, with phoneme-level processing and long-context modeling identified as the primary bottlenecks

entries.name: VoiceAgentBench
entries.full_title: VoiceAgentBench: Are Voice Assistants ready for agentic tasks?
entries.summary: VoiceAgentBench evaluates SpeechLMs in realistic spoken agentic settings, covering single-tool invocations, multi-tool workflows, multi-turn dialogue and safety. Speaker variability is simulated with a sampling strategy that picks TTS voice-conversion audio by speaker embedding to maximize acoustic diversity, and evaluation measures tool selection accuracy, structural consistency and the correctness of tool invocations, including adversarial robustness.
entries.note: ASR-LLM pipelines beat end-to-end SpeechLMs (up to 60.6% average parameter-filling accuracy on English), and all models struggle on sequential workflows, Indic languages and safety

entries.name: VoiceAgentEval (OutboundEval)
entries.full_title: VoiceAgentEval: A Dual-Dimensional Benchmark for Expert-Level Intelligent Voice-Agent Evaluation of Xbench's Professional-Aligned Series
entries.summary: A benchmark for expert-level intelligent outbound-calling agents, spanning six business domains and 30 representative sub-scenarios, each with scenario-specific process decomposition, weighted scoring and domain-adaptive metrics. A large-model-driven User Simulator generates persona-rich virtual users with realistic behaviour, emotional variability and communication styles, and a dynamic evaluation method combines automated and human-in-the-loop assessment.
entries.note: across 12 state-of-the-art LLMs, expert-level task completion trades off against interaction fluency

entries.name: When Silence Matters
entries.full_title: When Silence Matters: The Impact of Irrelevant Audio on Text Reasoning in Large Audio-Language Models
entries.summary: A diagnostic study of cross-modal interference in large audio-language models: how irrelevant audio (silence, synthetic noise, environmental sounds) affects performance on three text-based reasoning benchmarks where audio is unnecessary. Interference is measured as a function of duration, amplitude and decoding temperature, and prompting and self-consistency are tested as mitigations.
entries.io: audio plus text in, text out
entries.note: Silence, usually assumed neutral, destabilizes outputs as strongly as synthetic noise; larger models are more resilient but none are immune

entries.name: XModBench
entries.full_title: XModBench: Benchmarking Cross-Modal Capabilities and Consistency in Omni-Language Models
entries.summary: A large-scale tri-modal benchmark of 60,828 multiple-choice questions spanning five task families and all six modality compositions of question-answer pairs, built to measure cross-modal consistency in omni-modal LLMs. It diagnoses modality-invariant reasoning, modality disparity, and directional imbalance, finding that performance drops substantially when the same semantic content is delivered by audio rather than text.
entries.venue: Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2026

entries.name: AudioMotionBench
entries.full_title: AudioMotionBench: Evaluating Auditory Motion Perception in Audio LLMs
entries.summary: The first benchmark explicitly designed to evaluate auditory motion understanding in Large Audio-Language Models, using controlled question answering over binaural audio to test whether models can infer the direction and trajectory of moving sound sources. Average accuracy stays below 50%, which the authors read as a systematic motion-perception deficit.

entries.name: AV-ConfuseBench
entries.full_title: When Eyes and Ears Disagree: Can MLLMs Discern Audio-Visual Confusion?
entries.summary: A benchmark that simulates "Audio-Visual Confusion" scenes by modifying the sound of an object in a video (e.g., muting a sounding object) and asking whether that object's sound is present. Experiments show MLLMs such as Qwen2.5-Omni and Gemini 2.5 struggle to discriminate non-existent audio because of visually dominated reasoning.

entries.name: AVFakeBench
entries.full_title: AVFakeBench: A Comprehensive Audio-Video Forgery Detection Benchmark for AV-LMMs
entries.summary: An audio-video forgery detection benchmark of 12K curated audio-video questions covering seven forgery types and four levels of annotation, built with a multi-stage hybrid forgery framework spanning human and general subjects. It defines a multi-task evaluation covering binary judgment, forgery-type classification, forgery-detail selection, and explanatory reasoning, and evaluates 11 Audio-Video Large Language Models plus two detection methods.

entries.name: HPSU
entries.full_title: HPSU: A Benchmark for Human-Level Perception in Real-World Spoken Speech Understanding
entries.summary: Human-level Perception in Spoken Speech Understanding: a benchmark of over 20,000 expert-validated spoken language understanding samples in English and Chinese, spanning tasks from basic speaker attribute recognition to inference of latent intentions and implicit emotions in real-world speech. Data was produced with a semi-automatic annotation process fusing audio, textual and visual information; open-source and proprietary Speech LLMs are evaluated.
entries.note: Even top-performing Speech LLMs fall considerably short of human capability on genuine spoken interactions

entries.name: LALM-Eval (factual music comprehension benchmark)
entries.full_title: Assessing Factual Music Comprehension in Large Audio Language Models
entries.summary: Shows that assessing LALMs with the popular MusicQA dataset fails to measure factual correctness, and proposes an evaluation protocol that prompts a LALM for factually verifiable information and parses open-ended responses into a structured format scored with Precision, Recall and F1. The benchmark comprises six factual information retrieval tasks over MusicNet, the Free Music Archive, and OverClocked ReMix, with nine recent LALMs benchmarked.
tasks: factual music information retrieval from audio
entries.size: six tasks over three datasets; nine LALMs evaluated

entries.name: MedVoiceBias
entries.full_title: MedVoiceBias: A Controlled Study of Audio LLM Behavior in Clinical Decision-Making
entries.summary: A controlled study of audio LLM behaviour in clinical decision-making: 170 clinical cases are each synthesized into speech from 36 voice profiles varying age, gender and emotion, and model recommendations are compared against identical text inputs. Chain-of-thought prompting is tested as a mitigation.
entries.note: Surgical recommendations varied by up to 35% between audio and identical text input, with age disparities up to 12% persisting despite CoT; explicit reasoning did remove gender bias

entries.name: MTR-DuplexBench
entries.full_title: MTR-DuplexBench: Towards a Comprehensive Evaluation of Multi-Round Conversations for Full-Duplex Speech Language Models
entries.summary: A benchmark for multi-round evaluation of full-duplex speech language models, addressing blurred turn boundaries and context inconsistency by segmenting continuous full-duplex dialogue into discrete turns for turn-by-turn assessment. Beyond conversational features it also scores dialogue quality, instruction following and safety across rounds.
entries.note: Current FD-SLMs struggle to maintain consistent performance across multiple rounds and across evaluation dimensions

entries.name: MULTI-Bench
entries.full_title: MULTI-Bench: A Multi-Turn Interactive Benchmark for Assessing Emotional Intelligence ability of Spoken Dialogue Models
entries.summary: A multi-turn interactive benchmark for spoken dialogue models focused on emotional intelligence, organized hierarchically into a basic track (emotion understanding and reasoning) and an advanced track (emotion support and application). It comprises five tasks and about 3.2K samples with a reproducible evaluation framework; six representative SDMs are evaluated on eight subsets.
entries.note: Models do well on basic emotion understanding but leave clear room on advanced multi-turn interaction, emotion awareness and application

entries.name: ORCA
entries.full_title: ORCA: Open-ended Response Correctness Assessment for Audio Question Answering
entries.summary: An evaluation resource for judging open-ended responses from large audio language models: a three-stage annotation pipeline (human judgment, structured feedback, human-AI correction) yielding 9,663 annotations across 3,699 question-answer pairs from 15 LALMs on three audio understanding and reasoning benchmarks, with Krippendorff's alpha of 0.82. The resulting ORCA models reach Spearman 0.91 with human correctness ratings on seen benchmarks and 0.85 on unseen ones, outperforming LLM-judge baselines, and their predicted variance flags problematic benchmark items.
entries.size: 9,663 annotations over 3,699 QA pairs from 15 LALMs

entries.name: ParaS2SBench
entries.full_title: ParaS2S: Benchmarking and Aligning Spoken Language Models for Paralinguistic-aware Speech-to-Speech Interaction
entries.summary: A benchmark that scores speech-to-speech models on the naturalness of input-output pairs in terms of both response content and speaking style, using expressive and challenging queries with paralinguistic cues such as emotion, tone and speaker attributes. Its automatic judge uses a PolyTone training strategy and a multi-stage framework to avoid style hallucination in end-to-end audio-LLM judging, and correlates with human preference; the same paper introduces the ParaS2SAlign RL alignment method built on top of it.
metrics: automatic judge score for content and speaking-style appropriateness
entries.note: Existing S2S models respond to paralinguistic attributes no better than pipeline baselines; RL alignment gives a 10% relative improvement over SFT

entries.name: SACRED-Bench
entries.full_title: Speech-Audio Compositional Attacks on Multimodal LLMs and Their Mitigation with SALMONN-Guard
entries.summary: Speech-Audio Composition for RED-teaming: a black-box safety benchmark that attacks audio-capable LLMs by composing auditory scenes rather than optimizing perturbations, using three mechanisms — overlapping harmful and benign speech, mixing benign speech with harmful non-speech audio, and multi-speaker dialogue. Questions refer to audio content implicitly so no harmful information appears in the text prompt alone. The paper also proposes SALMONN-Guard, a guard model that jointly inspects speech, audio and text.
tasks: speech mixed with harmful non-speech audio
entries.io: speech and non-speech audio in, text out
entries.note: Gemini 2.5 Pro with guardrails enabled still shows a 66% attack success rate, reduced to 20% by SALMONN-Guard

entries.name: Speech-DRAME (EvalBench + RoleBench)
entries.full_title: Speech-DRAME: A Framework for Human-Aligned Benchmarks in Speech Role-Play
entries.summary: Speech-DRAME is a framework for human-aligned benchmarks in speech role-play, contributing Speech-DRAME-EvalBench (bilingual human-annotated data and protocols for training/testing speech evaluation models), DRAME-Eval (a fine-tuned evaluation model that outperforms zero-shot and few-shot ALLMs), and Speech-DRAME-RoleBench (a speech role-play benchmark using DRAME-Eval as automatic judge to compare speech foundation models). It distinguishes Archetype Evaluation (adherence to broad role archetypes) from Realism Evaluation grounded in real-world roles, addressing how zero-shot ALLM judges miss paralinguistic cues.
languages: bilingual (two languages, not specified in abstract)

entries.name: VocalBench-zh
entries.full_title: VocalBench-zh: Decomposing and Benchmarking the Speech Conversational Abilities in Mandarin Context
entries.summary: An ability-level divided evaluation suite for Mandarin speech-to-speech interaction, consisting of 10 subsets and over 10K instances covering 12 user-oriented characters. Fourteen mainstream models are evaluated; code and data are to be released.
entries.note: Fills the gap of comprehensive Mandarin S2S evaluation and exposes common challenges shared by current architectural routes

entries.name: AMUSE
entries.full_title: AMUSE: Audio-Visual Benchmark and Alignment Framework for Agentic Multi-Speaker Understanding
entries.summary: An audio-visual benchmark built around agentic, dialogue-centric tasks that require models to track who speaks, maintain roles and ground events over time. It evaluates MLLMs (e.g. GPT-4o, Qwen3-Omni) across three modes (zero-shot, guided, agentic) and six task families including spatio-temporal speaker grounding and multimodal dialogue summarization, finding weak multi-speaker reasoning across the board.

entries.name: Audio MultiChallenge
entries.full_title: Audio MultiChallenge: A Multi-Turn Evaluation of Spoken Dialogue Systems on Natural Human Interaction
entries.summary: An open-source multi-turn benchmark for end-to-end spoken dialogue systems under natural interaction patterns. It ports the text MultiChallenge axes (Inference Memory, Instruction Retention, Self Coherence) to audio, adds a Voice Editing axis testing robustness to mid-utterance speech repairs and backtracking, and adds Audio-Cue challenges requiring recall of ambient sounds and paralinguistic signals beyond semantics. 452 conversations from 47 speakers with 1,712 instance-specific rubrics were curated by a hybrid audio-native agentic and human-in-the-loop pipeline that preserves natural disfluencies.
entries.note: Frontier models struggle — the best, Gemini 3 Pro Preview (Thinking), reaches 54.65% pass rate, with failures concentrated on the new axes and Self Coherence degrading with longer audio context

entries.name: AV-SpeakerBench
entries.full_title: See, Hear, and Understand: Benchmarking Audiovisual Human Speech Understanding in Multimodal Large Language Models
entries.summary: A curated benchmark of 3,212 multiple-choice questions on speaker-centric audiovisual reasoning in real-world videos, designed to test whether MLLMs can align who speaks, what is said and when it occurs. It uses a speaker-centred formulation (speakers, not scenes, as the reasoning unit), fusion-grounded question design that embeds audiovisual dependencies into question semantics, and expert-curated annotations for temporal precision and cross-modal validity. The Gemini family outperforms open-source systems (Gemini 2.5 Pro best); Qwen3-Omni-30B approaches Gemini 2.0 Flash but lags mainly due to weaker audiovisual fusion rather than visual perception.
entries.io: real-world video with speech audio plus multiple-choice question -> selected option
entries.note: Diagnoses audiovisual fusion specifically: the open-model gap is attributed to fusion weakness, not visual perception.

entries.name: FysicsWorld
entries.full_title: FysicsWorld: A Unified Full-Modality Benchmark for Any-to-Any Understanding, Generation, and Reasoning
entries.summary: FysicsWorld is described as the first unified full-modality benchmark supporting bidirectional input-output across image, video, audio, and text, enabling any-to-any evaluation across understanding, generation, and reasoning. It comprises 16 primary tasks and 3,268 curated samples aggregated from over 40 sources, and uses a Cross-Modal Complementarity Screening strategy to produce omni-modal data for spoken interaction and fusion-dependent cross-modal reasoning; over 30 baselines including MLLMs, unified understanding-generation models, and omni-modal language models are evaluated.

entries.name: JointAVBench
entries.full_title: JointAVBench: A Benchmark for Joint Audio-Visual Reasoning Evaluation
entries.summary: A benchmark for joint audio-visual reasoning in Omni-LLMs with strict audio-video correlation, so questions cannot be answered from vision or audio alone. It spans five cognitive dimensions, four audio information types (speech, sound events, music, vocal traits) and three scene spans (single-, cross- and full-scene). Questions and answers are synthesized by an automated pipeline using vision-LLMs, audio-LLMs and general-purpose LLMs. Leading vision-only, audio-only and Omni-LLMs are evaluated; the best Omni-LLM reaches only 65.3% average accuracy, with cross-scene reasoning weakest.
tasks: speech / sound event / music / vocal-trait understanding
entries.io: video with audio track plus text question -> answer
entries.note: Built so that uni-modal (audio-only or vision-only) models cannot succeed, making it an explicit audio-grounding diagnostic; best Omni-LLM only 65.3% average accuracy.

entries.name: LongShOTBench
entries.full_title: A Benchmark for Omni-Modal Reasoning in Long Videos
entries.summary: A long-video benchmark designed around holistic omni-modal integration, intent-driven open-ended interaction, and rubric-level diagnosis, building single- and multi-turn questions from real viewing scenarios that probe visual, speech, ambient-audio, temporal, and cross-modal reasoning. Each item carries a reference answer and a weighted criterion-level rubric so scoring can identify which perceptual facts, temporal links, and modality-grounding requirements were missed.
tasks: single- and multi-turn omni-modal video QA

entries.name: MAC-SLU
entries.full_title: MAC-SLU: Multi-Intent Automotive Cabin Spoken Language Understanding Benchmark
entries.summary: A multi-intent spoken language understanding dataset set in the automotive cabin, built to raise task difficulty with authentic complex multi-intent utterances, plus a unified benchmark over leading open-source LLMs and large audio language models. Evaluation covers in-context learning, supervised fine-tuning, and both end-to-end and pipeline paradigms; code and data are public.
entries.note: In-context learning still lags well behind SFT, while end-to-end LALMs match pipeline systems and avoid ASR error propagation

entries.name: SH-Bench
entries.full_title: Protecting Bystander Privacy via Selective Hearing in Audio LLMs
entries.summary: The first benchmark for "selective hearing": whether an audio LLM can attend to an intended main speaker while refusing to process or reveal information about incidental bystander speech. It contains 3,968 real and synthetic multi-speaker audio mixtures paired with 77k multiple-choice questions probing models in general and selective operating modes, and introduces the Selective Efficacy metric combining multi-speaker comprehension with bystander-privacy protection. The paper also proposes Bystander Privacy Fine-Tuning.
entries.note: State-of-the-art models leak substantial bystander information; strong audio understanding does not translate into privacy protection

entries.name: Spoken DialogSum
entries.full_title: Spoken DialogSum: An Emotion-Rich Conversational Dataset for Spoken Dialogue Summarization
entries.summary: A corpus aligning raw conversational audio with both factual and emotion-rich summaries plus utterance-level labels for speaker age, gender and emotion, aimed at emotion-aware spoken dialogue summarization. It is built by having an LLM rewrite DialogSum scripts with Switchboard-style fillers and back-channels and tag each utterance with emotion, pitch and speaking rate, then synthesizing speech with an expressive TTS engine aligned to those labels. It comprises 13,460 emotion-diverse dialogues with baseline results for an Audio-LLM versus a cascaded ASR-LLM system.
entries.size: 13,460 dialogues, each with a factual and an emotion-focused summary
entries.note: An Audio-LLM raises emotional-summary ROUGE-L by 28% relative to a cascaded ASR-LLM pipeline, supporting end-to-end speech modelling

entries.name: WearVox
entries.full_title: WearVox: An Egocentric Multichannel Voice Assistant Benchmark for Wearables
entries.summary: WearVox is a benchmark of 3,842 multi-channel egocentric audio recordings collected via AI glasses across five tasks: Search-Grounded QA, Closed-Book QA, Side-Talk Rejection, Tool Calling, and Speech Translation, spanning varied indoor/outdoor environments and acoustic conditions with rich per-recording metadata. Benchmarking leading proprietary and open-source speech LLMs shows most real-time SLLMs perform in a limited accuracy range under these wearable conditions.

entries.name: (unnamed) likelihood- and generative-based evaluation suite for spoken language models (replacement for global token perplexity)
entries.full_title: On the Fallacy of Global Token Perplexity in Spoken Language Model Evaluation
entries.summary: The paper argues that 'global token perplexity', which transplants the text perplexity formulation onto speech tokens, misjudges generative spoken language models, and proposes a variety of likelihood-based and generative-based evaluation methods in its place. The proposed measures correlate more strongly with human mean opinion scores, and re-ranking models under them reshapes the performance landscape, shrinking the apparent gap between the best model and the human topline.

entries.name: AEQ-Bench
entries.full_title: AEQ-Bench: Measuring Empathy of Omni-Modal Large Models
entries.summary: The Audio Empathy Quotient benchmark assesses two empathetic capabilities of omni-modal large models: generating empathetic responses from affective cues in audio plus text, and judging the empathy of audio responses without relying on a transcript. It adds two settings that vary context specificity and speech tone, and scores models on both linguistic and paralinguistic metrics.
entries.io: audio + text in, speech or text out
entries.note: Models with audio output generally beat text-only-output models, and OLM judges match humans on coarse quality but are unreliable on fine-grained paralinguistic expressiveness.

entries.name: AGL1K
entries.full_title: The Sonar Moment: Benchmarking Audio-Language Models in Audio Geo-Localization
entries.summary: A benchmark for audio geo-localization by audio language models: given a recording, infer its geographic origin. Clips are drawn from a crowd-sourced platform and filtered with a proposed Audio Localizability metric that quantifies how informative each recording is. The paper also analyses model reasoning traces, regional bias, error causes and the interpretability of the localizability metric.
entries.size: 1,444 curated audio clips spanning 72 countries and territories
entries.note: Across 16 ALMs, closed-source models substantially outperform open-source ones and linguistic clues often dominate as the scaffold for prediction.

entries.name: AQUA-Bench
entries.full_title: AQUA-Bench: Beyond Finding Answers to Knowing When There Are None in Audio Question Answering
entries.summary: A benchmark for Audio Question Unanswerability Assessment: whether audio-aware LLMs recognise that no reliable answer can be inferred from the audio instead of answering anyway. It covers three scenarios — Absent Answer Detection (the correct option is missing), Incompatible Answer Set Detection (choices are categorically mismatched with the question), and Incompatible Audio Question Detection (the question is irrelevant to or ungrounded in the audio).
entries.note: Models that excel on standard answerable questions face notable difficulty on unanswerable ones, exposing a blind spot in audio-language understanding.

entries.name: ART (Audio Reasoning Tasks)
entries.full_title: A Benchmark for Audio Reasoning Capabilities of Multimodal Large Language Models
entries.summary: A benchmark for multimodal large language models that requires combining audio subtasks of different categories into a single answer, rather than testing tasks such as speaker diarization or gender identification in isolation. The stated goal is to verify whether models can reason over an audio signal to answer composite questions.
entries.note: Motivated by the observation that existing audio benchmarks test isolated tasks and cannot verify cross-task reasoning.

entries.name: ChronosAudio
entries.full_title: ChronosAudio: A Comprehensive Long-Audio Benchmark for Evaluating Audio-Large Language Models
entries.summary: A multi-task benchmark for long-audio understanding by audio large language models. It spans six major task categories and stratifies instances into short, middle and long-form durations to measure length generalization.
entries.size: 36,000 test instances totalling over 200 hours of audio
entries.note: Across 16 models the paper reports long-context collapse (over 90% degradation on some tasks from short to long), attention dilution that breaks temporal locality, and mitigation strategies that recover only about 50%.

entries.name: FOCAL
entries.full_title: FOCAL: A Novel Benchmarking Technique for Multi-modal Agents
entries.summary: FOCAL is a benchmarking framework for multi-modal (voice-to-voice plus text input) agents that measures end-to-end reasoning, component-wise error propagation, and error analysis in both automated and human-assisted testing. It introduces two metrics, Reasoning and Semantic scores, to assess how well an agent holds meaningful conversations in voice mode, motivated by error propagation in cascading voice-agent pipelines.

entries.name: FutureOmni
entries.full_title: FutureOmni: Evaluating Future Forecasting from Omni-Modal Context for Multimodal LLMs
entries.summary: The first benchmark for omni-modal future forecasting from audio-visual environments, requiring cross-modal causal and temporal reasoning plus internal knowledge to predict future events. Built with a scalable LLM-assisted, human-in-the-loop pipeline, it contains 919 videos and 1,034 multiple-choice QA pairs across 8 primary domains. Evaluating 13 omni-modal and 7 video-only models shows current systems struggle, especially in speech-heavy scenarios, with a best accuracy of 64.8% (Gemini 3 Flash). The authors also release a 7K-sample instruction-tuning set and an Omni-Modal Future Forecasting (OFF) training strategy that improves forecasting and generalization.
tasks: future event forecasting from audio-visual context
entries.io: audio-visual video context plus multiple-choice question -> predicted future event
entries.size: 919 videos, 1,034 multiple-choice QA pairs across 8 domains
entries.note: Prospective rather than retrospective evaluation; 13 omni-modal and 7 video-only models compared, best 64.8%; speech-heavy scenarios are the weakest, and a 7K instruction-tuning set plus OFF training recipe is released alongside.

entries.name: HearSay
entries.full_title: HearSay Benchmark: Do Audio LLMs Leak What They Hear?
entries.summary: A benchmark testing whether audio large language models leak user privacy purely from acoustic voiceprints. Real-world clips are curated through automated profiling plus human verification so that all privacy labels are grounded in factual records; models are probed both for private-attribute inference and for whether they refuse privacy-intruding requests.
entries.note: Reports 92.89% accuracy on gender inference, near-zero refusal rates for physiological traits, and that chain-of-thought reasoning amplifies privacy leakage in capable models.

entries.name: HumDial Challenge
entries.full_title: The ICASSP 2026 HumDial Challenge: Benchmarking Human-like Spoken Dialogue Systems in the LLM Era
entries.summary: A shared-task benchmark for human-like spoken dialogue systems built on a dataset derived from authentic human conversations. It defines two tracks: Emotional Intelligence (long-term emotion understanding and empathetic generation) and Full-Duplex Interaction (real-time decision-making while listening and speaking, e.g. turn-taking). The paper summarizes the dataset, track configurations and final challenge results.
entries.note: First challenge to benchmark emotional intelligence and full-duplex interaction jointly for LLM-era spoken dialogue systems.

entries.name: LongSpeech
entries.full_title: LongSpeech: A Scalable Benchmark for Transcription, Translation and Understanding in Long Speech
entries.summary: A large-scale benchmark for evaluating speech and audio-language models on long-duration audio, targeting settings such as meeting transcription, spoken document understanding and conversational analysis. Each segment carries annotations for ASR, speech translation, summarization, language detection, speaker counting, content separation and question answering, and the authors release a reproducible pipeline for building further long-form benchmarks.
entries.size: over 100,000 speech segments of roughly 10 minutes each
entries.note: Initial experiments show models specialising in one task at the expense of others and struggling with higher-level reasoning over long audio.

entries.name: MTAVG-Bench
entries.full_title: MTAVG-Bench: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Multi-Talker Dialogue-Centric Audio-Video Generation
entries.summary: A failure-driven diagnostic benchmark for multi-talker dialogue-centric audio-video generation, built semi-automatically from 1.8k videos generated by mainstream text-to-audio-video models and 2.4k manually annotated QA pairs. It evaluates four levels — audio-visual signal fidelity, temporal attribute consistency, social interaction, and cinematic expression — and is primarily designed to test whether omni-models can reliably identify failure modes such as identity drift, unnatural turn transitions, and audio-visual misalignment.
tasks: failure-mode identification QA over generated multi-talker dialogue video

entries.name: PALM-Bench
entries.full_title: PALM-Bench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Personalized Audio-Language Models
entries.summary: A benchmark for Personalized Audio-Language Models (PALM), formalizing the task of recognizing personal concepts (e.g. which speaker is 'my best friend') and reasoning within a personal context. It provides structured evaluation on several tasks in multi-speaker scenarios, in contrast to generic spoken-content questions such as plain summarization.
entries.note: Training-free prompting and supervised fine-tuning both help but remain limited at modelling personalized knowledge and transferring it across tasks.

entries.name: Pardon? (EAR score)
entries.full_title: Pardon? Evaluating Conversational Repair in Large Audio-Language Models
entries.summary: A repair-aware evaluation setting for spoken question answering that explicitly separates answerable from unanswerable audio inputs, with paired conditions built by a semantic-acoustic masking protocol. It introduces the Evaluability Awareness and Repair (EAR) score, a non-compensatory metric that jointly rewards task competence on answerable inputs and appropriate repair behaviour (e.g. asking for clarification) on unanswerable ones.
entries.note: On two spoken QA benchmarks, models that answer accurately when inputs are answerable mostly fail to recognise semantic unanswerability and initiate repair, revealing a gap between accuracy and conversational reliability.

entries.name: PhoStream
entries.full_title: PhoStream: Benchmarking Real-World Streaming for Omnimodal Assistants in Mobile Scenarios
entries.summary: A mobile-centric streaming benchmark for omnimodal assistants that unifies on-screen and off-screen scenarios and evaluates video, audio and temporal reasoning on continuous streams. Open-ended QA pairs are produced by an automated generative pipeline with human verification, and models are run through an online inference pipeline and scored by LLM-as-a-judge, so the assistant must decide both what to say and when to say it.
entries.size: 5,572 open-ended QA pairs from 578 videos across 4 scenarios and 10 capabilities
entries.note: Shows a temporal asymmetry: models score well on Instant and Backward tasks (Gemini 3 Pro above 80) but collapse on Forward tasks (16.40) by answering before the required cues appear.

entries.name: RSA-Bench
entries.full_title: RSA-Bench: Benchmarking Audio Large Models in Real-World Acoustic Scenarios
entries.summary: A robustness benchmark that stress-tests audio large models under realistic layered acoustic environments rather than synthetic Gaussian noise or single-source interference. Evaluation samples superimpose environmental soundscapes (pasture, extreme weather, classroom, outdoors) onto clean speech at a range of interference intensities, across six core tasks from low-level perception to complex reasoning.
entries.size: six core tasks across four soundscape types
entries.note: Reports a perception-cognition gap (reasoning collapses under stress while recognition holds), vocal-like interference being more destructive than mechanical noise, and a denoising paradox where speech enhancement makes performance worse.

entries.name: SayNext-Bench
entries.full_title: SayNext-Bench: Why Do LLMs Struggle with Next-Utterance Anticipation?
entries.summary: A benchmark evaluating MLLMs on anticipating a human speaker's next utterance across diverse real-world scenarios, supported by SayNext-PC, a large-scale multimodal dialogue dataset, and a multi-level evaluation framework spanning lexical similarity, emotion-intention consistency, and LLM-based overall alignment. The paper reports that leading models struggle to anticipate forthcoming utterances that humans readily predict from multimodal cues such as gestures, gaze and emotional tone.

entries.name: SEE (Signal Embedding Energy)
entries.full_title: SEE: Signal Embedding Energy for Quantifying Noise Interference in Large Audio Language Models
entries.summary: SEE is a method for quantifying the impact of noise intensity on Large Audio Language Model inputs, enabling differentiation of LALM robustness in real-world deployments. It works from structured activation subspaces derived from the model's internal representations rather than raw audio features, correlates 0.98 with LALM performance, and shows that traditional audio denoising is only marginally effective for LALMs and can even worsen results.
tasks: noise-robustness quantification for audio LLM inputs

entries.name: SONIC-O1
entries.full_title: SONIC-O1: A Real-World Benchmark for Evaluating Multimodal Large Language Models on Audio-Video Understanding
entries.summary: SONIC-O1 is a fully human-verified benchmark of 60 hours (231 clips) of real-world conversational audio-video across 13 domains, with 4,958 annotations and demographic metadata. It evaluates three capabilities of multimodal LLMs: open-ended summarization, multiple-choice QA, and temporal localization with supporting rationales. Results show a 22.6% gap between the best closed- and open-source models on temporal localization and accuracy gaps of up to 21.4% across demographic groups.

entries.name: SonicBench
entries.full_title: SonicBench: Dissecting the Physical Perception Bottleneck in Large Audio Language Models
entries.summary: A psychophysically grounded benchmark probing whether large audio language models perceive fundamental physical attributes of sound such as pitch, loudness and spatial location. Stimuli are built with a controllable generation toolbox for two paradigms — recognition (absolute judgment) and comparison (relative judgment) — so both sensory precision and relational reasoning can be measured, complemented by linear probing of frozen audio encoders.
entries.size: 12 core physical attributes across five perceptual dimensions
entries.note: Most models are near random and, unlike humans, gain no advantage on comparison tasks, yet frozen encoders capture the physical cues (at least 60% probe accuracy), locating the bottleneck in alignment and decoding rather than sensing.

entries.name: SpeakerSleuth
entries.full_title: SpeakerSleuth: Can Large Audio-Language Models Judge Speaker Consistency across Multi-turn Dialogues?
entries.summary: A benchmark testing whether large audio-language models used as judges can assess speaker consistency across multi-turn dialogues, via three tasks reflecting real deployment needs. Instances are human-verified and drawn from four datasets covering synthetic and real speech with controlled acoustic difficulty.
entries.size: 1,818 human-verified evaluation instances across four datasets
entries.note: Across twelve LALMs, judgments degrade sharply when other interlocutors' turns are supplied as text — models prioritise textual coherence over acoustics and miss even obvious gender switches — while ranking acoustic variants remains comparatively strong.

entries.name: SYAUDIO
entries.full_title: Hearing is Believing? Evaluating and Analyzing Audio Language Model Sycophancy with SYAUDIO
entries.summary: A benchmark for sycophancy in audio language models — the tendency to agree with a user's assertion even when it contradicts the acoustic evidence. Questions are built on established audio benchmarks and augmented with TTS-generated arithmetic and moral reasoning items, spanning Audio Perception, Audio Reasoning, Audio Math and Audio Ethics, with additional analysis under noise and varied speech rate.
entries.note: First benchmark dedicated to sycophancy in the audio modality; supervised fine-tuning with chain-of-thought data is shown to reduce it.

entries.name: TRACE (with HCoT annotations)
entries.full_title: Hearing Between the Lines: Unlocking the Reasoning Power of LLMs for Speech Evaluation
entries.summary: TRACE (Textual Reasoning over Audio Cues for Evaluation) is an evaluation framework that lets text LLM judges reason over cheap audio-derived signals to score speech-to-speech systems, as an alternative to opaque and expensive audio-LM judges. It introduces a Human Chain-of-Thought annotation protocol that splits judgments into content, voice quality, and paralinguistics dimensions, and fuses dimension-wise ratings into an overall score, reporting higher agreement with human raters than ALM and transcript-only LLM judges.

entries.name: UltraEval-Audio
entries.full_title: UltraEval-Audio: A Unified Framework for Comprehensive Evaluation of Audio Foundation Models
entries.summary: A unified, modular evaluation framework for audio foundation models covering both understanding and generation, with one-command evaluation and public leaderboards. It adds a holistic audio-codec evaluation scheme (semantic accuracy, timbre fidelity, acoustic quality) and introduces two new Chinese spoken benchmarks, SpeechCMMLU (Chinese knowledge proficiency) and SpeechHSK (Chinese language fluency), to counter the English bias of existing speech benchmarks.
entries.io: audio in, text or speech out
entries.size: 14 core task categories, 36 integrated benchmarks, 24 integrated models
entries.note: Bundles scattered datasets and code into one harness with live leaderboards, and targets the lack of Chinese-language spoken evaluation.

entries.name: VoxPrivacy
entries.full_title: VoxPrivacy: A Benchmark for Evaluating Interactional Privacy of Speech Language Models
entries.summary: A benchmark for what the authors call interactional privacy: whether a speech language model in a shared, multi-user setting distinguishes speakers and adapts what it discloses to whom. It spans three tiers of difficulty, from following direct secrecy commands to proactively inferring what should stay private, and is validated on Real-VoxPrivacy, a human-recorded subset.
entries.size: 32-hour bilingual evaluation set, plus a released 4,000-hour training set
entries.note: Across nine SLMs most open-source models sit near chance (~50%) on conditional privacy decisions and even strong closed-source systems fall short on proactive privacy inference; fine-tuning on the released training set improves privacy behaviour.

entries.name: ALLM Fairness, Safety and Security Evaluation
entries.full_title: Evaluation of Audio Language Models for Fairness, Safety, and Security
entries.summary: A structure-aware evaluation framework for fairness, safety and security of audio large language models. It first proposes a taxonomy along two axes — the form of audio input representation (discrete vs continuous) and the locus of semantic reasoning (cascaded, multimodal, or audio-native) — then assesses semantic invariance under paralinguistic variation, refusal and toxicity behaviour on unsafe prompts, and robustness to adversarial audio perturbations.
entries.note: Applied to two representative systems, it finds systematic audio-versus-text gaps in refusal, attack success and toxicity, arguing FSS behaviour is tied to how acoustic information enters semantic reasoning.

entries.name: ALME
entries.full_title: When Audio-LLMs Don't Listen: A Cross-Linguistic Study of Modality Arbitration
