entries.summary: ALME is a dataset of controlled stimuli in which the audio and an accompanying text disagree, paired with the Text Dominance Ratio metric that counts how often a model follows the conflicting text despite being instructed to trust the audio. A matched control replaces the audio with its transcript under otherwise identical conditions, isolating modality arbitration from information content; four audio-LLMs are compared across eight languages.
entries.io: conflicting audio and text in, text out
entries.note: Gemini 2.0 Flash and GPT-4o show TDR 10-26x higher than the transcript-substituted baseline, and framing the transcript as deliberately corrupted cuts TDR by 80%.

entries.name: AudioCapBench
entries.full_title: AudioCapBench: Quick Evaluation on Audio Captioning across Sound, Music, and Speech
entries.summary: A compact audio-captioning benchmark drawn from established datasets covering environmental sound, music and speech. Predictions are scored both with reference-based metrics and an LLM-as-Judge that rates accuracy, completeness and hallucination separately; 13 models from two providers are evaluated.
entries.note: All models caption speech best and music worst; Gemini scores highest overall while OpenAI models hallucinate less.

entries.name: AudioRAG
entries.full_title: AudioRAG: A Challenging Benchmark for Audio Reasoning and Information Retrieval
entries.summary: A benchmark for audio reasoning that requires grounding in externally retrieved information rather than only the model's internal knowledge, using LLM-generated and manually curated question-answer pairs set in realistic web environments. The authors also provide an agentic pipeline combining audio reasoning with retrieval-augmented generation as a stronger baseline.
entries.note: State-of-the-art LALMs struggle on questions that need external information grounding.

entries.name: BASS
entries.full_title: BASS: Benchmarking Audio LMs for Musical Structure and Semantic Reasoning
entries.summary: BASS evaluates music understanding and reasoning in audio language models across four categories: structural segmentation, lyric transcription, musicological analysis and artist collaboration. It spans 12 tasks over nearly 2,000 songs from a wide range of genres, and 14 open-source and frontier multimodal LMs are evaluated.
entries.size: 2,658 questions over 12 tasks, 1,993 unique songs, 138+ hours of music
entries.note: Models do best on lyric transcription and worst on higher-level reasoning such as structural segmentation and artist collaboration, indicating reliance on linguistic priors over musical structure.

entries.name: BiasInEar
entries.full_title: Bias in the Ear of the Listener: Assessing Sensitivity in Audio Language Models Across Linguistic, Demographic, and Positional Variations
entries.summary: A speech-augmented benchmark built on Global MMLU Lite that re-renders multiple-choice questions as audio in English, Chinese and Korean, balanced by gender and accent. Nine multimodal LLMs are evaluated under linguistic (language, accent), demographic (gender) and structural (option order) perturbations using accuracy, entropy, APES and Fleiss' kappa, to measure fairness and robustness of speech-integrated LLMs.
entries.note: Models are relatively robust to demographic factors but highly sensitive to language and option order, suggesting speech amplifies existing structural biases.
aka: Bias in the Ear of the Listener

entries.name: Cascade Equivalence Hypothesis (matched-backbone testing)
entries.full_title: The Cascade Equivalence Hypothesis: When Do Speech LLMs Behave Like ASR$\rightarrow$LLM Pipelines?
entries.summary: An evaluation methodology, matched-backbone testing, that separates a speech LLM's audio pathway from the reasoning ability of its underlying text LLM so speech LLMs can be compared fairly against ASR-then-LLM cascades. It is combined with a mechanistic analysis (logit lens, LEACE) showing the literal transcript emerging in hidden states and text representations being causally necessary.
entries.note: Argues most deployed speech LLMs behave as expensive cascades, with clean-condition advantages reversing by up to 7.6% at 0dB SNR.

entries.name: Interspeech 2026 Audio Reasoning Challenge (MMAR-Rubrics)
entries.full_title: The Interspeech 2026 Audio Reasoning Challenge: Evaluating Reasoning Process Quality for Audio Reasoning Models and Agents
entries.summary: A shared task evaluating the quality of the reasoning process, not just the final answer, for audio reasoning models and agents. It introduces MMAR-Rubrics, an instance-level protocol that scores the factuality and logic of chain-of-thought traces, and runs Single Model and Agent tracks.
entries.size: 156 participating teams from 18 countries and regions; two tracks
entries.note: Agent systems currently lead on reasoning quality through iterative tool orchestration and cross-modal analysis, while single models advance rapidly via reinforcement learning and data pipelines.

entries.name: LALM-as-a-Judge
entries.full_title: LALM-as-a-Judge: Benchmarking Large Audio-Language Models for Safety Evaluation in Multi-Turn Spoken Dialogues
entries.summary: An open benchmark of multi-turn spoken dialogues, each containing one localized socially unsafe turn drawn from eight categories and five severity levels, used to test large audio-language models acting as safety judges. Six open and closed models are run in text-only, audio-only and multimodal settings and scored on sensitivity, severity-order specificity and turn-position bias.
tasks: text-only vs audio-only vs multimodal comparison
entries.io: multi-turn spoken dialogue in, judgement text out
entries.size: 24,000 multi-turn spoken dialogues, 8 unsafe categories, 5 severity levels
entries.note: Audio supplies non-lexical evidence beyond transcript semantics, but multimodal gains are not universal and can be text-anchored, conservative or interfering.

entries.name: RA-QA
entries.full_title: RA-QA: A Benchmarking System for Respiratory Audio Question Answering Under Real-World Heterogeneity
entries.summary: A Respiratory-Audio Question-Answering benchmark with a standardized data generation pipeline, a multimodal QA collection, and a unified evaluation protocol, harmonizing public respiratory-audio datasets into 9 million format-diverse QA pairs covering diagnostic and contextual attributes. It benchmarks general audio-language models alongside domain-specific architectures and shows how current approaches fail under real-world heterogeneity across modalities, devices, and question types.

entries.name: UNICBench
entries.full_title: UNICBench: UNIfied Counting Benchmark for MLLM
entries.summary: A unified multimodal, multi-level counting benchmark and evaluation toolkit spanning image, text and audio, comprising 5,300 images (5,508 QA), 872 documents (5,888 QA) and 2,069 audio clips (2,905 QA) with a three-level capability taxonomy and difficulty tags. Under a standardized protocol with fixed splits, prompts and seeds, 45 state-of-the-art MLLMs are evaluated, showing large gaps on reasoning and the hardest partitions.
entries.size: 2,069 audio clips / 2,905 audio QA (plus image and document splits)

entries.name: Voices of Civilizations
entries.full_title: Voices of Civilizations: A Multilingual QA Benchmark for Global Music Understanding
entries.summary: Voices of Civilizations is a multilingual QA benchmark for evaluating audio LLMs' cultural comprehension of full-length music recordings, covering 380 tracks across 38 languages with 1,190 multiple-choice questions produced by a four-stage automated pipeline with manual verification at each stage. Questions probe language, region associations, mood, and thematic content; models are evaluated under four conditions with per-language accuracy reported, showing that even state-of-the-art audio LLMs miss cultural nuance without rich textual context and show systematic biases across traditions.
tasks: language and region identification from audio

entries.name: WavBench
entries.full_title: WavBench: Benchmarking Reasoning, Colloquialism, and Paralinguistics for End-to-End Spoken Dialogue Models
entries.summary: A benchmark for end-to-end spoken dialogue models organised into three subsets: a Pro subset of harder items for reasoning-enhanced models, a Basic subset defining a standard for spoken colloquialism that prioritises listenability (natural vocabulary, fluency, interactive rapport) over written accuracy, and an Acoustic subset covering explicit paralinguistic understanding, paralinguistic generation and implicit dialogue.
entries.note: Argues that current evaluations apply text-generation standards to speech and therefore miss colloquialism and paralinguistics; five state-of-the-art models are evaluated.

entries.name: (unnamed) blind-baseline membership-inference auditing protocol for LALMs
entries.full_title: Membership Inference Attacks against Large Audio Language Models
entries.summary: The first systematic membership inference attack evaluation of large audio language models. Using multi-modal blind baselines from textual, spectral and prosodic features, the paper shows common audio datasets are almost perfectly train/test separable without any model inference, then introduces a blind-baseline protocol and distribution-matched datasets that allow reliable MIA evaluation, finding LALM memorization to be cross-modal — arising from binding a speaker's vocal identity to its text.

entries.name: AHA-Eval
entries.full_title: Audio Hallucination Attacks: Probing the Reliability of Large Audio Language Models
entries.summary: An attack suite of 6.5K QA pairs that tests whether large audio-language models actually ground answers in the audio, using two attack surfaces: query-based attacks that exploit question structure to induce hallucination of absent sounds, and audio-based attacks that inject synthetic speech describing non-existent events into the audio stream. A companion 120K-QA post-alignment dataset, AHA-Guard, is proposed as mitigation.
entries.note: Attack success rates of 95.35% on Audio Flamingo 3 and 79.65% on Gemini 3 Pro reveal a reliability gap hidden by standard benchmark scores; AHA-Guard cuts attack success by up to 49%.

entries.name: AKB-2000
entries.full_title: How Auditory Knowledge in LLM Backbones Shapes Audio Language Models: A Holistic Evaluation
entries.summary: A curated benchmark probing the breadth and depth of auditory knowledge encoded in LLM backbones through text-only pre-training, used in a three-setting comparison: direct text probing on AKB-2000, cascade evaluation where the LLM reasons over an audio captioner's text descriptions, and audio-grounded evaluation where each LLM is fine-tuned into a LALM with an audio encoder.
entries.io: text in, text out for probing; audio in, text out for the audio-grounded setting
entries.note: Auditory knowledge varies substantially across LLM families and text-only probe results correlate strongly with downstream audio performance.

entries.name: ALICE
entries.full_title: ALICE: A Multifaceted Evaluation Framework of Large Audio-Language Models' In-Context Learning Ability
entries.summary: ALICE is a three-stage evaluation framework that progressively strips away textual task guidance in order to test whether large audio-language models can infer a task from in-context audio examples. Six LALMs are evaluated on four audio understanding tasks under two categories of output constraint.
entries.note: In-context demonstrations reliably improve format compliance but fail to improve, and often degrade, core task performance.

entries.name: APUN-Bench
entries.full_title: Words at Play: Benchmarking Audio Pun Understanding in Large Audio-Language Models
entries.summary: APUN-Bench is the first benchmark dedicated to spoken pun understanding in large audio-language models, with audio samples annotated in three stages: recognizing that a pun is present, locating the pun word, and inferring its meaning. Ten state-of-the-art LALMs are evaluated.
entries.note: Substantial gaps in all three stages, including positional bias when locating the pun word and systematic errors in meaning inference.

entries.name: DEAF
entries.full_title: DEAF: A Benchmark for Diagnostic Evaluation of Acoustic Faithfulness in Audio Language Models
entries.summary: DEAF pits acoustic evidence against textual evidence across three dimensions - emotional prosody, background sounds and speaker identity - to test whether audio multimodal LLMs actually process the acoustic signal or infer answers from text semantics. A multi-level protocol escalates textual influence from in-content semantic conflict to misleading prompts and their combination, separating content-driven bias from prompt-induced sycophancy, with diagnostic metrics quantifying reliance on text.
entries.note: Across seven audio MLLMs, predictions are predominantly text-driven despite measurable sensitivity to acoustic variation, exposing a gap between standard benchmark scores and genuine acoustic understanding.

entries.name: DoWhatISay (DOWIS)
entries.full_title: Do What I Say: A Spoken Prompt Dataset for Instruction-Following
entries.summary: A multilingual dataset of human-recorded spoken prompts paired with written equivalents, designed to be attached to any existing benchmark so speech LLMs can be evaluated under spoken rather than typed instruction conditions. It spans 9 tasks and 11 languages with 10 prompt variants per task-language pair across five styles, allowing analysis of the interplay between prompt modality, style, language and task type.
entries.io: speech in, text out (speech out for speech-output tasks)
entries.size: 9 tasks x 11 languages, 10 prompt variants per pair across five styles
entries.note: Text prompts consistently outperform spoken prompts, especially for low-resource and cross-lingual settings; only tasks with speech output close the gap.

entries.name: EcoG-Bench
entries.full_title: Listening with the Eyes: Benchmarking Egocentric Co-Speech Grounding across Space and Time
entries.summary: EcoG-Bench is an evaluation-only bilingual (EN/ZH) diagnostic benchmark of 811 egocentric clips with dense spatial annotations and millisecond-level co-speech pointing-stroke supervision, requiring a model to jointly predict What, Where, and When for underspecified deictic commands. Under its Progressive Cognitive Evaluation protocol, humans reach 96.9% strict Eco-Accuracy while the best native video-audio model setting (Gemini-3-Pro) reaches 17.0%, exposing a severe executability gap.

entries.name: ERM-MinMaxGAP
entries.full_title: ERM-MinMaxGAP: Benchmarking and Mitigating Gender Bias in Multilingual Multimodal Speech-LLM Emotion Recognition
entries.summary: A multilingual, multimodal speech-emotion-recognition benchmark built on MELD-ST covering English, Japanese and German, used to quantify language-specific SER performance and male-female performance gaps in speech LLMs. The paper also proposes ERM-MinMaxGAP, a fairness-informed training objective adding an adaptive fairness weight and a regularizer on the maximum male-female loss gap within each language and modality.
entries.note: Bias is strongly language-dependent and multimodal fusion does not reliably improve fairness; the proposed objective improves SER by ~5% while shrinking the gender gap only slightly.

entries.name: EscapeCraft-4D
entries.full_title: Evaluating Time Awareness and Cross-modal Active Perception of Large Models via 4D Escape Room Task
entries.summary: EscapeCraft-4D is a customizable 4D escape-room environment plus curated benchmark for assessing selective cross-modal perception and time awareness in Omni models. It incorporates trigger-based auditory sources, temporally transient evidence, and location-dependent cues, requiring agents to perform spatio-temporal reasoning and proactive multimodal integration under time constraints; evaluation indicates models struggle with modality coordination.

entries.name: HumMusQA
entries.full_title: HumMusQA: A Human-written Music Understanding QA Benchmark Dataset
entries.summary: A human-written music understanding QA benchmark of 320 hand-written questions curated and validated by experts with musical training, arguing manual curation better probes complex audio comprehension. Six state-of-the-art LALMs are benchmarked and additionally tested for robustness to uni-modal shortcuts.
entries.venue: Proceedings of the 4th Workshop on NLP for Music and Audio (NLP4MusA 2026), pages 58-67, R

entries.name: Interspeech 2026 Audio Encoder Capability Challenge (XARES-LLM)
entries.full_title: The Interspeech 2026 Audio Encoder Capability Challenge for Large Audio Language Models
entries.summary: A shared-task benchmark that evaluates pre-trained audio encoders in their role as front-end modules for large audio-language models. The XARES-LLM framework provides a unified generative evaluation over a diverse suite of downstream classification and generation tasks, decoupling encoder development from LLM fine-tuning to give a standardized protocol for general-purpose audio representations.
entries.note: Targets the integration gap between encoder representation quality and downstream LALM performance.

entries.name: KoALa-Bench
entries.full_title: KoALa-Bench: Evaluating Large Audio Language Models on Korean Speech Understanding and Faithfulness
entries.summary: A Korean benchmark for large audio-language models with six tasks: four covering fundamental speech understanding (ASR, speech translation, speech QA, speech instruction following) and two designed to probe speech faithfulness, motivated by the observation that several LALMs fail to fully use the speech modality. Content includes listening questions from the Korean college scholastic ability test and Korean cultural domains; six white-box and black-box models are evaluated with a public leaderboard.
entries.note: Adds explicit faithfulness tasks that test whether the model actually uses the audio rather than answering from text priors.

entries.name: LVOmniBench
entries.full_title: LVOmniBench: Pioneering Long Audio-Video Understanding Evaluation for Omnimodal LLMs
entries.summary: A benchmark for cross-modal comprehension of long-form audio and video, comprising 275 manually selected and annotated videos of 10 to 90 minutes with 1,014 question-answer pairs. It probes long-term memory, temporal localization, fine-grained understanding, and multimodal perception, with open-source omnimodal LLMs generally scoring below 35%.

entries.name: MMOU
entries.full_title: MMOU: A Massive Multi-Task Omni Understanding and Reasoning Benchmark for Long and Complex Real-World Videos
entries.summary: MMOU is a massive multi-task benchmark of 20,000 manually annotated questions over 11,877 web-collected videos of varying length, designed to test joint reasoning over omni-modal (visual, audio, textual) signals in long and complex real-world videos. It covers 13 skill categories that all require integrating evidence across modalities and time; the best closed-source model reaches only 64.2% accuracy and the strongest open-source model 46.8%.

entries.name: MUGEN
entries.full_title: MUGEN: Evaluating and Improving Multi-audio Understanding of Large Audio-Language Models
entries.summary: MUGEN evaluates whether large audio-language models can reason across several audio inputs at once, covering speech, general audio and music. Beyond the benchmark, the paper tests training-free mitigations, notably Audio-Permutational Self-Consistency, which shuffles the order of candidate audios before aggregating predictions.
entries.io: multiple audio clips in, text out
entries.note: Performance degrades sharply as the number of concurrent audio inputs grows, identifying input scaling as a bottleneck; permutation self-consistency gains up to 6.28% accuracy, 6.74% combined with chain-of-thought.

entries.name: Multi-Event Audio Grounding Sensitivity Analysis
entries.full_title: A Sensitivity Analysis of Multi-Event Audio Grounding in Audio LLMs
entries.summary: A large-scale evaluation of event grounding and false alarms in audio LLMs as auditory scene complexity increases. Normalized (source, attribute) events are extracted from 71K AudioCapsV2 clips and turned into present-event queries for ground-truth detection and absent-event queries (via similarity-filtered negative sampling in an audio-aligned text embedding space) to probe hallucination. Four audio LLMs are tested with 12 prompt variants over 500K yes/no queries each.
entries.size: 71K AudioCapsV2 clips; 500K yes/no queries per model; 12 prompt variants
entries.note: Increasing event count consistently lowers true-positive rate and raises false-positive rate, prompts induce a strong trade-off between the two, and models become more uncertain on multi-event audio.

entries.name: MUSE (Multimodal Unified Safety Evaluation)
entries.full_title: MUSE: A Run-Centric Platform for Multimodal Unified Safety Evaluation of Large Language Models
entries.summary: MUSE is an open-source, run-centric platform for safety evaluation and red-teaming of large language models across audio, image, and video inputs, integrating automatic cross-modal payload generation, three multi-turn attack algorithms, provider-agnostic model routing, and an LLM judge with a five-level safety taxonomy. A dual-metric framework separates hard from soft attack success rate, and Inter-Turn Modality Switching augments multi-turn attacks with per-turn modality rotation. Experiments across six multimodal LLMs from four providers show multi-turn strategies reaching up to 90-100% ASR against models with near-perfect single-turn refusal.
entries.size: six multimodal LLMs from four providers; three attack algorithms

entries.name: OMD-Bench
entries.full_title: Omni-Modal Dissonance Benchmark: Systematically Breaking Modality Consensus to Probe Robustness and Calibrated Abstention
entries.summary: An omni-modal benchmark that begins with congruent modalities - each presenting the same anchor object or event independently perceivable through video, audio and text - and then systematically corrupts them to isolate each modality's true contribution rather than confounding reliance with information asymmetry. It also evaluates calibrated abstention: whether models refrain from answering when evidence conflicts. It comprises 4,080 instances spanning 27 anchors across eight corruption conditions.
entries.io: video + audio + text in, text out
entries.note: Ten omni-modal models over-abstain when two modalities are corrupted yet severely under-abstain when all three are, staying ~60-100% confident under full corruption; chain-of-thought improves abstention alignment but amplifies overconfidence.

entries.name: OmniACBench
entries.full_title: OmniACBench: A Benchmark for Evaluating Context-Grounded Acoustic Control in Omni-Modal Models
entries.summary: OmniACBench tests context-grounded acoustic control: given a spoken instruction, a text script and an image, a model must read the script aloud with the tone and manner appropriate to that multimodal context. Instances cover six acoustic features - speech rate, phonation, pronunciation, emotion, global accent and timbre - and eight omni-modal models are evaluated on their spoken, not textual, output.
entries.io: spoken instruction + text script + image in, speech out
entries.note: The bottleneck is integrating multimodal context for faithful speech generation rather than processing individual modalities; three failure modes are identified (weak direct control, failed implicit inference, failed multimodal grounding).

entries.name: PARSA-Bench
entries.full_title: PARSA-Bench: A Comprehensive Persian Audio-Language Model Benchmark
entries.summary: The first benchmark for evaluating large audio-language models on Persian language and culture, spanning speech understanding, paralinguistic analysis and culturally grounded audio understanding. Ten of the sixteen tasks are new, including poetry meter and style detection, traditional Persian music understanding and code-switching detection.
entries.io: speech and music audio in, text out
entries.note: Text-only baselines consistently beat their audio counterparts, and all models sit near chance on vazn (poetic meter) detection regardless of scale.

entries.name: PolyBench
entries.full_title: PolyBench: A Benchmark for Compositional Reasoning in Polyphonic Audio
entries.summary: A benchmark for compositional reasoning over polyphonic audio, where multiple sound events co-occur and induce compositional structure. It has five evaluation subsets - counting, classification, detection, concurrency and duration estimation - all requiring reasoning over multiple concurrent events and their relations.
entries.note: State-of-the-art LALMs degrade consistently in polyphonic settings, indicating a fundamental bottleneck.

entries.name: SCENEBench
entries.full_title: SCENEBench: An Audio Understanding Benchmark Grounded in Assistive and Industrial Use Cases
entries.summary: SCENEBench (Spatial, Cross-lingual, Environmental, Non-speech Evaluation) measures audio comprehension beyond ASR across four categories chosen from understudied accessibility-technology and industrial noise-monitoring needs: background sound understanding, noise localization, cross-linguistic speech understanding and vocal characterizer recognition. Items are synthetically constructed (e.g. by overlaying natural samples) and validated against 20 natural audio items per task for ecological validity; both accuracy and model latency are reported for five LALMs.
entries.note: Performance varies widely across tasks, with some falling below random chance.

entries.name: SDiaReward / ESDR-Bench
entries.full_title: SDiaReward: Modeling and Benchmarking Spoken Dialogue Rewards with Modality and Colloquialness
entries.summary: An end-to-end multi-turn reward model for spoken dialogue that operates directly on full multi-turn speech episodes, trained with pairwise preference supervision on episode-level preference pairs that target the modality gap (prosody, emotion) and the colloquialness gap (written script vs natural speech). The paper additionally establishes ESDR-Bench, a stratified benchmark for episode-level evaluation of such spoken-dialogue evaluators.
entries.io: multi-turn speech in, preference score out
entries.note: The dedicated reward model significantly outperforms general-purpose audio LLMs at judging spoken dialogue, capturing relative conversational expressiveness beyond superficial synthesis cues.

entries.name: SID-Bench
entries.full_title: Semantic-Aware Interruption Detection in Spoken Dialogue Systems: Benchmark, Metric, and Model
entries.summary: SID-Bench is a benchmark for semantic-aware interruption detection in full-duplex spoken dialogue systems, built entirely from real human dialogues, and paired with Average Penalty Time, a metric that assigns a temporal cost to both false alarms and late responses so the responsiveness-robustness trade-off can be scored jointly. The paper also contributes an LLM-based detection model trained under a new paradigm.
entries.io: streaming speech in, interruption decision out
entries.note: Targets the gap between trigger-happy VAD methods that misfire on backchannels and end-to-end models that respond too slowly; the proposed model cuts APT roughly threefold over baselines.

entries.name: SocialOmni
entries.full_title: SocialOmni: Benchmarking Audio-Visual Social Interactivity in Omni Models
entries.summary: A benchmark operationalizing conversational social interactivity for omni-modal LLMs along three dimensions: speaker separation and identification (who is speaking), interruption timing control (when to interject) and natural interruption generation (how to phrase the interruption). It provides 2,000 perception samples plus a quality-controlled diagnostic set of 209 interaction-generation instances with strict temporal and contextual constraints, complemented by controlled audio-visual inconsistency scenarios for robustness.
entries.note: Across 12 leading omni-modal LLMs, perceptual accuracy is pronouncedly decoupled from the ability to generate contextually appropriate interruptions.

entries.name: SpokenElyza
entries.full_title: Speech-Worthy Alignment for Japanese SpeechLLMs via Direct Preference Optimization
entries.summary: A Japanese benchmark for 'speech-worthiness' - whether a SpeechLLM response is concise, conversational and readily synthesized as natural speech rather than written-register text - derived from ELYZA-tasks-100 with auditory verification by native experts. It accompanies a direct-preference-optimization alignment method for adapting Japanese SpeechLLMs to speech-worthy output.
entries.io: speech in, text out (judged for suitability to be spoken)
entries.note: Japanese spoken and written registers differ substantially in politeness markers, sentence-final particles and syntactic complexity, so ASR-encoder + text-LLM SpeechLLMs inherit unsuitable written-style output.

entries.name: StyleBench
entries.full_title: StyleBench: Evaluating Speech Language Models on Conversational Speaking Style Control
entries.summary: A multi-turn dialogue benchmark that quantifies how well speech language models interpret and control speaking-style intensity from user prompts, along four dimensions: emotion, speed, volume and pitch. Results compare leading speech LMs against omni language models.
entries.note: Reveals performance gaps between speech LMs and omni language models on style-intensity control.

entries.name: tau-Voice
entries.full_title: $τ$-Voice: Benchmarking Full-Duplex Voice Agents on Real-World Domains
entries.summary: A benchmark that extends tau^2-bench into the voice setting, requiring full-duplex agents to complete verifiable grounded tasks through multi-turn conversation while following domain policies and interacting with an environment. A controllable LLM-driven voice user simulator supplies diverse accents, realistic acoustic environments and rich turn-taking dynamics, and decouples simulation from wall-clock time so the strongest LLM can drive the user side; the identical text tasks allow direct voice-vs-text comparison.
entries.note: Voice agents reach only 31-51% pass@1 under clean conditions and 26-38% under noise and accent variation, versus 85% for GPT-5 (reasoning) on text, retaining just 30-45% of text capability.

entries.name: VoxEmo
entries.full_title: VoxEmo: Benchmarking Speech Emotion Recognition with Speech LLMs
entries.summary: VoxEmo is a speech emotion recognition benchmark built for speech LLMs used through generative interfaces, aggregating many emotion corpora across multiple languages. It provides a standardized toolkit with prompts of varying complexity, from direct classification to paralinguistic reasoning, plus a distribution-aware soft-label protocol and a prompt-ensemble strategy that emulates annotator disagreement, addressing zero-shot prompt stochasticity and the ambiguity of human emotion.
entries.note: Zero-shot speech LLMs trail supervised baselines on hard-label accuracy yet uniquely align with human subjective label distributions.

entries.name: Audio2Tool
entries.full_title: Audio2Tool: Speak, Call, Act -- A Dataset for Benchmarking Speech Tool Use
entries.summary: A dataset of roughly 30,000 spoken queries for evaluating tool-calling by speech language models across Smart Car, Smart Home and Wearables domains. Items are arranged in a multi-tier complexity hierarchy from simple direct commands to multi-intent and needle-in-a-haystack extraction, and audio is produced with zero-shot voice-cloning TTS plus varied noise profiles to approximate in-the-wild conditions. Both end-to-end SpeechLMs and ASR-LLM cascades are evaluated.
entries.note: models handle simple commands well but degrade sharply under compositional queries and acoustic noise

entries.name: AudioSafetyBench
entries.full_title: AudioGuard: Toward Comprehensive Audio Safety Protection Across Diverse Threat Models
entries.summary: A policy-grounded audio safety benchmark built from large-scale red teaming of audio systems, organised by an audio risk taxonomy. It covers audio-native harmful sound events, speaker attributes such as child voice, impersonation and voice-cloning misuse, and compositional voice-plus-content harms, and spans multiple languages and suspicious voice identities. The same paper proposes the AudioGuard guardrail (SoundGuard for waveform-level detection, ContentGuard for policy-grounded semantic checks) evaluated on this benchmark plus four others.
entries.note: argues audio risk is not just "unsafe text spoken aloud" and grounds the benchmark in a policy-based risk taxonomy

entries.name: AVID
entries.full_title: AVID: A Benchmark for Omni-Modal Audio-Visual Inconsistency Understanding via Agent-Driven Construction
entries.summary: AVID is a large-scale benchmark for audio-visual inconsistency understanding in long videos, built with an agent-driven pipeline that segments videos into Active Speaker, Voiceover, and Scenic categories and injects cross-modal conflicts via five specialized injectors. It contains 11.2K long videos (avg 235.5s) with 39.4K annotated inconsistency events and 78.7K segment clips, supporting detection, temporal grounding, classification, and reasoning over 8 inconsistency categories. Evaluations of state-of-the-art omni-models reveal significant limitations in perceiving cross-modal conflicts.
entries.size: 11.2K long videos (avg 235.5s), 39.4K inconsistency events, 78.7K segment clips

entries.name: DialBGM
entries.full_title: DialBGM: A Benchmark for Background Music Recommendation from Everyday Multi-Turn Dialogues
entries.summary: A benchmark for dialogue-conditioned background music recommendation: 1,200 open-domain daily dialogues, each paired with four candidate music clips and human preference rankings based on contextual relevance, non-intrusiveness and consistency. A wide range of open-source and proprietary models, including audio-language models and multimodal LLMs, fall far short of human judgments, with no model exceeding 35% Hit@1.

entries.name: EchoChain
entries.full_title: EchoChain: A Full-Duplex Benchmark for State-Update Reasoning Under Interruptions
entries.summary: A controlled full-duplex benchmark for state-update reasoning when users interrupt mid-response. It generates scenario-driven conversations and injects interruptions at a standardized point relative to assistant speech onset, enabling controlled cross-model comparison, and identifies three recurring post-interruption failure patterns: contextual inertia, interruption amnesia and objective displacement.
entries.note: A paired half-duplex control drops total failures by 40.2% relative to interrupted runs, and no evaluated real-time voice model exceeds a 50% pass rate.

entries.name: Full-Duplex-Bench-v3 (FDB-v3)
entries.full_title: Full-Duplex-Bench-v3: Benchmarking Tool Use for Full-Duplex Voice Agents Under Real-World Disfluency
entries.summary: A benchmark for spoken language models under naturalistic speech conditions and multi-step tool use, built entirely from real human audio annotated for five disfluency categories and paired with scenarios requiring chained API calls across four task domains. Six configurations - GPT-Realtime, Gemini Live 2.5, Gemini Live 3.1, Grok, Ultravox v0.7 and a Whisper to GPT-4o to TTS cascade - are scored on accuracy, latency and turn-taking.
entries.io: speech in, speech out plus tool/function calls
entries.size: real human audio with five disfluency categories across four task domains
entries.note: GPT-Realtime leads Pass@1 (0.600) and interruption avoidance (13.5%), Gemini Live 3.1 is fastest (4.25 s) but lowest turn-take rate (78.0%), and the cascade has a perfect turn-take rate with the worst latency (10.12 s); self-correction handling remains a universal failure mode.

entries.name: HalluAudio
entries.full_title: HalluAudio: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Hallucination Detection in Large Audio-Language Models
entries.summary: A large-scale benchmark for evaluating hallucination in large audio-language models across speech, environmental sound and music, with over 5K human-verified QA pairs spanning binary judgments, multi-choice reasoning, attribute verification and open-ended QA. Adversarial prompts and mixed-audio conditions are designed to systematically induce hallucination, and the protocol reports hallucination rate, yes/no bias, error-type analysis and refusal rate beyond plain accuracy.
entries.note: First large-scale hallucination comparison spanning speech, sound and music; reveals deficits in acoustic grounding, temporal reasoning and music attribute understanding.

entries.name: HUMANS
entries.full_title: Putting HUMANS first: Efficient LAM Evaluation with Human Preference Alignment
entries.summary: A study of whether small curated subsets can stand in for full large-audio-model benchmarks, analysing 10 subset-selection methods over 18 audio models and 40 tasks covering major LAM evaluation dimensions. Subsets of 50 examples reach over 0.93 Pearson correlation with full benchmark scores, while both subsets and the full benchmark correlate only about 0.85 with 776 human preference ratings collected from realistic voice assistant conversations. Regression models trained on the selected subsets reach 0.98 correlation with human preference and are released as the HUMANS benchmark.
entries.size: 50-example subsets (0.3% of data); 40 tasks; 776 human preference ratings
entries.note: well-curated 50-example subsets predict human preference better than the full benchmark does

entries.name: HumDial-EIBench
entries.full_title: HumDial-EIBench: A Human-Recorded Multi-Turn Emotional Intelligence Benchmark for Audio Language Models
entries.summary: A multi-turn emotional-intelligence benchmark for audio language models built on real recorded human dialogues from the ICASSP 2026 HumDial Challenge rather than synthesized speech. Emotional tracking and causal reasoning are reformulated as multiple-choice questions with adversarial distractors to reduce subjective scoring bias, while empathetic response generation is retained and an acoustic-semantic conflict task tests robustness to contradictory multimodal signals.
entries.note: Across eight ALMs, multi-turn emotional tracking and implicit causal reasoning are weak, textual and acoustic empathy are decoupled, and cross-modal conflicts expose a severe text-dominance bias.

entries.name: HumDial-FDBench
entries.full_title: Full-Duplex Interaction in Spoken Dialogue Systems: A Comprehensive Study from the ICASSP 2026 HumDial Challenge
entries.summary: A benchmark for full-duplex spoken dialogue systems built from the Full-Duplex Interaction Track of the ICASSP 2026 HumDial Challenge, released with a high-quality dual-channel dataset of real human-recorded conversations capturing interruptions, overlapping speech and feedback mechanisms. It assesses whether a system handles interruptions while maintaining conversational flow, and is accompanied by a public leaderboard comparing open-source and proprietary models.
entries.note: Provides a dual-channel corpus of genuine human overlapping conversation plus a public leaderboard for reproducible full-duplex comparison.

entries.name: Jamendo-MT-QA
entries.full_title: Jamendo-MT-QA: A Benchmark for Multi-Track Comparative Music Question Answering
entries.summary: A dataset and benchmark for multi-track comparative music question answering, with 36,519 comparative QA items over 12,173 Creative Commons track pairs, each pair yielding yes/no, short-answer, and sentence-level questions. Representative audio-language models are benchmarked with both automatic metrics and LLM-as-a-Judge evaluation.
tasks: comparative music question answering across track pairs

entries.name: LAT-Bench
entries.full_title: Listening with Time: Precise Temporal Awareness for Long-Form Audio Understanding
entries.summary: A human-verified benchmark for long-form temporal awareness in large audio language models, supporting audio up to 30 minutes and covering Dense Audio Caption, Temporal Audio Grounding and Targeted Audio Caption. It is released with LAT-Chronicle, a 1.2k-hour long-form audio dataset with temporal annotations across real-world scenarios, and with LAT-Audio, a model that treats temporal awareness as global-to-local reasoning with a Think-With-Audio chain-of-thought that calls tools on local audio.
entries.size: audio up to 30 minutes, 3 tasks; LAT-Chronicle training set of 1.2k hours
entries.note: temporal alignment in LALMs degrades as audio duration grows, which this benchmark isolates

entries.name: MCBench
entries.full_title: MCBench: A Multicontext Safety Assessment Benchmark for Omni Large Language Models
entries.summary: A safety benchmark for omni large language models that process vision, audio and text jointly, containing 1,196 scenarios across four safety categories where correct safety judgement requires integrating more than one modality. Each unsafe scenario is paired with a minimally different safe counterpart to measure model sensitivity rather than blanket refusal.
entries.note: models extract modality-specific cues but fail to integrate them, struggling most with subtle or non-physical risks

entries.name: OmniGUI
entries.full_title: OmniGUI: Benchmarking GUI Agents in Omni-Modal Smartphone Environments
entries.summary: OmniGUI is a step-level benchmark for evaluating GUI agents in omni-modal smartphone environments, providing continuous interleaved inputs of static images, synchronous audio, and video clips at every action step. It contains 709 expert-demonstrated episodes (2,579 action steps) across 29 applications, annotated with objective multimodal dependency levels. Foundational omni-modal models serve as agent proxies, and evaluation shows action-prediction performance degrades significantly in environments requiring synchronous temporal and auditory signals.
tasks: step-level GUI action prediction with audio/video context

entries.name: ProVoice-Bench
entries.full_title: From Reactive to Proactive: Assessing the Proactivity of Voice Agents via ProVoice-Bench
entries.summary: An evaluation framework for proactive voice agents, i.e. agents that intervene or monitor rather than only answering when addressed. It defines four tasks and uses a multi-stage data synthesis pipeline to curate 1,182 samples, and is used to evaluate state-of-the-art multimodal LLMs.
entries.note: current multimodal LLMs show a large gap on proactivity, especially over-triggering and reasoning

entries.name: RoleJudge
entries.full_title: Character Beyond Speech: Leveraging Role-Playing Evaluation in Audio Large Language Models via Reinforcement Learning
entries.summary: An evaluation framework that uses audio large language models to judge how well a speech role-playing agent's output aligns with an intended character, across modalities and dimensions including paralinguistic vocal features rather than text alone. It is paired with RoleChat, a voice role-playing evaluation dataset with chain-of-thought reasoning annotations built from authentic and LLM-generated speech, and the judge is trained in multiple stages with reinforcement learning using Standard Alignment to reduce reward misalignment.
entries.note: targets character attributes carried by voice, which text-only role-play evaluation misses

entries.name: SpeechParaling-Bench
entries.full_title: SpeechParaling-Bench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Paralinguistic-Aware Speech Generation
entries.summary: A benchmark for paralinguistic-aware speech generation by large audio-language models, expanding coverage from fewer than 50 to over 100 fine-grained paralinguistic features and supported by more than 1,000 English-Chinese parallel speech queries. It is organized into three progressively harder tasks - fine-grained control, intra-utterance variation and context-aware adaptation - and scores candidate responses by pairwise comparison against a fixed baseline with an LALM judge, framing evaluation as relative preference rather than absolute scoring.
metrics: pairwise preference (LALM judge vs fixed baseline)
entries.size: over 100 fine-grained features; more than 1,000 English-Chinese parallel speech queries
entries.note: Even leading proprietary models struggle with comprehensive static control and dynamic modulation, and misinterpreting paralinguistic cues accounts for 43.3% of errors in situational dialogue.

entries.name: Text Prior / Audio Reliance diagnostic (All That Glitters Is Not Audio)
entries.full_title: All That Glitters Is Not Audio: Rethinking Text Priors and Audio Reliance in Audio-Language Evaluation
entries.summary: A diagnostic framework for audio-language evaluation built on two axes: text prior, measuring answerability from text and general knowledge alone, and audio reliance, measuring actual dependency on the acoustic signal. It is applied to eight LALMs across three existing benchmarks and concludes with practical guidelines for benchmark design.
metrics: fraction of items requiring the full clip
entries.io: audio in, text out (with audio-ablated controls)
entries.note: Models retain 60-72% of their full-audio scores with no audio input at all, and among items that do require audio only 3.0-4.2% need the complete clip - the rest are solvable from localized fragments.

entries.name: TPI-Bench
entries.full_title: Still Between Us? Evaluating and Improving Voice Assistant Robustness to Third-Party Interruptions
entries.summary: An evaluation framework for measuring how Spoken Language Models handle Third-Party Interruptions, rigorously testing interruption-handling strategy and speaker discrimination in deceptive contexts. It is released alongside TPI-Train, an 88K-instance dataset with speaker-aware hard negatives that mitigates semantic shortcut learning where models exploit semantic context while neglecting acoustic speaker-change cues.
entries.size: TPI-Train has 88K instances; TPI-Bench size not stated in abstract

entries.name: VIBE
entries.full_title: VIBE: Voice-Induced open-ended Bias Evaluation for Large Audio-Language Models via Real-World Speech
entries.summary: A framework for evaluating generative bias in large audio-language models through open-ended tasks such as personalized recommendation, using human-recorded rather than synthetic speech. Avoiding multiple-choice formats lets stereotypical associations manifest organically without predefined options, and the design is extensible to new tasks.
entries.note: Across 12 state-of-the-art LALMs, both gender and accent cues trigger statistically significant distributional shifts, with bias magnitude strongly task-dependent.

entries.name: VoxSafeBench
entries.full_title: VoxSafeBench: Not Just What Is Said, but Who, How, and Where
entries.summary: A two-tier benchmark jointly evaluating social alignment of speech language models across safety, fairness and privacy. Tier 1 tests content-centric risks with matched text and audio inputs; Tier 2 targets audio-conditioned risks where the transcript is benign but the appropriate response hinges on who is speaking, paralinguistic cues or the surrounding environment, validated with intermediate perception probes confirming that frontier SLMs can detect those cues. It spans 22 tasks with bilingual coverage.
languages: bilingual (languages not specified in the abstract)
entries.io: speech in, text out (with matched text controls)
entries.note: Documents a pervasive 'speech grounding gap': models recognize the relevant social norm in text yet fail to apply it when the decisive cue must be grounded in speech.

entries.name: Afrispeech Semantics
entries.full_title: Afrispeech Semantics: Evaluating Audio Semantic Reasoning in Spoken Language Models Across Domains and Accents
entries.summary: An evaluation of audio language models on five semantic and paralinguistic reasoning tasks over accented speech: entailment, consistency, plausibility, accent drift and accent restraint. The tasks treat the audio as the primary evidence source, asking whether a textual hypothesis is entailed, contradicted or left undetermined by what was said, whether claims are plausible given the discourse, and whether predictions stay stable or appropriately constrained under accent variation and domain shift.
entries.note: targets semantic over-inference, i.e. models asserting more than the audio supports, and the effect of accent variation on it

entries.name: CBT-Audio
entries.full_title: CBT-Audio: Evaluating Audio Language Models for Patient-Side Distress Intensity Estimation in CBT Session Recordings
entries.summary: A dataset for evaluating patient-side distress intensity estimation from spoken cognitive behavioural therapy sessions with audio language models. It contains 1,802 patient turns from 96 publicly available CBT recordings, with turn-level distress labels validated on an expert-annotated subset, and evaluates 10 open-source audio language models under three input conditions: patient audio only, transcript only, or both.
tasks: patient distress intensity estimation from speech
audio vs transcript vs audio+transcript ablation
entries.size: 1,802 patient turns from 96 CBT session recordings

entries.name: ChildVox
entries.full_title: ChildVox: A Speech, Audio, and Large Audio-Language Model Benchmark in Understanding and Characterizing Sound across Childhood
entries.summary: A benchmark characterising the acoustic signals through which children communicate across the developmental trajectory from birth to school age, covering physiological sounds, non-linguistic vocalizations, canonical syllables and spoken language. It integrates more than 20 sub-tasks over 17 child-centred audio and speech datasets to allow cross-corpus and cross-domain comparison, and evaluates self-supervised, ASR-oriented and large audio-language models on tasks including physiological sound classification, vocalization and canonical syllable modelling, and speech quality assessment and recognition.
entries.note: supports downstream uses such as characterising children's language level and tracking speech production with age

entries.name: EnvMem
entries.full_title: Why Can't They Remember? Uncovering Representation and Retrieval Bottlenecks in Multi-Turn Acoustic Memory
entries.summary: EnvMem is a controlled multi-turn benchmark built to study why large audio language models fail to retain non-speech (environmental acoustic) information across turns, isolating failures at the representation (latent embedding) and retrieval (attention allocation) levels. Post-hoc interventions probe representational structure and attention dynamics, identifying representational trajectory drift as the key failure mode while attention allocation plays a limited role.

entries.name: EVA-Bench
entries.full_title: EVA-Bench: A New End-to-end Framework for Evaluating Voice Agents
entries.summary: An end-to-end evaluation framework for voice agents that both simulates and scores conversations: it orchestrates bot-to-bot audio dialogues over dynamic multi-turn scenarios with automatic simulation validation that detects user-simulator error and regenerates conversations before scoring. Scoring uses two composite metrics, EVA-A for task completion, faithfulness and audio-level speech fidelity, and EVA-X for conversation progression, spoken conciseness and turn-taking timing, both applicable across agent architectures. It includes 213 scenarios in three enterprise domains, a controlled accent and noise perturbation suite, and pass@1 / pass@k / pass^k measurement.
entries.size: 213 scenarios across three enterprise domains; 12 systems evaluated
entries.note: no system exceeds 0.5 on both EVA-A and EVA-X pass@1, and peak versus reliable performance diverge by a median 0.44 pass@k-pass^k gap

entries.name: FMSU-Bench
entries.full_title: Towards Fine-Grained Multi-Dimensional Speech Understanding: Data Pipeline, Benchmark, and Model
entries.summary: A benchmark covering 14 speech attribute dimensions, built to test whether speech LLMs can disentangle micro-acoustic cues, acoustic scenes and paralinguistic signals rather than only transcribe. It is released alongside a data curation pipeline that extracts spontaneous expressive speech from audiovisual sources while handling complex acoustic environments and long-audio timestamp alignment, and alongside FM-Speech, a model using decoupled attribute modelling and progressive curriculum fine-tuning.
entries.note: current speech LLMs remain weak at fine-grained multi-dimensional perception on this benchmark

entries.name: Instruct-FD
entries.full_title: Instruct-FD: Can Your Full-Duplex Speech System Follow Turn-Taking Instructions?
entries.summary: An instruction-conditioned benchmark for controllable turn management in full-duplex spoken dialogue systems: given an explicit conversational policy (e.g. proactive tutoring vs passive counseling), does the system adapt its turn-taking behavior accordingly? Conversations come from a human-validated synthetic generation pipeline, and scoring uses a deployment-agnostic multi-turn protocol with an LLM judge.
entries.note: Across six state-of-the-art full-duplex systems the best model reaches only 64.4% adherence, with proactive behaviors (model backchanneling, interruption) the weakest.

entries.name: KVoiceBench / KOpenAudioBench / KMMAU
entries.full_title: KVoiceBench, KOpenAudioBench, and KMMAU: Agent-Driven Korean Speech Benchmarks for Evaluating SpeechLMs
entries.summary: Three Korean SpeechLM benchmarks totalling 12,345 samples, produced by two human-agent construction frameworks: one transfers source-language SpokenQA benchmarks into the target language while preserving language-specific instructions, answer constraints and spoken forms, and the other converts target-language ASR corpora into audio understanding benchmarks using transcripts and speaker metadata. KVoiceBench and KOpenAudioBench cover Korean SpokenQA and KMMAU covers Korean audio understanding; eight recent SpeechLMs are evaluated.
entries.note: English-Korean gaps vary widely by model and SpokenQA vs audio-understanding rankings diverge, exposing weaknesses invisible to English-only evaluation

entries.name: MedMosaic
entries.full_title: MedMosaic: A Challenging Large Scale Benchmark of Diverse Medical Audio
entries.summary: MedMosaic is a large-scale medical audio question-answering dataset built to benchmark language and audio reasoning models under realistic clinical constraints. It spans condition-related physiological sounds, synthetic voices mimicking speech artifacts, and real short and long clinical conversations, with 46,701 QA pairs across multiple-choice, sequential multi-turn, and open-ended formats to probe multi-hop reasoning and answer generation. Benchmarking 13 audio and multimodal reasoning models shows reasoning remains challenging, with Gemini-2.5-pro reaching only 68.1%.

entries.name: MSEB
entries.full_title: Benchmarking LLMs on the Massive Sound Embedding Benchmark (MSEB)
entries.summary: An empirical evaluation of audio-native large language models from the Gemini and GPT families across the eight core capabilities of the Massive Sound Embedding Benchmark (MSEB), which was originally used for specialized audio encoders. The study assesses whether a single multimodal backbone can replace task-specific pipelines and measures audio-text parity against cascaded architectures.
entries.note: Reports a persisting modality gap in performance and robustness, and finds the evidence for an optimal architecture (audio-native vs cascaded) inconclusive.

entries.name: MTAVG-Bench 2.0
entries.full_title: MTAVG-Bench 2.0: Diagnosing Failure Modes of Cinematic Expressiveness in Multi-Talker Audio-Video Generation
entries.summary: A benchmark for diagnosing failure modes of cinematic expressiveness in multi-talker audio-video generation, targeting short-drama and scene-level content with a high-level failure taxonomy spanning acting, narrative, atmosphere, and audio-visual language. It provides over 10,000 QA evaluation instances plus subsets for short-drama-level assessment and temporal localization of failures, to test whether omni large language models can diagnose high-level audio-visual failures.

entries.name: MUSA
entries.full_title: Can Large Audio Language Models Ignore Multilingual Distractors? An Evaluation of Their Selective Auditory Attention Capabilities
entries.summary: A cocktail-party-inspired multilingual benchmark for source-grounded spoken-language understanding and reasoning in large audio language models. Each item pairs an English target dialogue with a semantically plausible distractor in English, Spanish, Korean or Chinese, and models are evaluated in single-source, source-separation-based two-stage, and end-to-end cocktail-party settings under controlled SNRs.
entries.note: strong single-source performance does not imply robust selective attention; errors are dominated by distractor-grounded source confusion, and separation leaves source attribution unresolved

entries.name: MusTBENCH
entries.full_title: MusTBENCH: Benchmarking and Advancing Temporal Grounding in Music LLMs
entries.summary: A music-expert-validated benchmark that evaluates whether Large Audio-Language Models ground their answers in the correct temporal regions of the audio, via five temporally grounded question-answering tasks. Experiments show existing LALMs struggle with precise temporal grounding; the paper additionally proposes MusT, a four-stage temporal optimization recipe.

entries.name: Omni-DeepSearch
entries.full_title: Omni-DeepSearch: A Benchmark for Audio-Driven Omni-Modal Deep Search
entries.summary: A benchmark for audio-driven omni-modal deep search: given one or more audio clips and a related question, a model must infer clues from the audio, invoke text, image and video search tools, and perform multi-hop reasoning to produce a short verifiable answer. It contains 640 samples across 15 fine-grained categories spanning four retrieval target modalities and four audio content types, filtered in multiple stages to guarantee audio dependence, retrieval necessity, visual-modality necessity and answer uniqueness.
entries.note: the strongest evaluated model, Gemini-3-Pro, reaches only 43.44% average accuracy

entries.name: Omni-Persona
entries.full_title: Omni-Persona: Systematic Benchmarking and Improving Omnimodal Personalization
entries.summary: The first comprehensive benchmark for omnimodal personalization, formalizing the task as cross-modal routing over a Persona Modality Graph with 4 task groups and 18 fine-grained tasks across roughly 750 items spanning text, image and audio. It proposes Calibrated Accuracy, which jointly evaluates correct grounding and appropriate abstention on absent-persona queries, and finds a consistent audio-vs-visual grounding gap in open-weight models.

entries.name: OmniInteract
entries.full_title: OmniInteract: Benchmarking Real-World Streaming Interaction for Real-Time Omnimodal Assistants
entries.summary: A streaming benchmark for real-time omnimodal LLMs evaluated through native online inference over audio-visual streams, where user queries and ambient sounds are embedded in the audio track so models must detect multimodal triggers, decide when to respond, and answer as the stream unfolds. It contains 250 videos with 1,430 temporally grounded response slots and scores correctness, timing, invalid outputs, interruption handling and context continuity; the best model reaches only 0.368 IA-QTF1.

entries.name: OmniPro
entries.full_title: OmniPro: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Omni-Proactive Streaming Video Understanding
entries.summary: OmniPro is a benchmark for omni-proactive streaming video understanding, i.e. autonomously deciding when to speak and what to say from continuous audio-visual streams. It comprises 2,700 human-verified samples across 9 sub-tasks and 3 cognitive levels covering 6 video-understanding capabilities, with 84% of samples requiring audio signals (speech or non-speech) and modality-isolation labels for fine-grained analysis. A dual-mode protocol evaluates content understanding (Probe mode) and full proactive responding (Online mode).

entries.name: PitchBench
entries.full_title: PitchBench: Measuring Pitch Hearing in Audio-Language Models
entries.summary: An evaluation suite measuring pitch hearing in audio-language models directly rather than through higher-level multiple-choice music tasks. It comprises 28 experiments covering absolute and relative pitch perception within sequences and chords while varying loudness, note duration, sound source, time stretching and background noise, with tasks ranging from identifying isolated pitches to tracking a melodic line inside a four-part texture. It is released as a Python package with the evaluation data and data generation tools.
entries.note: frontier ALMs lack stable pitch perception even on controlled synthetic and instrumental stimuli, with accuracy swinging by sound source, note duration and notation format

entries.name: PolySpeech-100
entries.full_title: PolySpeech-100: A Large-Scale Benchmark for Speech Understanding Across 100+ Languages and Dialects
entries.summary: A large-scale speech understanding benchmark covering 110 linguistic variants, built with a hybrid pipeline that augments gold-standard human recordings with instruction-driven synthetic speech so that 19 Chinese dialects and over 80 low-resource languages are represented. It targets semantic comprehension rather than transcription and is used to evaluate 22 end-to-end Speech-LLMs against cascaded ASR+LLM systems.
languages: multilingual (110 linguistic variants, incl. 19 Chinese dialects and 80+ low-resource languages)
entries.note: open-source end-to-end models beat cascades on heavy dialects, open models collapse on low-resource languages, and chain-of-thought prompting often hurts speech understanding

entries.name: SURE
entries.full_title: A Unified and Reproducible Experimentation Framework for Speech Understanding
entries.summary: A unified experimentation framework for speech understanding that standardizes prediction formats, normalization and scoring so that conventional pipelines and Speech LLMs can be compared fairly. It evaluates systems on representative tasks under realistic acoustic and linguistic stressors, and adds an agent-assisted flow that converts papers and code into versioned, runnable training pipelines on matched open-data subsets.
entries.note: Targets the fact that mismatched post-processing makes reported speech-understanding numbers non-comparable across papers.

entries.name: SVHalluc
entries.full_title: SVHalluc: Benchmarking Speech-Vision Hallucination in Audio-Visual Large Language Models
entries.summary: A benchmark for speech-vision hallucination in audio-visual LLMs. Unlike prior benchmarks that use environmental sounds as event indicators, SVHalluc tests whether models align rich human speech content with the corresponding visual signal, probing two complementary axes: semantic alignment and temporal alignment.
entries.note: State-of-the-art open-source audio-visual LLMs score near chance on multiple tasks while Gemini 2.5 Pro is far stronger; failures are attributed to cross-modal integration rather than single-modality perception.

entries.name: Text-to-voice tool-calling evaluation framework (audio Confetti and When2Call)
entries.full_title: From Text to Voice: A Reproducible and Verifiable Framework for Evaluating Tool Calling LLM Agents
entries.summary: A dataset-agnostic framework that converts verified text tool-calling benchmarks into controlled audio-based evaluations using text-to-speech, speaker variation, and environmental noise, preserving the original tool schemas and gold labels. Seven omni-modal models are evaluated on audio versions of Confetti and When2Call, together with an ambiguity-based stress test and a reference-free LLM-as-judge analysis of failure cases.

entries.name: The Unwritten Benchmark
entries.full_title: The Unwritten Benchmark: A New Challenge for Multimodal Machine Learning in Abstract Perceptual Reasoning
entries.summary: A benchmark probing abstract perceptual reasoning via acousto-kinematic word inference: models must decipher words across 3 writing styles from the audio of pen scratches plus video of hand movements, with no visible ink trace. Humans exceed 80% ordered letter accuracy while GPT-4o and Gemini 2.5-Pro fail to surpass 10%, and providing both modalities often degrades performance (a paradoxical fusion effect).
tasks: acousto-kinematic word inference from pen-scratch audio and hand-movement video
entries.size: 3 writing styles; item count not stated in abstract

entries.name: TraceAV-Bench
entries.full_title: TraceAV-Bench: Benchmarking Multi-Hop Trajectory Reasoning over Long Audio-Visual Videos
entries.summary: The first benchmark to jointly evaluate multi-hop reasoning over long audio-visual trajectories and multimodal hallucination robustness, with 2,200 validated multiple-choice questions over 578 long videos totaling 339.5 hours across 4 dimensions and 15 sub-tasks. Each question is grounded in an explicit reasoning chain averaging 3.68 hops over a 15.1-minute span, with evidence deliberately split across the visual and auditory streams.

entries.name: VideoFDB
entries.full_title: VideoFDB: Evaluating Full-Duplex Vision-Speech Capabilities in Conversational Agents
entries.summary: The first benchmark for full-duplex audio-visual-to-audio-visual (AV2AV) conversational agents, extending full-duplex evaluation beyond speech to nonverbal cues such as nods, smiles and gestures. It contributes dyadic clips from real-world video calls, a taxonomy separating perception from generation behaviors, and a rubric-based LM-as-judge framework with interpretable axes.
entries.size: 237 dyadic clips spanning 11 nonverbal conversational dynamics
entries.note: Finds systematic failure modes — captioning collapse and visual-stream ignorance — and shows cascaded speech-to-avatar systems architecturally cannot produce full-duplex nonverbal cues.

entries.name: VoiceGiraffe
entries.full_title: VoiceGiraffe: A Benchmark for Extreme Long-Context Audio-Language Understanding
entries.summary: A benchmark for hour-level long-context audio-language understanding using real-world material such as podcasts and lengthy speeches rather than short clips or artificially concatenated segments. It comprises 1,500 curated triplets organised in a dual-level taxonomy of single-hop perception and multi-hop reasoning, spanning diverse scenarios, modalities and languages, and compares open and proprietary LALMs against human performance under end-to-end, cascaded caption-aggregation and reasoning-enhanced cascading inference.
entries.note: long-range memory persistence is the bottleneck: LALMs do better on salient causal cues than on sparse events tracked across long audio, the opposite of the human pattern

entries.name: VoxParadox
entries.full_title: Do Audio LLMs Listen or Read? Analyzing and Mitigating Paralinguistic Failures with VoxParadox
entries.summary: An adversarial benchmark of 2,000 verified examples across 10 paralinguistic tasks, created with controlled speech synthesis so that the transcript's claim deliberately mismatches the actual speaking style. This separates listening from reading and directly measures whether an audio LLM uses acoustic evidence or falls back on language-implied answers. The paper also probes layer-wise where paralinguistic cues degrade and proposes Prompt-Conditioned Layer Mixer plus DPO as mitigations.
tasks: paralinguistic attribute identification under conflicting transcript
entries.note: audio LLMs score low on acoustic ground truth and follow the language-implied wrong answer; the proposed fix lifts Audio Flamingo 3 from 17.40% to 65.20%

entries.name: (unnamed) evaluation framework for addressee detection, turn-change prediction and next-speaker prediction in meetings
entries.full_title: Evaluating Large Language Models Abilities for Addressee, Turn-change, and Next Speaker Prediction in Meetings
entries.summary: An evaluation framework covering three multi-party conversational tasks — addressee detection, turn-change prediction and next speaker prediction — comparing supervised models, text-based LLMs, multimodal LLMs and human subjects on the AMI corpus. LLMs beat supervised models and humans at next speaker prediction without audio or visual input, while the multimodal LLM beat text LLMs on addressee detection and turn-change prediction but stayed below humans, indicating difficulty exploiting raw audio-visual signals.

entries.name: AnyAudio-Judge Bench
entries.full_title: AnyAudio-Judge: A Dynamic Rubric-Based Benchmark and Evaluator for Audio Instruction Following
entries.summary: A bilingual benchmark plus evaluation paradigm for audio instruction-following alignment. Instead of holistic LLM scoring, complex audio captions are adaptively decomposed into a variable number of independent, verifiable binary rubric items, and the benchmark spans four audio domains (speech, sound, music, mixed) with deliberately constructed hard negatives. The paper additionally trains an evaluator model (AnyAudio-Judge) with SFT plus GRPO on a Chain-of-Thought rationale corpus.
languages: bilingual (languages not specified in the abstract)
entries.io: audio + instruction/caption in, text rubric verdict out
entries.size: 7,920 curated samples across four audio domains
entries.note: Rubric-based judging improves zero-shot alignment detection over prior baselines and supplies interpretable reward signals for downstream RL on audio generation.

entries.name: AOR-Bench
entries.full_title: AOR-Bench: Do Large Audio Language Models Over-Refuse Pseudo-Harmful Queries?
entries.summary: The first over-refusal benchmark for large audio language models: it measures how often safety mechanisms wrongly reject benign queries whose speech only sounds harmful in isolation but is benign given surrounding acoustic context such as background sounds. Pseudo-harmful audio samples are organized into six scenario categories.
entries.size: 3,000 pseudo-harmful audio samples across six scenario categories
entries.note: Over-refusal is widespread across 12 LALMs from six model families; the paper also tries Chain-of-Thought and activation steering as lightweight mitigations.

entries.name: AudioProcessBench
entries.full_title: AudioProcessBench: Benchmark for Identifying Process Errors in Audio-Grounded Reasoning
entries.summary: A benchmark for step-level process-error identification in audio-grounded reasoning, extending process reward model evaluation from text and vision to audio. Reasoning traces produced by six audio and omni language models are segmented into discrete steps and annotated with binary step correctness plus fine-grained error types, and models are tested under three paradigms: step correctness identification, error-type-conditioned detection, and chain-level aggregation across multiple traces for the same question.
entries.io: audio + reasoning trace in, text verdict out
entries.note: Provides a testbed for audio reasoning verifiers and process reward models, asking whether process verification actually improves answer selection.

entries.name: AVI-Bench
entries.full_title: AVI-Bench: Toward Human-like Audio-Visual Intelligence of Omni-MLLMs
entries.summary: A cognitively inspired benchmark evaluating omni-multimodal LLMs across three stages — perception, understanding, and reasoning — through cross-modal tasks that require joint audio-visual interpretation. An extension, AVI-Bench-PriSe, probes primitive audio-visual sensation with unfamiliar, low-semantic stimuli to test generalization beyond common training distributions, and the paper presents a four-level audio-visual intelligence taxonomy.

entries.name: CASU
entries.full_title: From Sounds to Scenes: A Benchmark for Evaluating Context-Aware Auditory Scene Understanding in Large Audio Language Models
entries.summary: A benchmark for Context-Aware Auditory Scene Understanding: instead of evaluating speech, sound and music layers in isolation, it tests whether audio LLMs can integrate co-occurring layers (speech, acoustic events such as announcements, background environments such as traffic) into a holistic scene and reason about the logical relations between them. Audio is built by a scalable pipeline that composes real-world scene sounds with synthetic speech into time-accurate semi-synthetic streams.
entries.note: Shows that effective scene understanding requires integrating all auditory layers rather than relying on speech or sound alone.

entries.name: GlobeAudio
entries.full_title: GlobeAudio: A Multilingual Multicultural Benchmark for Naturalistic Evaluation of Large Audio-Language Models
entries.summary: A multilingual, multicultural benchmark for naturalistic audio understanding by large audio-language models. Questions are multiple-choice, written by native speakers and grounded in naturally occurring audio, so that answering requires higher-level auditory reasoning and culturally grounded interpretation rather than clean-studio perception. Closed- and open-source LALMs are compared against cascaded ASR-LLM pipelines.
entries.note: Substantial performance gaps appear under natural acoustic conditions, particularly for open-source models and low-resource languages.

entries.name: IHBench
entries.full_title: IHBench: Evaluating Post-Interruption Recovery in Voice Agents with Structured Workflows
entries.summary: A benchmark for post-interruption recovery in voice agents executing state-machine-driven workflows. Where prior work measures interruption timing (barge-in detection, endpointing, turn-taking), IHBench measures what happens afterwards: whether the agent resumes at the correct workflow step, addresses the user's interjection, and avoids re-delivering already-heard content. Six interruption types are injected at controlled points mid-utterance, each with a generated evaluation rubric, and each is scored on task fulfillment and recovery quality.
metrics: LLM judge validated against human annotators
entries.size: six interruption types across 10 enterprise domains; 27 audio-language model configurations evaluated
entries.note: Closed-weight models are consistently more interruption-robust than open-weight ones, degrading roughly 3.3x more slowly as conversations lengthen and showing no audio-versus-text modality gap; cross-benchmark analysis against AudioMultiChallenge suggests recovery quality is a largely distinct capability axis.

entries.name: IndicContextEval
entries.full_title: IndicContextEval: A Benchmark for Evaluating Context Utilisation in Audio Large Language Models Across 8 Indic Languages
entries.summary: A benchmark that tests whether AudioLLMs genuinely use textual context supplied in the prompt (domain descriptions, entity lists) or fall back on parametric knowledge learned in pretraining. It pairs natural multilingual speech with a seven-level prompting framework that progressively adds contextual signals — metadata, natural-language descriptions, entity lists in English and in native script, and adversarial prompts containing incorrect entities.
entries.io: speech + text context in, text out
entries.size: 56 hours of speech from 555 speakers across 23 professional domains
entries.note: Five models show substantial differences in context-utilisation behaviour, motivating explicit evaluation of contextual grounding in AudioLLMs.

entries.name: LALM temporal-understanding diagnostic benchmark (unnamed)
entries.full_title: A Closer Look at Failure Modes in Temporal Understanding of Large Audio-Language Models
entries.summary: A benchmark of 1,657 questions across three foundational tasks, built specifically for mechanistic analysis of why Large Audio Language Models fail at temporal reasoning. Behavioral analysis across input settings shows models under-utilize audio when textual cues are available, and the paper adds the first causal mechanistic analysis of these failures, with attention scaling at bottleneck layers raising accuracy from 55.9% to 59.1% without fine-tuning.

entries.name: MSU-Bench
entries.full_title: MSU-Bench: Towards Speaker-Centric Understanding in Conversational Multi-Speaker Scenarios
entries.summary: A diagnostic benchmark for speaker-centric understanding in realistic multi-speaker conversations, covering 16 speaker-centric tasks and 2,300 QA instances in a two-tier framework running from speaker grounding to dialogue reasoning. It was built with a Gemini-assisted annotation and QA-generation pipeline with human-in-the-loop verification, and includes analysis of speaker-referencing schemes and diagnostic error types.

entries.name: OmniCap-IF
entries.full_title: OmniCap-IF: Benchmarking and Improving Instruction Following Abilities for Omni-Video Captioning
entries.summary: The first benchmark designed to evaluate instruction-following in omni-modal captioning, assessing captions on format correctness and content correctness. It spans 50 distinct constraint types across pure visual, pure audio, and audio-visual modalities with temporal grounding, and evaluations on 1,920 samples reveal a format-content tradeoff where increased formatting complexity degrades omni-modal content accuracy.

entries.name: OmniHalluc-L
entries.full_title: OmniHalluc-L: Counterfactual Benchmarking and Modality-Perturbation Reliability Calibration for Long-Form Omni Hallucination
entries.summary: A counterfactual event-binding benchmark for hallucination in long-video omni assistants, constructing paired supported/counterfactual claims from the same audio-visual event evidence and scoring strict-pair accuracy. It contains 3,600 single-claim QA items from 638 long-form videos averaging 24.16 minutes (256.87 hours), on which Qwen2.5-Omni-7B reaches 32.06% and Qwen3-Omni-Instruct 41.55% versus 76.54% for a closed-source reference.

entries.name: ParaPairAudioBench
entries.full_title: ParaPairAudioBench: Paralinguistic Pairwise Audio Benchmark for LALM-as-a-Judge
entries.summary: A pairwise benchmark for LALM-as-a-Judge on fine-grained paralinguistic distinctions rather than holistic naturalness. Audio pairs span five dimensions — Style, Rate, Emphasis, Age and Gender — and include both same-transcript and cross-transcript conditions so that lexical reliance can be separated from acoustic reliance. Tie cases test whether judges can correctly abstain.
entries.io: audio pair in, text preference out
entries.size: 5,175 audio pairs across five paralinguistic dimensions
entries.note: Current LALM judges trail human judgments by about 32 percentage points on average and show severe calibration failures, especially on Tie cases.

entries.name: Prosodic Underuse Probe Ladder
entries.full_title: Represented but Ignored: A Causal Account of Prosodic Underuse in Audio-Language Models
entries.summary: A stage-specific probe ladder for localizing where audio-LLMs fail on prosody: whether acoustic information is lost in the audio path, misinterpreted internally, or represented but not used in the answer. Matched-content contrasts are combined with layerwise probing and targeted hidden-state interventions to test the causal status of the latent prosodic representation across four understanding-only audio-LLMs.
